# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file. The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

## [11.0.0](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/compare/v10.0.0...v11.0.0) (2026-11-14)

### Breaking changes

- **skf-analyze-source:** `AN[auto]` (forge-auto included) now analyzes one target, and a call that passes several `--project-path` entries, or `--target-ref` or `--target-refs`, now exits `2` (`input-missing`, `error.phase` `init:2b`) before any analysis. Before, it analyzed the first path alone and reported success, after fetching the others and dropping them, a documentation URL among them included, and it ignored the ref flags. ([#1211](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1211); issue [#1123](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1123))

  **Migration:** Run `AN[auto]` once for each path, or analyze several paths together without `[auto]`. Pin an `[auto]` run on a GitHub repository with `--pin <tag-or-branch>` in place of `--target-ref` or `--target-refs`; to read another repository or a local path at a ref, analyze it without `[auto]`, where `--target-ref` and `--target-refs` still work.

- **skf-analyze-source:** The step-by-step Analyze Source no longer stops at `error.phase` `identify-units:4` (`resolution-failure`, exit `3`) when `skf-detect-language.py` is missing. Unit identification now takes each unit's language and scope patterns from the `skf-disqualify-candidates.py units` call, which loads the language detector from beside itself, so a missing or broken `skf-detect-language.py` makes that call exit `1` and name the file on stderr instead. ([#1211](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1211), [#1228](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1228); issue [#1126](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1126))

  **Migration:** A pipeline that branched on `error.phase` `identify-units:4` no longer sees it: a missing `skf-detect-language.py` now surfaces as a failed `skf-disqualify-candidates.py units` call at unit identification whose stderr names the file. Reinstall SKF (`npx bmad-module-skill-forge install`) so every shared script is present.

- **skf-analyze-source:** Analyze Source given a repository browser page, such as a Codeberg `/src/branch/...` link, a self-hosted GitLab `/-/tree/...` link, a link to a file or folder inside a repository or a Bitbucket Data Center `/projects/<p>/repos/<r>` page, now stops with exit `3` (`resolution-failure`) and names the repository's `.git` clone URL when git reads the repository at a shorter part of the address that keeps at least `owner/repo` (given with `.git`) or, for Bitbucket Data Center, at its `/scm/<p>/<r>.git` address. A page whose repository git finds neither way, such as a SourceForge or Launchpad code page, a page of a repository one folder below the host or of one git reads only without `.git`, is still read as documentation. So is a page whose repository git does not reach within the 20 seconds the address and the shorter parts tried share, and so is a project wiki page (a `/wiki/` or `/wikis/` page after `owner/repo`, or a GitLab `/-/wikis/` page), which git is not asked about past its own address, so a wiki still makes a docs-only brief. Before, an `AN[auto]` run (forge-auto included) wrote a docs-only brief from the page and reported success. When git reads an `http://` address as a repository, the stop message now asks for its `.git` clone URL with `http://` or its SSH address, no longer for the address without `https://`, which SKF clones over https. ([#1211](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1211); issue [#1123](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1123))

  **Migration:** Rerun with the clone URL the message names.

- **skf-analyze-source, skf-audit-skill, skf-brief-skill, skf-campaign, skf-create-skill, skf-create-stack-skill, skf-drop-skill, skf-export-skill, skf-quick-skill, skf-refine-architecture, skf-rename-skill, skf-test-skill, skf-update-skill, skf-verify-stack:** `on_complete` stays a shell command in 13 workflows and an instruction in Setup Forge and Verify Stack. Each `customize.toml` comment and the docs now say that, unlike BMad core, where `on_complete` is an instruction, these workflows hand the value to the shell, so an instruction such as "run Test Skill" fails; Create Skill's failure line says so when the hook exits 127. Every command-style workflow runs the hook from your project root and quotes the path it passes, so a project path with a space stays one argument, and Quick Skill's hook gets a 60s timeout. Stack Skill's hook now receives `--result-path=<version folder>/create-stack-skill-result-latest.json` and is skipped, with a line that says so, when the run wrote no result file, so a Stack Skill hook that refuses arguments it does not know, such as a bare `curl` call, now fails. Verify Stack deletes its run folder before it carries out the instruction, shows a failure on one line and goes on, and runs the health check even when the instruction started another workflow. ([#1207](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1207); issue [#1109](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1109))

  **Migration:** If your Stack Skill `on_complete` command refuses arguments it does not know, call it from a script that ignores its arguments or reads `--result-path`.

- **skf-audit-skill:** Audit Skill now loads its config and the `headless_mode` preference through `skf-preflight.py` before its first question. A missing or malformed `_bmad/skf/config.yaml` stops the run with `helper-missing` (exit 3) where it used to go on, and a forger sidecar folder that is missing or not set in the config stops it with `forge-tier-missing` (exit 3), both at phase `on-activation:config` with the preflight's own message; a missing sidecar folder stopped at phase `init:forge-tier` before. A missing `uv` now stops it at phase `on-activation:config` where it named `on-activation:helpers`, still `helper-missing`. These stops come before Audit Skill reads `headless_mode` from `preferences.yaml`, so they print the `SKF_AUDIT_RESULT_JSON` line only under `--headless` or `-H`: a run made headless by `headless_mode: true` alone that lacks `uv` now shows the message alone, where it printed the line. The forge tier now comes from `skf-forge-tier-rw.py effective`, so a `forge-tier.yaml` that cannot be read, is cut short or names no valid tier now stops with `forge-tier-missing` where the run used to go on at a tier read by hand. The compile tier, the scope type, the docs-only and no-baseline checks and the two baseline doubts come from the new `skf-load-provenance.py baseline` command, and a `metadata.json` or provenance map it cannot read stops with `provenance-invalid` (exit 3) at phase `init:baseline`; an unreadable provenance map stopped at phase `init:provenance` before. ([#1210](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1210); issue [#1132](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1132))

  **Migration:** Reinstall SKF (`npx bmad-module-skill-forge install`) so the installed `skf-forge-tier-rw.py` and `skf-load-provenance.py` are the current ones: an older copy stops Audit Skill with `helper-missing` before it audits. If a run now stops naming `sidecar_path`, set `sidecar_path: _bmad/_memory/forger-sidecar` in `_bmad/skf/config.yaml`; if it stops on a damaged `forge-tier.yaml`, re-run Setup Forge to rewrite it. A pipeline that branches on `error.phase` looks for `on-activation:config` for a missing sidecar folder (was `init:forge-tier`) or a missing `uv` (was `on-activation:helpers`), and `init:baseline` for an unreadable provenance map (was `init:provenance`), and passes `--headless` (or `-H`) so a stop when Audit Skill starts still prints its line.

- **skf-audit-skill:** The drift report now shows each section heading once, in the order the run writes its sections, where before the template laid out empty Structural Drift, Semantic Drift, Severity Classification, Documentation Drift, Remediation Suggestions and Provenance headings that each stage then wrote again below them, and a compose-mode stack or a docs-only skill wrote them in another order. The report's frontmatter now records `scope_type`, `is_stack_skill`, `legacy_stack_provenance` and `compose_mode_stack` beside `docs_only_skill`, and each stage that picks a route reads them there, so a run whose session context was compacted still passes a public-api skill's `--scope-type public-api`, still diffs a stack library by library and still takes a compose-mode stack's route. The Audit Summary's doc drift line takes its counts from the comparison the run saved instead of from the session. The unused `lastStep` and `previousWorkflow` keys are gone from the frontmatter. ([#1210](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1210); issue [#1129](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1129))

  **Migration:** If `drift_report_template_path` names a copy of the template, add `scope_type: ''`, `is_stack_skill: ''`, `legacy_stack_provenance: ''` and `compose_mode_stack: ''` to its frontmatter after `docs_only_skill`, and delete every heading after the Audit Summary's table, with its comment, so the copy ends with the `| **Total** |` row. `lastStep` and `previousWorkflow` can go too.

- **skf-audit-skill, skf-test-skill, skf-verify-stack, skf-campaign:** A template setting that names a missing file now stops the run in its first step or sooner, naming the setting and the path, and in Test Skill and Verify Stack so does a copy that lacks what the steps fill in. Audit Skill stops before its first question with the new halt reason `template-missing` (exit `3`) when `drift_report_template_path` names no readable file. Its envelope names `error.phase` `on-activation:template` and the template path. Test Skill checks `test_report_template_path` before any stage runs and stops with `input-invalid` when the file is missing or lacks its title line or a section heading, which it used to meet only after scoring, or lacks the `<!-- Populated by` comment under a section heading, which it used to accept. Verify Stack stops in its first step (`error.phase` `init:report-template`) with `resolution-failure` (exit `3`) when `report_template_path` names no readable file, and with `schema-violation` (exit `5`) when the report it creates from the copy fails the feasibility-report check, which it used to meet only at its last step, or has no table under `## Evidence Sources`, which it used to accept. Campaign checks `report_template_path` and `kickoff_template_path` as it starts and stops with exit `2` (`invalid-input`) on one that names no readable file, before Setup or a resume (`campaign status` skips the check); a bad report template used to surface only at the end. Campaign's `customize.toml` now ships its real defaults, `{forge_data_folder}/_campaign` and the bundled `templates/` files, and says a bare path resolves from the skill folder. ([#1207](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1207); issue [#1110](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1110))

  **Migration:** If Audit Skill stops with `template-missing` at `error.phase` `on-activation:template`, point `drift_report_template_path` in `_bmad/custom/skf-audit-skill.toml` or `.user.toml` at a readable copy, or reinstall SKF when it names the bundled `assets/drift-report-template.md`. If your `test_report_template_path` copy lacks the `<!-- Populated by` comment under one of its six section headings, copy that comment from the bundled `templates/test-report-template.md` under the heading, or Test Skill stops before any stage runs. If your Verify Stack `report_template_path` copy has no table under `## Evidence Sources`, copy the table's header and separator lines from the bundled `assets/feasibility-report-template.md` under that heading, or Verify Stack stops in its first step.

- **skf-brief-skill, skf-test-skill:** Brief Skill and Test Skill now read the forge tier, the tool flags and the `tier_override` in `preferences.yaml` with `skf-forge-tier-rw.py` instead of reading the files by hand, so an override applies only when it names `Quick`, `Forge`, `Forge+` or `Deep`, capital letters included. Brief Skill now stops at its first step, with no result envelope, when that helper is missing. It takes its Quick fallback and warning for a `forge-tier.yaml` that holds no usable `tier`, a truncated one included, as it did for one that does not parse, and it names an ignored `tier_override` or a `preferences.yaml` it cannot read in the envelope's `warnings`. Test Skill now stops with `forge-tier-missing` on a `forge-tier.yaml` it cannot read a tier from, where it used to go on, and with `helper-missing` when the helper is missing, unless `--tier` is passed. `--tier` now wins over `tier_override`: a Test Skill run given `--tier` tests at that tier. ([#1205](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1205); issue [#1118](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1118))

  **Migration:** Reinstall SKF (`npx bmad-module-skill-forge install`) so the installed `skf-forge-tier-rw.py` is the current one: an older copy makes Brief Skill fall back to Quick and Test Skill stop with `helper-failed`. If a run now stops on, or falls back to Quick from, a damaged `forge-tier.yaml`, re-run Setup Forge to rewrite it, or pass `--tier` to Test Skill.

- **skf-campaign:** Campaign drops two customization settings that could not do what they offered. `quality_gate_hard` had one accepted value, `zero-critical-high`, so the hard gate is now fixed: a skill passes it only when its Test Skill run finds no Critical or High gap, and a campaign brief's `quality_gate` may still name only `zero-critical-high`. `brief_template_path` swapped the template Setup writes `campaign-brief.yaml` from, but no later stage reads anything a copy could add, so Setup now always writes the brief from the bundled template. Both settings are ignored when an override sets them. `campaign-state.py init` no longer needs `--hard`, which defaults to `zero-critical-high`. ([#1214](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1214); issue [#1142](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1142))

  **Migration:** Remove `quality_gate_hard` and `brief_template_path` from `_bmad/custom/skf-campaign.toml` and `_bmad/custom/skf-campaign.user.toml`. A copy of the brief template no longer applies, so you can delete it.

- **skf-create-stack-skill:** A compose-mode Stack Skill run now reads its own stage files where it picks the constituent skills, sets the scope, reads the constituents and finds their pairs, and a halt there names that file in the envelope's `phase`: `compose-skills:enumerate`, `compose-skills:stale-manifest` and `compose-skills:no-skills` (formerly `detect-manifests:`), `compose-extract:enumerate`, `compose-extract:cycle` and `compose-extract:constituent-gone` (formerly `parallel-extract:`), and `compose-pairs:comention` and `compose-pairs:vs-report` (formerly `detect-integrations:`). Each constituent's `SKILL.md` is read by its own subagent; one it cannot read records a `constituent-read-failed` warning, and that skill's pairs cite its export names in place of signatures. ([#1215](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1215); issue [#1151](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1151))

  **Migration:** A pipeline that branches on `error.phase` for a compose-mode Stack Skill run looks for the new values: `detect-manifests:enumerate` is now `compose-skills:enumerate`, `detect-manifests:stale-manifest` is `compose-skills:stale-manifest`, `detect-manifests:no-skills` is `compose-skills:no-skills`, `parallel-extract:enumerate` is `compose-extract:enumerate`, `parallel-extract:cycle` is `compose-extract:cycle`, `parallel-extract:constituent-gone` is `compose-extract:constituent-gone`, `detect-integrations:comention` is `compose-pairs:comention` and `detect-integrations:vs-report` is `compose-pairs:vs-report`. Each halt keeps its exit code, `halt_reason` and message.

- **skf-create-stack-skill:** Stack Skill now renders the fixed parts of its reference files, its Library Reference Index and its evidence report with `skf-render-stack-metadata.py`, instead of retyping them from the run's files. The new `references` subcommand (`--mode code` or `compose`, which must match the extraction bundle's mode) prints the index rows in library order, each in its SKILL.md and its `stack-catalog.md` link form, and with `--out` writes each library's `references/<library>.md` (its title, version, import or export count, tier, every key export with its signature and source line or constituent, and its Migration & Deprecation findings) and each pair's `references/integrations/<a>-<b>.md` (its type, co-import file count, Confidence label with its compose suffixes, and its key files or, in compose mode, its evidence, reference and VS lines), leaving one `<!-- skf:fill ... -->` marker line for each part the run writes itself: the usage patterns, common imports, integration pattern and usage convention. A library name with a `/`, such as `@scope/pkg` or a Go module path, puts its files in subfolders (`references/@scope/pkg.md`), and `skf-validate-output.py --skill-type stack` now counts and checks the files in those subfolders too, instead of reporting a `library_count` or `integration_count` mismatch and skipping their structure checks. The new `evidence-report` subcommand writes `evidence-report.md` atomically from the bundle, the run's warnings and decisions, and the provenance map, which it bins by `signature_source` with `skf-render-metadata-stats.py`; a sink line it cannot read is named in the report, and a missing stats helper or an unreadable map writes "not computed" with the reason. A bad input to either exits `2` with one line on stderr and writes nothing, and a missing `skf-render-stack-metadata.py` now stops the write step at the reference files (phase `generate-output:references`) instead of at `metadata.json` (phase `generate-output:metadata`). A house-style copy of the stack template still shapes the prose and any section it adds, but no longer the reference files' header lines, key exports or key files. ([#1215](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1215); issue [#1156](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1156))

  **Migration:** A pipeline that branches on `error.phase` looks for `generate-output:references` where a missing `skf-render-stack-metadata.py` at the write step named `generate-output:metadata`, still `helper-missing` (exit `3`); reinstall SKF (`npx bmad-module-skill-forge install`) to clear it.

- **skf-create-stack-skill:** A headless Stack Skill run whose scope review finds no library in scope (none reached two importing files, or `scope_overrides` excluded every one) now stops with exit `2` (`empty-scope`) before it records a scope decision; its message lists each library left out with its reason and asks you to pass `scope_overrides` with `<name>: include` for each library the stack should cover. An interactive run in that state offers no `[C]`: it shows the libraries left out and takes names to add, a custom list or `[X]`. The ownership check on the stack's folder now runs at the first step, right after the stack name is set, so a folder SKF did not generate stops the run with exit `5` (`not-skf-output` or `flat-layout`) and a folder that holds another kind of skill with exit `4` (`write-failure`) before any library is counted, and its envelope names `error.phase` `init:ownership` or `init:not-a-stack` where it named `generate-output:ownership` or `generate-output:not-a-stack`; the check on the version folder still runs before the stack is written, with phase `generate-output:ownership`. When `stack_name` names a stack SKF already published, the scope review marks each library `kept` or `new` against that version, lists each published library the new scope leaves out with its reason, and in code mode keeps by default every published library still imported by at least one file, unless `scope_overrides` excludes it. The headless scope decision now always carries `prior_kept`, the published libraries kept that way (`[]` on a new stack and in compose mode), and a published library's `dropped` reason starts with `in v<version>: `. ([#1215](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1215); issue [#1152](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1152))

  **Migration:** A headless run whose scope review leaves no library in scope now stops with `empty-scope` (exit `2`) and names each library it left out, where it used to go on with no library in scope: pass `scope_overrides` with `<name>: include` for each library the stack should cover, then re-run. A pipeline that branches on `error.phase` looks for `init:not-a-stack` where it looked for `generate-output:not-a-stack`, and for `init:ownership` where a refusal of the stack's folder (not SKF output, still in the flat layout, or a folder SKF could not check) named `generate-output:ownership`; a refusal of the version folder still names `generate-output:ownership`, and each halt keeps its exit code and `halt_reason`.

- **skf-drop-skill:** Drop Skill's result record (`drop-skill-result-<timestamp>.json` and `drop-skill-result-latest.json`) no longer carries `summary.headless_provenance`. The record's `headless_decisions`, which already held a headless run's mode and confirm decisions, is now the one place they are kept: its `select.mode` entry gives the drop mode (`taken_action`) and where it came from (`reason`: `--mode argument`, or `draft-skill-forced-purge` for a skill with no manifest entry), and its `select.confirm` entry the confirmation a headless run gave itself. An interactive run records neither entry, so its record no longer says whether the mode came from `--mode` or the prompt, or that a person confirmed the drop. ([#1216](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1216); issue [#1161](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1161))

  **Migration:** Read `headless_decisions` instead of `summary.headless_provenance`, finding each entry by its `gate` (a run given `keep` also records `select.active-guard`, before `select.mode`): `mode_source` is the `select.mode` entry's `reason`, `headless: true` is the presence of a `select.mode` entry, and `confirm: "headless-auto"` that of a `select.confirm` entry. `headless: false`, `mode_source: "interactive-prompt"` and `confirm: "user-explicit"`, which an interactive run carried, have no counterpart.

- **skf-drop-skill, skf-campaign:** Drop Skill and Campaign no longer load every `project-context.md` in your project by default: their bundled `persistent_facts` is now empty. No Drop Skill stage reads the project context, and Campaign inlined those files into every Tier A kickoff although Brief, Create and Test Skill already load them in their own runs, so each of those runs read them twice. The twelve other workflows that read the project context keep the default. ([#1207](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1207); issue [#1107](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1107))

  **Migration:** To keep loading those files in Drop Skill or Campaign, add the entry `"file:{project-root}/**/project-context.md"` to the `persistent_facts` list under the `[workflow]` line of `_bmad/custom/skf-drop-skill.toml` or `_bmad/custom/skf-campaign.toml`, or the line `persistent_facts = ["file:{project-root}/**/project-context.md"]` when that file has no such list: a second `persistent_facts` line in one table is a TOML error, and the run then ignores the whole file. An old `!file:{project-root}/**/project-context.md` entry that only dropped the default now drops nothing and can be removed.

- **skf-export-skill:** Export Skill's orphaned context file question no longer offers (c) rewrite, so the result's `deviations` no longer holds a `rewrite_orphan_context` entry. That option rewrote the orphaned file with `.agents/skills/` in every row's `root:` path, though `CLAUDE.md` and `.cursorrules` have skill folders of their own, and the next export asked about the file again, since no IDE in `config.yaml` targets it. ([#1209](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1209); issue [#1165](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1165))

  **Migration:** To keep such a file current, choose (b) keep, then add its IDE back to `ides` in `config.yaml` and run the export again. To refresh it once, run the export with `--context-file CLAUDE.md`, which writes that one file with the skill root the IDE mapping gives it; a later export without that option asks about the file again. A script that matched `rewrite_orphan_context` in the result's `deviations` can drop that match.

- **skf-export-skill:** Export Skill now checks each context snippet draft before it lists or publishes it. `skf-validate-output.py` gains `<draft-dir> --snippet-check --package <skill-package-dir>`, which reads the draft's `context-snippet.md` and reports, beside the line 1 and line 2 checks it already ran, a header that does not name the package's skill at its `metadata.json` version, a blank or bare `|` line inside the snippet (the managed section reads it as the end of the row), an SKF marker, and a `SKILL.md#slug` or `references/<file>.md#slug` anchor whose file or heading the package does not hold, the slug read as GitHub writes it. It prints JSON and exits `0` on PASS, `1` on FAIL and `2` when `--package` names no folder. Step 2 runs it on each draft, corrects the draft once when it fails, and stops the run with exit `4` (`context-rebuild-failed`) when it still fails. Step 3 also stops with exit `4` when `assemble` refuses the draft of a skill the run exports, where it used to print a skipped row and still record and copy that snippet. ([#1209](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1209); issue [#1166](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1166))

  **Migration:** If an export now stops with exit `4` (`context-rebuild-failed`) on a snippet draft, read the checks it names. When `snippet_format_path` names your own copy of `snippet-format.md`, keep its line 1 as `[{skill-name} v{version}]|root: ...` and give its quick-start and key-types lines only anchors whose headings the package holds, then run the export again. Otherwise re-run Update Skill or Create Skill on the skill, so its `metadata.json` gives a version and its `SKILL.md` holds the headings, and export it again.

- **skf-export-skill:** Export Skill's bundled `assets/snippet-format.md` now holds only the two snippet templates and the note on the lines scripts parse. Its Skill Root Path, Format Rules and Rules sections and the line bullets under the single-skill template are gone: step 2 (`references/generate-snippet.md`) states each of those rules, and the two copies had to change together. If `snippet_format_path` points Export Skill at your own copy, that copy now keeps the `|api:` label and the gotchas line's `; ` separator as they are, beside the lines it already kept, because Export Skill reads both lines of the prior snippet back to rank the api names and carry gotchas forward; the quick-start and key-types lines stay free to restyle, as long as each anchor they hold names a heading of the package. ([#1209](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1209); issue [#1164](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1164))

  **Migration:** If `snippet_format_path` names your own copy, put back the `|api:` label and the gotchas line's `; ` separator where the copy changed them, as the bundled file writes them. Delete the copy's Skill Root Path, Format Rules and Rules sections and the line bullets under its single-skill template too: Export Skill now states each of those rules itself, and a copy's own can only disagree with them.

- **skf-export-skill, skf-update-skill:** Export Skill and Update Skill now read a skill's prior `|gotchas:` and `|api:` lines, and write its new gotchas line, through the `gotchas` action of `skf-rebuild-managed-sections.py`, where the model used to split the line, track the `[CARRIED]` marker, fill the 3 slots and rewrite each `; ` by following prose. `gotchas prior` reads the prior snippet and whether an export recorded the skill, and `gotchas resolve` takes the run's judgments from a JSON file (which prior pitfalls a current source still states, and the new gotchas) and returns the line with the gotchas it left off, carried or dropped, so the same judgments give the same line on every run. Update Skill now marks a prior pitfall no current source states `[CARRIED]` only once an export has recorded the skill, as Export Skill does: before the skill's first export it keeps that pitfall unmarked. A prior snippet SKF cannot read, such as one saved in an encoding other than UTF-8, now stops the run: Export Skill exits `4` (`context-rebuild-failed`) and Update Skill halts with `halted-for-write-failure` (`error.phase` `write:context-snippet`). Update Skill halts there on an export manifest that does not parse too, which Export Skill already stops on in step 1, with exit `3`. ([#1209](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1209); issue [#1164](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1164))

  **Migration:** If Export Skill now stops with exit `4` (`context-rebuild-failed`), or Update Skill with `halted-for-write-failure` (`error.phase` `write:context-snippet`), on a skill's prior `context-snippet.md`, save that file as UTF-8 and run the workflow again. If Update Skill stops on the export manifest, fix or remove `.export-manifest.json` in your skills folder, as Export Skill's exit `3` already asks, then run it again.

- **skf-export-skill, skf-update-skill, skf-audit-skill, skf-test-skill:** When Export, Update, Audit or Test Skill found an SKF skill still in the old flat layout, the agent moved it into the versioned layout by hand, one command at a time, with nothing to undo a half-done move and no check afterwards, and it also rewrote `.export-manifest.json` itself, which only the manifest helper may change. The four workflows now move it with one `skf-skill-inventory.py migrate` call: it names the version folder from the skill's `metadata.json` (`1.0.0` when it has none), moves the package and points `active` at it, moves the old flat provenance map, evidence report, extraction rules, test and drift reports and gap ledgers into the version's forge folder, checks the result and reports what moved and what it left in place. It leaves the export manifest alone, and when a move or the `active` flip fails it puts everything back. Update Skill then reads the skill from the version folder the migration made, and its `--from-test-report` lookup finds the test report the migration moved into the version's forge folder. Where the hand steps carried on, the move now stops before anything moves: when a version folder, or the `<version>.skf-migrate` folder a cut-off migration left, is already there, when a package entry is a link, or when the `version` in `metadata.json` names no version or is not written as its folder name (`1.0` or `v1.2.3`, whose folders would be `1.0.0` and `1.2.3`, which the export manifest would never match). Update Skill then ends `blocked` with `error.phase` `init:migrate`, Export Skill exits `3` with `resolution-failure`, Audit Skill exits `3` with `skill-not-found`, and Test Skill stops with `helper-failed` at phase `init:resolve`, each with the reason. ([#1204](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1204); issue [#1121](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1121))

  **Migration:** Follow the reason the workflow gives, then re-run: delete or move out of the way the version folder already in `<skills folder>/<name>/`, or move what `<name>/<version>.skf-migrate/<name>/` holds back into `<name>/` and delete that folder; replace a linked package entry, such as `references`, with the folder or file it points to; or set `version` in `<name>/metadata.json` to a full version written as its folder name, such as `1.0.0`. The troubleshooting guide's "A flat skill cannot be moved into the versioned layout" entry covers each reason. Skills already in the versioned layout are not affected.

- **skf-forger:** The `compact_greeting` preference is gone. Only Ferris read it, from the `preferences.yaml` every SKF workflow loads, so a returning user now always gets the menu, and `skf-preflight.py` no longer prints `derived.compact_greeting`. A `compact_greeting` still set in `preferences.yaml` is ignored. ([#1212](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1212); issue [#1171](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1171))

  **Migration:** Delete the `compact_greeting` line from `_bmad/_memory/forger-sidecar/preferences.yaml`. Nothing replaces it.

- **skf-forger:** A pipeline chain now stops at Create Skill when it compiles a skill with no exports (its `partial` status, with `summary.warning` `zero-exports`), with the halt reason `zero-exports`, where it used to go on to Test Skill and Export Skill. The stop leaves the repair `fix-brief-scope`: fix the brief's `scope.include` or `target_version` so it reaches the package's public exports, then resume, and Create Skill runs again. A headless `resume` stops with `user-action-required` until you have done it. ([#1212](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1212); issue [#1168](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1168))

  **Migration:** When a chain stops with `zero-exports`, fix the brief's `scope.include` or `target_version` (or run Brief Skill again), then take Ferris's offer to resume the chain at Create Skill, or forge the package with `forge-quick <package>` instead.

- **skf-quick-skill:** Quick Skill now parses `_bmad/skf/config.yaml` and `preferences.yaml` with `skf-preflight.py`, the helper Setup Forge and Ferris use, instead of reading them by hand. A `config.yaml` that is missing or does not parse, or a `sidecar_path` that is missing or still holds a placeholder, stops Quick Skill with exit `3` (`resolution-failure`, phase `on-activation`) where it used to go on, and shows the helper's message, which names the file and the fix. Its `SKF_QUICK_SKILL_RESULT_JSON` line gives `Quick Skill cannot load its config.` as its message and the helper's code, such as `CONFIG_MISSING`, as `details.cause`. A `preferences.yaml` that does not parse is named in one line and the run goes on with the defaults, so only `--headless` or `-H` makes that run headless. ([#1205](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1205); issue [#1117](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1117))

  **Migration:** If Quick Skill now stops with exit `3` naming `sidecar_path`, set `sidecar_path: _bmad/_memory/forger-sidecar` in `_bmad/skf/config.yaml` and run it again.

- **skf-quick-skill:** Quick Skill now reports the version and the export count the installed `metadata.json` holds, in its completion summary and in the result envelope's `summary.version` and `summary.exports_documented`, and its context snippet names that version. When `skf-render-quick-metadata.py` goes missing after the run started, or fails twice, compiling stops with exit `3` (`resolution-failure`, `details.cause` `quick-metadata-renderer-missing` or `quick-metadata-renderer-error`) instead of writing `metadata.json` by hand. The compiled `SKILL.md` and `context-snippet.md` are kept in the run folder and installed from there, as `metadata.json` is. ([#1223](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1223); issue [#1174](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1174))

  **Migration:** If Quick Skill now stops with exit `3` and `details.cause` `quick-metadata-renderer-missing`, re-install SKF so that `skf-render-quick-metadata.py` is back in `_bmad/skf/shared/scripts/`, then run it again. With `quick-metadata-renderer-error`, the error line shown on screen names the file or field the renderer could not read: run Quick Skill again, and if it stops the same way, report that line.

- **skf-refine-architecture:** A VS Report Integration Raises cell in a team's refinement rules copy (`refinement_rules_path`) that bolds nothing now raises a severity tier, or no issue, only when the whole cell is that tier, No issue or None, ignoring case, extra spaces and one trailing period (`Major`, `major.`, `None`). A cell such as `No Critical issue`, `Not a Major issue` or `A Critical issue: the architecture needs a redesign` used to raise the tier it mentions, negated or not; it now stops Refine Architecture before any analysis with exit `3` (`resolution-failure`, phase `init:rules`) and a `vs-raises` violation. A cell that bolds a tier, No issue or None, as the bundled rules do, raises what it bolds as before. ([#1219](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1219); issue [#1176](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1176))

  **Migration:** In your `refinement_rules_path` copy, bold the tier or the No issue each VS Report Integration Raises cell raises (`A **Major** issue`), or leave only the tier, No issue or None in the cell.

- **skf-rename-skill:** Rename Skill now reads the old skill's `active` link through the inventory helper and rolls the rename back (exit `4`, `write-failed`, phase `execute:active-link`) when the link is broken or leads outside the skill's own folder. Before, it took the last part of the link's text as the version, so it pointed the renamed skill's link at a version folder of the same name in another skill, and repaired a broken link that still ended in a version the rename moved. A link SKF wrote can end up that way: on Windows without symlink rights the link is a junction to an absolute path, which moving the project folder breaks, and which a copy of the project that keeps the junction leaves pointing into the original project. A headless run whose skill roster helper cannot run now stops at phase `select:list-skills`, where a manifest read that could not run stopped at `select:read-manifest`. A run whose export manifest is not UTF-8, or is JSON but not a manifest, now stops with `manifest-corrupt` (exit `3`) in place of `write-failed` (exit `4`), and a missing `skf-skill-roster.py` stops the run at `select:start-run`. ([#1221](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1221); issue [#1180](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1180))

  **Migration:** When a rename stops at `execute:active-link`, point the old skill's `active` link at the version the export manifest has active (any of its version folders when the manifest does not list it), as the message says (`uv run _bmad/skf/shared/scripts/skf-atomic-write.py flip-link --link <skills_output_folder>/<old name>/active --target <version>`), or remove the link, then run the rename again.

- **skf-rename-skill:** Rename Skill now checks, before it copies anything, whether the rewrite would leave the old name where the final no-trace check refuses it, for example in a `metadata.json` `description` that names the library the skill is named after. On a match it stops with `verify-failed` (exit `5`, phase `select:predict-verify`), with nothing changed, and names each file of the old skill to edit, with the line number and text of that file as the rename would write it: a JSON file comes out indented, so find the line by its key. `--dry-run` runs the same check, so a dry run of such a skill now stops with exit `5` where it exited `0` and the real run then rolled back. A missing `skf-rewrite-skill-name.py` now stops the run at `select:start-run`. A file of the old skill the rewrite cannot read stops it at `select:predict-verify` (`write-failed`, exit `4`), before the copy, and so does a missing `skf-verify-no-trace.py`, which stopped it at `execute:resolve-helpers` before. ([#1221](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1221); issue [#1181](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1181))

  **Migration:** For each line the message names, edit or remove a note an earlier run wrote, or a `context-snippet.md` line such as `|gotchas:`, in the old skill's file, then re-run the rename. When the line names the library or repository the skill is named after, the skill cannot be renamed: create it again under the new name with Brief Skill and Create Skill.

- **skf-setup:** `headless_mode: true` in `preferences.yaml` no longer turns `/skf-setup` into an envelope-only run. As the docs say, the preference now only skips the question: Setup keeps orphaned QMD collections without asking, with a notice that names `headless_mode: true`, and still shows its FORGE STATUS banner and notices and runs the health check. `--headless`, `-H`, `--quiet` and a Ferris pipeline still print the `SKF_SETUP_RESULT_JSON` line alone. ([#1218](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1218); issue [#1183](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1183))

  **Migration:** A script that runs `/skf-setup` with only `headless_mode: true` set and reads its `SKF_SETUP_RESULT_JSON` line passes `--headless` or `--quiet`.

- **skf-setup:** Setup Forge now creates its run folder when it starts, before it runs the customization resolver, instead of in its first step. When the folder cannot be created, the blocked envelope of a `--headless` or `--quiet` run now names phase `on-activation:run-folder` where it named `step 1:run-folder`; its reason and path are unchanged. ([#1205](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1205); issue [#1119](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1119))

  **Migration:** A pipeline that branched on `error.phase` `step 1:run-folder` branches on `on-activation:run-folder` instead.

- **skf-setup, skf-quick-skill:** Setup Forge and Quick Skill now look for every helper their stage files declare, and for `skf-resolve-customization.py`, when they start, and stop there, before any source is fetched or any skill file is written, when any of them is missing, naming each one: Setup Forge at phase `on-activation:helper-missing`, Quick Skill with exit `3` (`resolution-failure`), `details.cause` `helpers-missing` and `details.missing` listing the missing files. This covers helpers a run used to go on without, or needed only on some runs. In Quick Skill they include the security scan (`skf-security-scan.py`), description guard (`skf-description-guard.py`), content hash (`skf-hash-content.py`), skill inventory (`skf-skill-inventory.py`), metadata renderer (`skf-render-quick-metadata.py`), the atomic writer (`skf-atomic-write.py`), without which the active-pointer flip used to be skipped, the frontmatter validator (`skf-validate-frontmatter.py`) on a run with skill-check installed, the language detector (`skf-detect-language.py`) on a run with a language hint, and, on a single-target run, `skf-quick-batch.py`; in Setup Forge they are the ccc exclusion merger (`skf-merge-ccc-exclusions.py`) and the qmd classifier (`skf-qmd-classify-collections.py`) on any tier, and the envelope emitter (`skf-emit-result-envelope.py`) that renders the banner. A missing `skf-resolve-customization.py` used to print the `customization_resolver_unavailable` warning and go on with the bundled defaults; it now stops the run. A `--batch` run with `skf-quick-batch.py` missing exits `3` where it exited `2`. ([#1205](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1205); issue [#1117](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1117))

  **Migration:** Reinstall SKF (`npx bmad-module-skill-forge install`) so every helper resolves. A pipeline that branched on a step's `step <N>:helper-missing` phase, on a per-helper Quick Skill cause such as `github-fetch-missing`, or on exit `2` for a missing batch helper branches on `on-activation:helper-missing`, `helpers-missing` and exit `3` instead.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's signature rules now say that a const annotated with an interface or object type literal that writes call signatures, such as storybook's `export const actions: ActionsFunction = (...args: any[]) => ...`, declares each call signature that type has, as a const annotated with a function type declares that type's parameters, and that several of them are one overload set whose implementation is the const's value. A const the source declares as a component, such as `export const Badge: React.FC<BadgeProps> = ...`, whose `React.FC` type writes a call signature too, is still compared by its props alone, its return type and wrapper never. A form that matches any of them, such as `actions` documented as `(handlerMap: Record<T, string>, options?: ActionOptions) => ActionsMap<T>`, the first of `ActionsFunction`'s call signatures, is therefore no mismatch; before, a judge that compared it with the arrow's own `(...args: any[])` could raise a Critical `signature-mismatch` gap on that form and fail the hard gate, while another judge passed the same skill. For such a const whose type has one call signature, a form that matches only the arrow's own list is now compared with that signature, and one that differs from it in more than its parameter names, such as one that leaves out a parameter the signature requires, can be a Critical gap, so a skill some runs passed can now stop at the hard gate. Create Skill records such a const's parameters from the arrow's own list, so a skill it generates can write that form. Several call signatures also make such a const an overload set when Test Skill looks for the source to settle a `split-body-mismatch` gap over it, so its declaration no longer settles one: the gap's Source stays the reference file that sorts last, and its remediation says no source settled it. ([#1098](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1098); issue [#1085](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1085))

  **Migration:** If a skill now stops at the hard gate on a `signature-mismatch` gap over a const annotated with an interface or object type literal that writes call signatures, write the form as one of those call signatures takes it, as the gap's `source_sig` gives it, then run Test Skill again. Create Skill writes the arrow's own list there each time it generates the skill, so make that edit again after it does.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's signature rules now say that a list that marks a member `?` and writes no type, such as storybook's `Story` documented as `{ of?, meta?, inline?, height?, autoplay? }`, claims its list is complete, as a list that writes a type or a default does; `score-signatures.py` already reads a parameter list that marks a member `?`, such as `(of?, meta?)`, this way. A component's props list that gives a prop a default and writes no type, such as `({ of, meta = {} })`, likewise claims its props list is complete. An optional parameter or optional own prop such a form leaves out is therefore an `omitted-optional` mismatch; before, the rules put that list in neither class, so judges split between that mismatch and no mismatch on the same form, which on a form not labelled partial is a Critical `signature-mismatch` gap against none. A full form of that kind that leaves out an optional own prop or parameter is now a Critical gap, so a skill some runs passed can now stop at the hard gate. ([#1098](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1098); issue [#1089](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1089))

  **Migration:** If a skill now stops at the hard gate on a `signature-mismatch` gap over a form that marks members `?`, or a props list that gives a prop a default, write the members the gap says the form leaves out, as its `source_sig` gives them, or label the form partial when it shows only some of them on purpose (`Props (simplified)`), then run Test Skill again.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's signature rules now read a return written in words as a container of a type, such as `list of X` or `X list`, as that container with X as its type argument, not as a description followed by a type. A plural such as `dicts` names its type, a braced or bracketed list of key names inside the words is description, even a key named `type`, and words for the items that name no type, such as `list of results` or `HTML list`, write no type argument, which is then not compared. A documented `list of {type, count, samples, sample_size, relationships} dicts` therefore states `list[dict]` and matches the source's `list[dict[str, Any]]`. A parameter or prop type written that way reads the same. Before, a judge that read `dicts` as a type after a description compared `dict` alone and raised a Critical `signature-mismatch` gap on the correct form, failing the hard gate, while another judge passed the same skill. Because the item type now counts, a documented `Node list` against a source's `list[Edge]`, or `list of Nodes` against `Node`, makes the documented type differ from the source's, a Critical gap that some runs passed, so such a skill can now stop at the hard gate. ([#1096](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1096); issue [#1083](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1083))

  **Migration:** If a skill now stops at the hard gate on a `signature-mismatch` gap whose documented return or type is written in words as a container, write the container and item type the source declares, then run Test Skill again.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's signature rules now give one reading for two cases judges read either way. In the split-body cross-check, a return type one documented form writes that leaves out a member of the other form's union disagrees with it, whichever form writes it, so `-> Node` against `-> Node | None` is a High `split-body-mismatch` gap, while a parameter type that names some of the members of the other form's union, such as `node_name: list[str]` against `node_name: list[str] | None = None`, still agrees. In a Python call, a `*items` argument with no parameter left to pass (none a caller may pass by position from its position on, and no `*args`), or a `**mapping` argument with none left that a caller may pass by name and no `**kwargs`, passes arguments the declaration does not take, and a parameter a literal, variable or `name=value` argument of the call already passes is not left. So a documented `f(*items)` against `def f()`, or `f(a, **options)` against `def f(a)`, is a Critical `signature-mismatch` gap even though the call runs when its unpacking is empty, and a High `split-body-mismatch` gap against another documented form that writes that declaration, while `Settings(**config)` still matches `__init__(self, host, port)`. Before, one judge passed such a skill and another stopped it, so a skill some runs passed can now stop at the hard gate. ([#1096](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1096); issue [#1065](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1065))

  **Migration:** If a skill now stops at the hard gate on a `split-body-mismatch` gap, follow the gap's remediation: edit the file it names so it writes the return type or call of the form it says to take, whether or not a source settled it. If it stops on a `signature-mismatch` gap for a call whose `*items` or `**mapping` the declaration cannot take, drop that unpacking from the call. Then run Test Skill again.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's signature rules now say which declaration a type name means when the skill and the package between them document or export more than one declaration under it, such as cognee's base `DataPoint` and `ExtendableDataPoint`, which `cognee.low_level` exports as `DataPoint`. A form that writes that name bare means the one of them that the source file that writes the signature the form is compared with (the declaration's own file, or the file of the type or base class whose signature it takes) reaches by that name, as the source's own use of it does: the one that file imports (a star import included), declares or has in scope without an import (its own package or namespace) under that name, or names through a module or namespace it imports (`engine.DataPoint`). A form that writes the name through a module or namespace path means the one that path names, whatever that file reaches (`cognee.low_level.DataPoint` is `ExtendableDataPoint`). When that file reaches none of them by that name, the bare name means the type that file declares under it other than as an alias (a local `interface Options`), as before, and when it declares none, the one the skill documents under it, or any of them when the skill documents none or several; a judge that does not read the source matches a form that writes that name bare with any of them. A documented `-> DataPoint` therefore matches a source returning the base class it imports as `DataPoint`; before, a judge that read the name as the skill's `ExtendableDataPoint` could raise a Critical `signature-mismatch` gap on that form and fail the hard gate, while another judge passed the same skill. A form that writes the name in the skill's sense where that file reaches another of them (`-> DataPoint` for a declaration typed `ExtendableDataPoint`, in a file that imports the base `DataPoint`) now reads as the one that file reaches and is a Critical gap, so a skill some runs passed can now stop at the hard gate. ([#1098](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1098); issue [#1082](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1082))

  **Migration:** If a skill now stops at the hard gate on a `signature-mismatch` gap over a type name under which the skill and the package between them document or export more than one declaration, write the type the source writes there, as the gap's `source_sig` gives it (for example `ExtendableDataPoint`), or name the declaration meant through its module path (`cognee.low_level.DataPoint`), then run Test Skill again.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill now parses `_bmad/skf/config.yaml` and `preferences.yaml` with `skf-preflight.py`, the helper Setup Forge, Quick Skill and Ferris use, instead of reading them by hand. A `config.yaml` that is missing or does not parse, or a `sidecar_path` that is missing or still holds a placeholder, stops Test Skill when it starts (`helper-failed`, phase `on-activation:config`) with the helper's message and code, such as `CONFIG_MISSING`, where it used to go on; a missing `skf-preflight.py` stops it with `helper-missing` at the same phase. A missing `uv` now stops it at phase `on-activation:runtime` where it named `init:runtime`, still `runtime-missing`. These stops come before Test Skill reads `headless_mode` from `preferences.yaml`, so they print the `SKF_TEST_RESULT_JSON` line only under `--headless` or `-H`: a run made headless by `headless_mode: true` alone that lacks `uv` now shows the message alone, where it printed the line. A `preferences.yaml` that does not parse is named in one line and the run goes on with the defaults, so only `--headless` or `-H` makes that run headless. ([#1205](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1205); issue [#1118](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1118))

  **Migration:** If Test Skill now stops at phase `on-activation:config` naming `sidecar_path`, set `sidecar_path: _bmad/_memory/forger-sidecar` in `_bmad/skf/config.yaml` and run it again. A pipeline that branched on `error.phase` `init:runtime` for a missing `uv` branches on `on-activation:runtime` instead, and passes `--headless` (or `-H`) so a stop when Test Skill starts still prints its line.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill now compares the documented signature of a documented extra, a name the skill documents that no entry point exports but the extraction records in a scoped-in file (the recipe runner leaves out a Python name with a leading `_` and a TS or JS declaration its module does not export). The signature plan covered only the names the entry points export, so on oms-cocoindex 1.0.0 it checked 42 of the 67 documented signatures and Signature Accuracy read 100%, while no judge read the 25 extras' declarations, such as `detect_code_language`'s, and a Critical mismatch among them could not fail the hard gate. `load-coverage-inputs.py surface` now writes each such declaration under a new `internalDeclarations` key, which adds no name to a set and nothing to Export Coverage or Type Coverage. It leaves out a declaration where the stale-documentation lookup never looks, such as a test helper in `tests/` or `conftest.py`, or a file in a `scripts/` or `examples/` folder right below the package root, unless the provenance map cites that file for the name: a name declared only there stays stale documentation, and its signature is not compared there. `score-signatures.py plan` files the extra's check at that declaration, and `score` counts it in Signature Accuracy like any other documented signature, so a Critical mismatch adds a Critical `signature-mismatch` gap at the declaration. A method form the skill documents on such an extra, under `{owner}.{name}`, is compared and counted the same way, its check placed at the extra's declaration. When two files of the skill document the extra, or a method of it, differently, the split-body gap now cites the side that declaration contradicts, where it said no source settled the pair and could ask to edit the side that agrees with the source. Each such declaration also ends the span of the declaration before it in its file, as an exported one does, so for an exported name too a citation past it no longer binds a form to that earlier declaration, and an `annotation-contradicted` mismatch whose `evidence_line` lies past it is graded Critical, not Info. Forms that were never compared now are, so a skill that passed Test Skill can now stop at its hard gate. Type Coverage is unchanged, and the extra's Info observation now says its signature was compared with its declaration in the source. ([#1102](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1102); issue [#1087](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1087))

  **Migration:** If a skill now stops at the hard gate on a `signature-mismatch` gap, such as one at a documented extra's declaration, first check that the gap's Source is the declaration the skill documents and not an unrelated internal helper of the same bare name. If it is such a helper, add an `[AST:]` or `[SRC:]` citation of the right file on the line that documents the name, so the next test compares that declaration, instead of letting `@Ferris US <skill> --from-test-report` rewrite the form from the helper. Otherwise correct the form the gap quotes as `documented_sig`, then run Test Skill again.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's inventory contract and signature comparison rules now say, in the same words, that a `Key params` or `Key parameters` cell is a description cell, where a call that passes an argument, of a name the row's first cell lists, with no `await`, `new`, assignment, receiver or module path before it, such as `ValidationReport(status, summary, issues)` on a `cognee.ValidationReport` row, is that name's signature, its arguments, without the name, recorded in `params`, as the inventory floor already reads `Mem0Source(data, mode="re-derive")` in that column. Before, neither file named the column, so on a row the floor does not read, such as a `pydantic model` row, one reader recorded such a call in `params` and another as a usage, and on oms-cognee 1.6.2 eight PASS verdicts rested on that choice. Such a call's arguments are now compared as the parameter list they write: a `name=value` argument marks its parameter optional, and each bare argument beside it required. So a skill that passed can now stop at the hard gate on a `signature-mismatch` when its arguments are not the names of the parameters the constructor or function takes, or when they mark a parameter optional or required where the source does not, such as `status="pass"` for a pydantic model's required field. A call with a prefix, such as `await run(a, b)`, is still a usage, and an empty `name()` there is still a mention. ([#1103](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1103); issue [#1078](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1078))

  **Migration:** If Test Skill now stops at the hard gate on a `signature-mismatch` for a call written in a `Key params` cell, write that call's arguments as the bare names of the parameters the constructor or function takes, then run Test Skill again.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's inventory contract and signature comparison rules now say, in the same words, how a `Key params` or `Key parameters` cell's other calls are read: any call there but the row's own call with no prefix, whether of another name, of a method (a list of the row's class's methods included) or of a name the row's first cell lists, called with a prefix before the name or with empty parentheses, is read as in any other description cell, one the cell says the row's export runs included. So a call that passes an argument, such as `nodes_of_type(node_type)` on a `GraphSnapshot` row, `ZepSource(data, mode="hybrid")` on a `GraphitiSource` row, `forget(memory_only=True)` on a `cognee.update` row that says it runs that call or `.prune_system(graph=True)` on a `cognee.prune` row, is recorded whole in `usage_signature`, a bare leading `.` kept as its receiver, and an empty call, such as `.prune_data()` there or `get_cognee_version()` on a `cognee.__version__` row, is a mention with no form. Before, the files named only the row's own call, so on oms-cognee 1.6.2 readers split on seven names, `link_relations()`, `records()`, `to_dict()`, `.prune_data()`, `.prune_system(graph=True, ...)`, `get_cognee_version()` and `serve()`: a usage, `params`, `params ""` or no entry, the leading `.` kept or dropped. Such a call is now compared as a call, on a `method` entry with the member of that name its owner declares, under `{owner}.{name}`, as Test Skill compares a method form that names its owner, and on any other entry with its name's declaration: each argument it passes must exist, each required parameter must be passed, and a keyword-only one only by name. On oms-cognee 1.6.2 each such call matches its source, the method calls `nodes_of_type(node_type)` and `.prune_system(graph=True, vector=True, metadata=False, cache=True)` as well as `forget(memory_only=True)`, `recall(query_text, scope=["tools"])` and `ZepSource(data, mode="hybrid")`. So a skill that passed while a reader recorded such a call in `params`, a method's call included, can now stop at the hard gate on a `signature-mismatch`, such as for a keyword-only parameter passed by position, while a bare argument is now a value at its position, so one that is not the parameter's name no longer stops it, and the totals can move either way. The signature score also now matches a mismatch to the documented form it quotes whether or not it writes a usage's bare leading `.`, so a partial usage's mismatch is filed against that usage and keeps its partial grade. ([#1103](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1103); issue [#1073](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1073))

  **Migration:** If Test Skill now stops at the hard gate on a `signature-mismatch` for a call written in a `Key params` cell, pass each argument as the callable takes it, a keyword-only parameter as `name=value`, or write the parameters with their types, as in `fetch(url: str)`, which reads as a signature, then run Test Skill again.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill no longer counts a name the skill writes only as a mention as an export it documents, whatever the prose says of it. A name bare in prose, a bullet list or a description cell, in an import, an `__all__` or other export list or a comment, or after a heading's first word (`cognee.low_level` in "Data primitives: `cognee.low_level`") gets no inventory entry unless the inventory floor gives it a place. It records no Medium `stale-documentation` gap asking Update Skill to remove accurate text, as 74 of oms-storybook-react-vite's 75 did on its latest run, and no Info documented extra, but it is no longer checked against the source either, so a stale one records no gap. Where Export Coverage counts the inventory's names (the barrel branch, and the scalar branch when it counts its set or looks the documented names up), a name the source exports and the skill writes only as a mention now counts as undocumented and lowers Export Coverage, with a Medium `missing-export` gap (`missing-type` for a type): in a rehearsal with three readers per reference skill, all three leave out eight exports oms-uitripled's latest run counted as documented, such as `Button` and `Card`, and oms-storybook-react-vite's `storybookTest`. A stack skill's count of the export names its provenance map cites now counts such a name as missing too, and the verified count of a padded declared count as absent, so a declared count that equals the denominator records a High `numerator-inflation` gap; a docs-only run counts it as no item. So this can block a skill that passed: that gap stops Test Skill at its hard gate, and a lower Export Coverage can turn a PASS verdict into a FAIL. A name a place writes a form, `methods`, `properties` or `fields` of, or writes in a heading that opens with it, an export table's first cell or a fenced declaration of it, keeps its entry, which with no form sits at that heading, row or declaration, never at a prose line that names it first. This narrows the type-mention and not-covered rules, which counted a code span that is the name, or prose that describes it. ([#1103](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1103); issue [#1071](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1071))

  **Migration:** If Test Skill now stops at the hard gate on a `numerator-inflation` gap, or its verdict falls to FAIL on a lower Export Coverage, because of a name the skill writes only as a mention, document that name where the inventory gives it an entry (a heading that opens with it, an export table's first cell or a fenced declaration of it), or remove a name the gap lists as absent, or a stack counts as missing, from `metadata.json` `exports` or the provenance map, then run Test Skill again.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's verified count of a padded declared count, and a stack skill's count of the export names its provenance map cites, now count a name only when the documented inventory gives it an entry and the skill's text writes it. Before, both looked each name up in the skill's text alone. A name the skill writes only in a type position such as a parameter type, only in a sentence saying it does not cover it, only as a local import alias or a name it says the source does not export, or only in a form marked removed or from an earlier version now joins the High `numerator-inflation` gap's absent exports or the stack's missing count, as it already did where Export Coverage counts the inventory's names. A name a module path qualifies, such as `cognee.add` or `ops.text.RecursiveSplitter`, has the entry the inventory gives its last segment, and a name the provenance map types `module` or `package`, which the inventory has no kind for, still counts when the text writes it. A stack counted from its libraries and integration pairs still looks them up in the skill's text, since the inventory lists exports, not libraries. This can block a skill that passed: such a name now makes a declared count that equals the denominator a High `numerator-inflation` gap, and lowers a stack's Export Coverage. ([#1097](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1097); issue [#1068](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1068))

  **Migration:** If Test Skill now stops at the hard gate on a `numerator-inflation` gap, document each absent name it lists where the inventory gives it an entry (a heading, an export table's first cell or a fenced declaration), or remove it from `metadata.json` `exports`, then run Test Skill again. Do the same for a cited name a stack now counts as missing, removing it from the provenance map instead.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill now reads a documented table row's cited files in its cells alone. For a name the source declares in several files, that scan picks the declaration a signature check reads and, when the name's documented forms cite none of those files, the declaring file of a stale homonym; it also finds a file that passes on another package's names. It read the `[AST:]` and `[SRC:]` citations on the line after each line that wrote the name, so a row also took the citations of the next row, which documents another export: a row with no citation could place the check at the file the next row cites, with no `candidates` for the judge, and a row that cited its own declaration could count a second file and leave the check unsettled. A table row outside a fenced block now reads no line after it, a line after the table included, as a form's own citations are already read, while a heading, a prose line and a line in a fenced block read the next line as before. For cocoindex, the `Settings` row no longer takes `python/cocoindex/setting.py` from the `ServerSettings` row after it. This can block a skill that passed: a check that listed candidates can now sit at the one declaration a row cites and record a Critical `signature-mismatch` gap there. A Gap Report can also gain a Medium `stale-documentation` gap where the next row's citation alone made a stale name an Info documented extra, or an Info observation of another package's `export *`. ([#1104](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1104); issue [#1066](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1066))

  **Migration:** If a skill now stops at the hard gate on a check placed at the declaration a table row cites, correct the form, or the row's citation when it points at the wrong declaration, then run Test Skill again. A row that relied on a citation written on the line after it, or after its table, takes that citation into one of its cells. Where a new Medium `stale-documentation` gap points at a table row whose name the source still declares, or passes on from another package, cite that file in one of the row's cells, then run Test Skill again.

- **skf-test-skill:** When the threshold fallback accepts a run at the 80% floor (a score of 80% or more under a higher target, with no cap fired), Test Skill no longer writes `evidence-report-fallback.md` beside the test report. Its findings were the Gap Report again and its summary repeated the score, it had no run id in its name, and nothing read it. Instead, `build-result-context.py settle` adds a `### Threshold Fallback` subsection to the test report's Completeness Score section, right after the Result block (on a degraded run, the Access Degradation Notice still follows it): the attempted threshold, the achieved score, the accepted floor, the threshold source, the latest earlier test report beside this one (or none found) and a pointer to the Gap Report, which lists the run's gaps. The report frontmatter loses `evidenceReportPath`, and the result file's `summary` loses `evidence_report_path`. `threshold_fallback` and `original_threshold` are unchanged. ([#1217](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1217); issue [#1190](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1190))

  **Migration:** Read a fallback's details from the test report's Threshold Fallback subsection and its gaps from the Gap Report, and stop reading `evidenceReportPath` from the report frontmatter and `summary.evidence_report_path` from `skf-test-skill-result-latest.json`. An `evidence-report-fallback.md` an earlier run left in a version folder still counts as SKF's file and can be deleted.

- **skf-test-skill, skf-update-skill:** Test Skill now compares each method form the skill documents (an inventory `method` entry that names its `owner`) with the member of that name its owner declares in the source (for an object, its class), or a base class there (in Java, Kotlin, C# and Swift, any overload of that name the owner or a base declares), and counts it in Signature Accuracy. Before, no method form was compared, so a wrong one passed, even one written in a single file where no split-body pair could catch it. A method is checked only when the source surface records its owner and the ast-grep recipe runner built it (the per-file scan Test Skill falls back to when the runner cannot run compares no method form), under the name `{owner}.{name}`, never mixed with a function of the same name, and its gap is titled `Signature mismatch: {owner}.{name}`, with its Source at the file and line of the member the source declares. A wrong method form now raises a Critical `signature-mismatch` gap, so a skill that passed Test Skill can now stop at its hard gate. A member that no declaration in the source tree gives the owner, such as one inherited from another package's class, is left uncompared and counts as matching. Update Skill's `--from-test-report` run does not repair such a gap, since a method is no export of the provenance map: it lists the gap as not repaired, with the reason, and writes nothing for it. ([#1101](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1101); issue [#1088](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1088))

  **Migration:** For a skill that now stops at the hard gate on such a gap, correct by hand the method form the gap quotes to the signature its Source cites, then run Test Skill again.

- **skf-update-skill:** Update Skill no longer asks `[C] Continue to Write` after you resolve `[MANUAL]` conflicts: the merged version is already written by then, so a clean or resolved merge goes straight on to write the skill's metadata. A headless run no longer records the `merge.clean-merge-gate` decision, which leaves the `headless_decisions[].gate` enum of the `SKF_UPDATE_RESULT_JSON` line. With no wait left before it, the update no longer renews its run lock before it writes the metadata, so `write:run-lock` no longer occurs as an `error.phase`. ([#1220](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1220); issue [#1194](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1194))

  **Migration:** Stop reading the `merge.clean-merge-gate` decision in `headless_decisions`. Treat `merge:run-lock` as the only `error.phase` of an update that lost its run lock while it waited; `write:run-lock` no longer occurs.

- **skf-update-skill:** A headless Update Skill run with `--from-test-report` that finds no finished test report of the skill, or cannot look for one because `skf-find-test-report.py` is missing or fails, now stops `blocked` before it takes the run lock (`error.phase` `init:test-report`, an `error.reason` that starts `input-missing`) and writes nothing. Before, it went on as a normal update that checked the source for changes and reported `success` or `no-changes`, so a pipeline's repair call ran an update nobody asked for. An interactive run still warns and checks the source for changes, and now records a `test-report-missing` warning. ([#1220](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1220); issue [#1194](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1194))

  **Migration:** Run Test Skill on the skill before a headless `--from-test-report` run, or drop the flag to check the source for changes. A pipeline that repairs a skill from its test report branches on `error.phase` `init:test-report` to run Test Skill first, unless the `error.reason` names `skf-find-test-report.py`, which asks for a re-install of SKF.

- **skf-update-skill, skf-create-skill:** Update Skill now moves the citations of the exports that moved in the source with the provenance verifier (`skf-verify-provenance-completeness.py fix --moves`) instead of having the model edit each one: in one pass, so when one export moves from line 6 to 7 and the next from 7 to 8, each citation moves once and lands on its own export's line, never twice onto a neighbour's. A move across files also changes the cited file, a citation another export claims or one inside a `[MANUAL]` block stays where it is with a `provenance:` warning in the run log, and a repair moves the citations of each export its spot-check found moved in every file of the package. The labels and node kinds the provenance checks flag are now set by the verifier's new `relabel` subcommand, which applies the Relabel Rule and writes the map, instead of by the model. A repair now runs the public-API runner once over the whole scope, and its entry-point diff, the one a normal update reads, decides whether each new export the repair located is public or internal, instead of the model walking barrels: you are asked only where the runner cannot tell (Quick tier, a run that did not finish, a name the runner could not trace, a language no recipe reads). When an export moved and the verifier is missing or refuses its input, the update now stops with `halted-for-write-failure` (`error.phase` `merge:move-citations`) before it publishes the new version, where before the model moved the citations itself. When the verifier is missing and no export moved, the evidence report shows `Provenance: SKIP (verifier missing; re-install SKF)` and the run log warns, instead of the model comparing the export lists by hand. A reference app's `pattern_surfaces_documented`, in Update Skill and Create Skill alike, is now the number of data rows in SKILL.md's `## Pattern Surface` tables, counted by `skf-render-metadata-stats.py --skill-md`, which refuses a count that differs. An Update Skill run on a reference app whose SKILL.md has no `Pattern Surface` heading now stops with `halted-for-write-failure` (`error.phase` `write:stats`), where before the rows were counted by eye and the run went on; Create Skill has you fix its staged table instead. ([#1220](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1220); issue [#1191](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1191))

  **Migration:** Before you update a reference app, make sure its SKILL.md holds its pattern table under a `## Pattern Surface` heading, the heading Create Skill writes. When the stop names a missing `skf-verify-provenance-completeness.py` or `skf-scan-skill-md-structure.py`, re-install SKF and run the update again.

### Added
