- **skf-brief-skill:** When a finished `skill-brief.yaml` already covers the target, an interactive Brief Skill run now offers, right after the target, `[U] Revise` to review that brief and write it back with every field it holds, or `[N] New brief` to gather a new one. Several such briefs are listed as `[U1]`, `[U2]` and so on, newest first, each with its name and date. The match reads the brief's `source_repo`, or the `doc_urls` of a docs-only brief, however the target is written. Before, a run never offered to revise a finished brief. ([#1213](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1213); issue [#1137](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1137))
- **skf-campaign:** An invalid pin no longer ends an interactive campaign at Pin Validation. Campaign shows each invalid pin with its suggestions, asks for the corrected pins, writes each answer with the new `campaign-state.py set-skill --pin` (an empty pin means the latest release, and a Tier A pin that is not an `X.Y.Z` version is refused with exit code `2`) to `_campaign-state.yaml` and, through `--brief-file`, to the skill's target in `campaign-brief.yaml`, so the kickoff and a campaign seeded from that brief again hold the corrected pin, logs it as a `decision` and checks the pins again. A headless run still stops with exit code `5` (`invalid-pin`), and its halt message now names the ways out: run `campaign resume` interactively, which asks for the corrected pins, or, since a headless `campaign resume` checks the same pin again, run `campaign`, choose overwrite and give the archived `campaign-brief.yaml` with corrected pins. ([#1214](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1214); issue [#1143](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1143))
- **skf-campaign:** `campaign-report.md` now says why each failed or skipped skill failed or was skipped, and ends with an Operator Decisions section that lists the `decision` and `auto` lines the campaign wrote to the decision log: your choices at each question and the defaults a headless or unattended run took. An overwrite leaves the decision log in place, so the lines stamped before the campaign started, an earlier campaign's among them, are left out. Each skill in `_campaign-state.yaml` keeps the reason as `halt_reason`, which the Skill Loop writes with the new `campaign-state.py set-skill --halt-reason` (a test failure, a sub-skill's halt reason, a directive Skip List entry or an unmet dependency) and the Tier B batch with `apply-batch` (the batch's error code, `no-batch-result`, or the Skip List entry). A copy of the report template set in `report_template_path` shows the Operator Decisions section only once it adds `{{operator_decisions}}`. ([#1214](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1214); issue [#1143](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1143))
- **skf-campaign:** Campaign's plan gate now offers `[U]nattended` beside `[P]roceed` and `[C]ancel`, and `campaign resume` takes `--unattended`. Either one makes the rest of the campaign unattended (`campaign.unattended` in the state, written by `campaign-state.py apply-plan --unattended` or `set-campaign --unattended`): at a skill whose dependencies have not completed, the Skill Loop takes the default a headless run takes, skipping the skill when every unmet dependency failed or was skipped and halting with exit code `13` otherwise, and logs it as `auto`, while every other question, the Export gate included, still waits for you. Each choice is logged as a `decision`. ([#1214](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1214); issue [#1143](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1143))
- **skf-create-stack-skill:** An interactive Stack Skill run that stopped after it wrote its draft, and before it wrote the stack, can now pick up at the review. The next interactive run with the same `stack_name` finds that run's folder under `_bmad-output/.skf-run/` and asks whether to resume at the review of that draft (`[Y]`), the draft kept as it was, your own edits included, or start fresh (`[N]`), which leaves the earlier folder untouched and shows its path, so you can delete it yourself. Once a later run has finished that stack, no run offers that draft again. A headless run never asks and always starts fresh. Each run now saves its first-step settings (the stack name, mode, scanned folder, inputs, template paths, hook and the forge tier after any downgrade) to `run.json` in its run folder, so steps 7 and 8, which write and validate the stack, read the tier from there, and a run now stops with exit `3` (`helper-missing`) at its first step, before any library is counted or extracted, when `skf-atomic-write.py` is missing (it stopped only at the output step before), and with exit `4` (`write-failure`) when `run.json` cannot be written. ([#1215](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1215); issue [#1150](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1150))
- **skf-create-stack-skill:** Stack Skill's helpers now read the extraction bundle themselves, so no step copies its data by hand. `skf-render-stack-metadata.py pair-tiers` and `metadata` take `--bundle <extraction-bundle.json>` in place of `--input`, `pair-tiers` on a code-mode bundle taking the qualifying pairs from `--pairs`, and `skf-skill-inventory.py version primary --bundle <extraction-bundle.json>` picks the primary library from a code-mode bundle; steps 4 to 7 call them on the bundle file instead of piping a payload they built. `metadata` also prints `hubs` (each library with 3 or more partners, with its partners) and `library_order` (by partner count, then import count in code mode or tier in compose mode, then name), which step 5 shows and step 6 compiles from, and step 4 counts the libraries at each tier with it. The provenance map's `detection_method` now comes from each pair's `qualifier` by a fixed table (`grep-co-import` gives `co-import grep`, and the three compose qualifiers their schema values), and `provenance` refuses a missing qualifier, an unknown one or one of the other mode with exit `2`, so a run can no longer write a detection method outside the schema; the bundle's pairs no longer carry `detection_method` or `hubs`. `skf-enumerate-stack-skills.py` entries carry the skill's `metadata_name`, `version` and `source_authority`, so step 2 no longer reopens each constituent's `metadata.json`, and `enumerate --bundle-entries <names>` prints each compose-mode bundle entry (`confidence` its `evidence_tier`) and the names it did not find, which step 4 writes to the bundle and halts on. ([#1215](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1215); issue [#1154](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1154))
- **skf-create-stack-skill:** Stack Skill's scope review now takes the recommended scope from the import counter in both modes: `skf-count-imports.py` gains a `scope` subcommand that turns the import counts (code mode) or the picked skills (compose mode), `scope_overrides` and the published stack into the libraries in scope, each library left out with its reason, the published libraries kept and the unknown overrides, and the headless scope decision copies `scope`, `dropped` and `prior_kept` from it. The scope review's below-threshold table becomes a Left out table that lists every library left out with its reason, override and published-stack exclusions included, in compose mode too. A code-mode `scope_overrides` key that names no dependency now records a `scope-override-unknown` warning, as compose mode already did. When the import name of an unresolved dependency is known, the count runs again with the new repeatable `--module <name>=<import name>` flag of `skf-count-imports.py count`, and the library ranks with the others; a value that is not `<name>=<import name>`, names no dependency or names dependencies of several ecosystems exits `2`. Compose mode reads each skill's architecture layer from `skf-comention-pairs.py mentions`, records an `architecture-doc-parse-failed` warning when that helper is missing or cannot read the document, and halts with exit `3` (`helper-missing`, phase `compose-scope:scope`) when `skf-count-imports.py` is missing. ([#1215](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1215); issue [#1153](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1153))
- **skf-create-stack-skill:** Stack Skill now writes and trims its `context-snippet.md` with the new `skf-render-stack-metadata.py snippet` subcommand, instead of trimming it by hand and measuring it after each cut. The run writes only the gotchas text; the helper builds the root, `|IMPORTANT:`, `|stack:` and `|integrations:` lines from the extraction bundle (libraries by import count, or export count in compose mode, pairs by co-import file count, `|integrations: none` for a stack with no pair), and while the snippet is above its token budget (`--budget`, 120 by default, counted as `len(text)//4`) it drops the gotchas line, strips the library versions, keeps the top 8 libraries and then the top 5 pairs, each cut list ending `, ...+N more`. It prints `tokens`, `trims_applied` and `over_budget`, and the run records `snippet-over-budget` when the last cut still leaves it above the budget. `skf-validate-output.py --skill-type stack` now reports a context snippet with no `|stack:` or `|integrations:` line as a `medium` issue, and takes `--forge-version <dir>`, which checks that the forge data version folder holds `provenance-map.json` and `evidence-report.md`, and `--active-link <skill_group> --expected-version <version>`, which checks that `<skill_group>/active` resolves to that version (a Windows junction included); each miss is a `medium` issue under `validation.stack_workspace`. The validation step passes these flags and records each workspace or link issue as an error, so it no longer checks those files and the link by hand unless the validator is missing. A house-style copy of the stack template no longer shapes the context snippet's lines: the helper writes them in the bundled form, and only a run whose installed helper has no `snippet` writes them from the copy. ([#1215](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1215); issue [#1157](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1157))
- **skf-drop-skill:** Dropping the active version while other versions remain no longer sends you out of the run: Drop Skill offers `[K] Keep`, which points the skill's `active` link at another version on disk, records it as the active version in the export manifest with the export date it already had, then drops the old version in the same run. A headless run takes the same path with a `keep=<version>` argument and records the choice in the result record's `headless_decisions`. Without it, a headless drop of the active version still stops with exit `5` (`active-version-guard-refused`), and its message now names the `keep=` value to re-run with. A `keep` makes that version active whichever version the run drops, so pass it only to change the active version. `[K] Keep` never moves an `active` link that names another version, such as one forged and not exported yet: it offers that version when the export manifest lists it, and no version otherwise. A `keep` that names no version the drop can keep stops with exit `2` (`input-invalid`), and an `active` link that cannot be moved stops with exit `4` (`write-failed`, phase `execute:keep-active`) before anything changes. The result record's summary names the kept version in `keep_version`. ([#1216](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1216); issue [#1160](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1160))
- **skf-drop-skill:** Drop Skill's scope question adds `[O] Older versions` (`version=older` in a headless run), which drops every version in the export manifest except the active one and the ones already deprecated, in one run with one confirmation and one context-file rebuild. Each version gets its own purge check, `active` link repair and final-state check, and the manifest marks them all deprecated in one write. When no such version is left, an interactive run asks again and a headless run stops with exit `2` (`input-invalid`). In an Older versions purge, the envelope's `forge_left_in_place` is a list of the forge folders left in place, even when there is one, instead of a single path. ([#1216](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1216); issue [#1160](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1160))
- **skf-export-skill:** Export Skill's result contract now records every orphan choice in `deviations`: `drop_external_skills` when you drop managed-section rows that no export manifest entry backs, each skill with its version and the context files it was found in, and `clear_orphan_context` with the context files the run cleared, beside the `preserve_external_skills` entry that keeping those rows already wrote. A run that dropped rows or cleared a file used to leave `deviations` out, so its result read as an export that changed nothing outside the canonical path. ([#1209](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1209); issue [#1165](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1165))
- **skf-export-skill:** A headless Export Skill run now records each warning it displays in its run folder, so the `SKF_EXPORT_RESULT_JSON` line lists them in `warnings` as `<code>: <skill>: <detail>`: a test report that failed, passed only with drift, was inconclusive, records no verdict or is missing, the export gate's warnings, gotchas left off, carried or dropped, a trimmed snippet, a context file with malformed markers, and each skill the managed section leaves out. The run used to record only the customization resolver's warning, so such a run read as a clean success. The `load-skill.confirmation` decision in `headless_decisions` also gains `evidence.test_results`, one `{skill, verdict, score, report}` per skill. The headless run folder's steps move from SKILL.md to the Run Folder section of `references/result-envelope.md`, which lists every code, so SKILL.md stays under its token budget. ([#1209](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1209); issue [#1166](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1166))
- **skf-export-skill, skf-drop-skill:** Export Skill takes `--version <v>` to make an earlier version of one skill active again, as a rollback: `@Ferris EX cocoindex --version 0.5.0` points the skill's `active` link at 0.5.0, exports it and records it as the manifest's `active_version`, which archives the version it replaces. It takes one skill, never `--all`, and only a version whose package is still on disk and that the export manifest does not mark deprecated: anything else stops the run with exit `3` (`resolution-failure`) before it writes, naming the versions it can restore. A link that cannot be moved stops it with exit `4` (`write-failed`) before the manifest changes. Drop Skill's refusal to drop the active version now names this command (`[EX] Export Skill <skill> --version <version to keep>`) in place of a `flip-link` run by hand, and Ferris's menu names the flag on its EX row. ([#1212](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1212); issue [#1172](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1172))
- **skf-forger:** On a first run, before Setup Forge has set a forge tier and with no `tier_override` in `preferences.yaml`, a pick you start Ferris with that needs the tier now asks first, instead of running at once and stopping at its first workflow that needs the tier. Such a pick runs Analyze Source, Brief Skill, Create Skill, Create Stack Skill, Test Skill, Update Skill or Audit Skill, as every alias does. The greeting says no forge tier is set yet and asks once whether to set it first or to run the pick as given. For an alias or a chain, setting it first runs `SF <pick>`, the pick as one chain with SF ahead of it: an alias keeps its arguments (`SF forge-auto <url>`) and each code its bracket (`SF AS[cocoindex] US TS`). For a pick that names one workflow, such as `TS cocoindex`, `BS`, `US cocoindex --from-test-report` or `audit cocoindex`, it runs SF, then the pick as given, so the pick keeps its arguments, its flags and its own questions. A `TS` pick with `--tier=` sets its own tier and runs at once, and a bare repository URL first asks whether you mean `QS` or `forge-auto`, after which only `forge-auto` gets the tier question. A headless start asks nothing and stops with "No forge tier yet. Run SF first, or start the chain as `SF <pick>`." for an alias or a chain, or with "No forge tier yet. Run SF first, then `<pick>`." for one workflow. ([#1212](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1212); issue [#1170](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1170))
- **skf-forger:** Ferris now answers a described goal, such as `@Ferris I want skills for my whole monorepo`, with the one code, alias or chain the Workflow Selection table of the skill lifecycle knowledge recommends for it, then waits for your pick; on a first run, a recommendation that needs the forge tier comes with `SF` ahead of it. A headless start that describes a goal runs nothing and stops with "No workflow named." and the recommendation to start with instead. `KI` now ends with an offer to explain any knowledge fragment you name, briefly, with the menu codes whose workflows put it to work. ([#1212](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1212); issue [#1171](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1171))
- **skf-forger:** A new `resume` pick takes the offer a stopped chain left at once: `@Ferris resume`, or `/skf-forger resume --headless` from a script (`campaign resume` stays Campaign's). A headless resume writes a failed pipeline result with no step and stops with `user-action-required: <action>` when the offer needs you to act first, so the offer stays for the next start, or with `nothing-to-resume: <message>` when there is no offer; one whose `reopen` call fails writes a failed result too. A headless start with no pick, which stops with "Nothing to run", now names `/skf-forger resume --headless` and the offer's route when a stopped chain left one. ([#1212](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1212); issue [#1169](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1169))
- **skf-forger:** A pipeline alias can now follow `SF`, as in `SF forge-auto <repo-or-doc-url>`, `SF maintain <skill>` or the legacy `SF deepwiki <url>`: the chain runs Setup Forge first, then the alias's workflows, keeping the alias, its threshold (forge-auto's 90%) and its arguments, which go to the workflow after SF. `parse-pipeline.py` used to report the alias as an unknown code. `SF onboard` stops as `onboard` does. ([#1212](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1212); issue [#1170](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1170))
- **skf-forger:** Ferris now names an unfinished campaign when you open him and in WS, with its stage and how many of its skills are done, and its skills take `CA` as their next code until it finishes. `forge-status.py` prints it as `campaign`, reads it from `--campaign-workspace` (`forge-data/_campaign/` by default), and gains `--campaign-only`, the greeting's check, which reads the campaign alone. A campaign state it cannot tally is a `campaign_unavailable` warning. ([#1212](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1212); issue [#1169](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1169))
- **skf-forger:** WS now reads each skill's latest audit. Drift an audit found after the skill's test (`MINOR`, `SIGNIFICANT` or `CRITICAL`) shows as the entry's `drift` and makes `US <name>` its next code, or `US <name> --target-ref <ref>` when the audit found that upstream moved to a newer ref. A `CLEAN` audit, one older than the test, or one that does not parse (an `audit_result_unreadable` warning) leaves the code the test verdict gives. ([#1212](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1212); issue [#1169](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1169))
- **skf-quick-skill:** When the skill's `active` pointer names a build another workflow made (a Create Skill build, for example), Quick Skill now asks whether to point it at the new quick skill or keep it, instead of moving it without asking. A headless or `--batch` run keeps it, records the new `finalize.active-pointer` decision in `headless_decisions`, and reports `summary.active_pointer` as the new value `kept-prior-active`, and its completion summary and `outputs` then leave out the pointer. A pointer on another quick skill is moved, and a missing one created, as before. Test Skill and Export Skill act on the version `active` names, so after a kept pointer a `forge-quick` or `QS TS EX` chain, and a campaign's export of a Tier B skill, test and export that other build, not the new quick skill: to test and export the quick skill, run `@Ferris QS <target>` on its own and answer `[F]` first. ([#1223](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1223); issue [#1175](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1175))
- **skf-quick-skill:** When the repository has no tag for the version you pinned (`@Ferris QS cognee@9.9.9`), an interactive Quick Skill run now lists the nearest tags and lets you build from one of them, drop the version and build from the default branch (or from the branch a `/tree/` URL names), or cancel (exit code `6`, `user-cancelled`), instead of stopping. A headless or `--batch` run still stops with exit code `3` (`resolution-failure`) and the tags in `error.details.available_tags`, and a run that cannot read the repository's tags at all still stops with exit code `3` in both modes. ([#1223](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1223); issue [#1175](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1175))
- **skf-refine-architecture:** Refine Architecture now offers the architecture document a Verify Stack report verified as the default for its architecture question, when the report it found or was given names that document and the file exists: press Enter to use it, or give another path. When you refine another document, it says once which document the report verified, since its verdicts are about that one. A headless run still needs `--architecture-doc`. The feasibility report's `architectureDoc` key is now part of the shared report contract, and `skf-validate-feasibility-report.py` returns it (`null` when it is empty or absent). ([#1219](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1219); issue [#1179](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1179))
- **skf-refine-architecture:** Refine Architecture can now resume a review that stopped before you approved it with `[C]` or cancelled it with `[X]`, when the session ended or lost its context. The next interactive run on the same architecture document, unchanged since that run read it, while that run's plan, its build record and its draft are still there, offers `[R] Resume the review of the draft from <timestamp>` or `[N] Start a new run`. `[R]` takes that run's settings back (its scope, its Verify Stack report, its output folder and its refinement rules), checks the refinement rules again, rebuilds the draft from the kept plan and shows the review again without reading the skills again; findings that review dropped or took back stay as it left them. `[N]` leaves the stopped run's folder as it is. A cancel at that prompt stops with exit `6` (`user-cancelled`). When the document was edited after that run read it, the run says so and starts over. A headless run, a run on another document, a review that ended with `[X]` or with a `[C]` that wrote the refined document, and a review a headless run stopped are never offered a resume, and any other run in between ends the chance to resume it once it has checked its inputs and found the skills. ([#1219](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1219); issue [#1178](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1178))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's result envelope and result files now list these degradations in `warnings` when a run meets one, where before they carried only the customization resolver's warning: `run-lock-replaced` (the run took over a stale lock), `flat-skill-migrated`, `metadata-missing`, `workspace-drift-not-checked` (the drift helper could not read a source tree), `test-mode-defaulted-naive`, `skill-check-unavailable` with the reason, and `tessl-review` for each warning Tessl Review raised. Each stage records its warning in the run folder as it meets it, so a long run that loses its context still reports it, and a record that fails never stops the run. ([#1217](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1217); issue [#1185](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1185))
- **skf-test-skill, skf-update-skill:** A Test Skill run that a cap fails now says which tooling to restore. The Completeness Score section shows the cap on a **Cap:** line, the result file's `summary` holds it as `capReason`, and the score step and the final report recommend making the named tool work again (the frontmatter validator finishing within 30 seconds, or skill-check running and scoring the skill, or Tessl Review turned on) and testing again, since no skill edit lifts a cap, with Update Skill as well only when the skill also scored below its threshold. The envelope's exit code and `next_workflow` (`update-skill`) are unchanged. When skill-check did not run, the Gap Report holds an Info `skill-check not run` gap with the reason (`not-available`, `timeout-120s` or `no-json`) and the steps that make it run again, a probe that exited 127 (no `timeout` or no `npx` command) included: `gap-ledger.py append --from external` takes the reason file as `--skill-check-not-run`. Update Skill's not-routed reason for an `external-validator` gap now also says to make skill-check run again when the gap says it did not run. The skill-check step handles its probe and its run in one place. ([#1217](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1217); issue [#1185](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1185))
- **skf-update-skill:** A headless Update Skill run whose only `[MANUAL]` conflicts are position conflicts, where new generated content shifts a `[MANUAL]` block, now keeps each block, which moves with its section, and goes on, recording one `merge.manual-conflict` decision per block in `headless_decisions`. A headless repair from a test report whose structural fix would edit inside a `[MANUAL]` block leaves that edit out and warns `structural-fix-skipped`. A headless run still stops `halted-for-manual-mismatch`, writing nothing, when a conflict is an orphaned block or a block that names a renamed export. ([#1220](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1220); issue [#1194](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1194))
- **skf-update-skill:** Update Skill's baseline summary now takes the export count and the provenance age from `skf-load-provenance.py normalize` instead of reading the provenance map by hand. Its new `--age-from-last-update` counts the age from the map's `last_update`, the skill's last extraction, else from its `generated_at`, else from the file's last change. A provenance map that is not JSON, or not a JSON object, now stops the run at once with `blocked` and the new halt reason `provenance-invalid` (`error.phase` `init:load-provenance-map`), instead of failing a later step. ([#1220](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1220); issue [#1193](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1193))
- **skf-update-skill:** Update Skill takes a new `--source-root <path>` flag for a skill built from a local folder that has moved: the run reads the source there, in every mode, adds a `source-root-overridden` warning, and records the new folder as `source_root` in `metadata.json` when it writes, so later runs read it too. A path that is not a folder halts `blocked` at `init:resolve-source-path` with `source-root-missing`. A skill read from a remote repository, at any tier and in every mode, and a docs-only skill halt `blocked` with `source-root-needs-local-source`. A folder you name when Update Skill asks for a moved local source is recorded the same way, while one you name for a remote skill is read for that run only, and a headless run whose local folder is gone now says to re-run with `--source-root`. `skf-build-change-manifest.py metadata` takes `--source-root` to write it, and the new `skf-source-tree.py classify` tells, with no network call, whether a skill is read from a remote repository. ([#1220](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1220); issue [#1193](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1193))
- **skf-update-skill:** Update Skill now chooses the version to update with `skf-skill-inventory.py resolve`, which checks that the version's package is on disk, instead of reading the export manifest and the `active` link by hand. An `active` link to an empty version folder no longer stops the run at "No SKILL.md found": Update Skill updates the version the export manifest names or, for a skill never exported, the newest version on disk, with a `version-newest-on-disk` warning. When the new version would go into a version folder that holds no skill, such as the empty folder that link names, the update leaves that folder as it is, writes the next patch version instead and warns `version-folder-skipped`, where before it stopped with `halted-for-write-failure` because that version already existed. When the helper cannot resolve the skill for another reason, the run stops with `blocked` and the new halt reason `resolve-failed` (`error.phase` `init:resolve`). ([#1220](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1220); issue [#1193](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1193))

### Changed

- **all workflows:** Text from a finding no longer runs as a shell command on your machine when the health check files an issue or a comment. The body went on the command line inside double quotes, so the shell ran each span in backticks (the paths and evidence a body quotes) as a command and put its output in its place: the `Section fingerprint:` line the dedup Action reads could come out empty, and a double quote in the body broke the command. Now each body goes to `gh` as a file with `--body-file`, one file for each post in the `bodies/` subfolder of the local queue folder (`{forge_data_folder}/improvement-queue`), kept there as the record of what was sent or tried, so backticks, `$` and quotes in it no longer run or break the command, and the `Section fingerprint:` line reaches the issue as written. A new issue that fails to post is now saved to the local queue with the reason "Posting these to GitHub failed." instead of being lost, its file holding the body that failed to post. A run that files some findings and saves others to the local queue now says `Workflow complete.` once, after the saved files, instead of after its new issues and again after the saved files, and a run whose findings all went to open issues as reactions or comments now ends with it too. ([#1206](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1206); issue [#1203](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1203))
- **all workflows:** At a matching open issue, the health check's `[R]` and `[C]` choices now react and comment on that issue in the health-check repository. Both calls named no repository: the reaction's path left out the owner, so it failed with a 404, and the comment went to an issue of your own project. Each choice was still recorded in the seen-issue cache (`~/.skf/health-check-seen.json`), which kept later sightings of the defect from being reported while the issue stayed open. Now a choice is recorded only when every call of it posted, and one with a call that fails is saved to the local queue with the reason "Posting these to GitHub failed." A `[C]` whose comment fails keeps the reaction it already added. ([#1206](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1206); issue [#1202](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1202))
- **all workflows:** On macOS, the health check that ends every workflow now reports a defect whose issue was closed as completed as a regression when it comes back: it checked the issue with `timeout 10 gh issue view`, and stock macOS has no `timeout`, so the check always failed and counted as handled. The health check now computes a finding's fingerprint, looks it up in the seen-issue cache (`~/.skf/health-check-seen.json`) and records it there through one shared helper, `skf-health-check-seen.py`, instead of having the model hash the fingerprint with `sha1sum`, run the issue check and merge the file by hand: the helper limits `gh issue view` to 10 seconds itself, and the fingerprint no longer needs `sha1sum` or `shasum`. Recording a finding keeps every other fingerprint in the cache, never turns a `resolved` record back into one that suppresses unless an open issue now tracks the recurrence, holds a lock so parallel sessions keep each other's records, and renames a cache that does not parse to `health-check-seen.json.corrupt-<UTC time>` instead of discarding it. When the helper is missing, the findings are saved to the local queue with the fingerprint `N/A`. ([#1206](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1206); issue [#1122](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1122))
- **all workflows, skf-forger:** In a project with SKF alone, where BMAD Method's customization script is missing, a workflow or Ferris with no override file for it (`_bmad/custom/<skill>.toml` or `_bmad/custom/<skill>.user.toml`) no longer warns `customization_resolver_unavailable: not found`. SKF's customization helper, `skf-resolve-customization.py`, now reads the bundled `customize.toml` itself in that case, so the warning is gone from the screen, from the `warnings` of the result envelope and result file, and from Campaign's decision log. The run uses the same bundled values as before, and the helper now resolves their `persistent_facts` as it does when BMAD Method's script runs: a `**` never enters a hidden folder or a folder reached through a link, so a `project-context.md` found only that way is not loaded. When an override file exists, the run still warns `customization_resolver_unavailable: not found` and uses the bundled values, since only BMAD Method's script can merge that file. ([#1218](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1218); issue [#1184](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1184))
- **all workflows, skf-forger:** A `persistent_facts` entry that starts with `!`, such as `"!file:{project-root}/**/project-context.md"` in a team or personal override, is now applied by SKF's customization helper (`skf-resolve-customization.py`) instead of by the model following a sentence in each workflow: every workflow and Ferris now run the helper with `--facts`, which removes each `!` entry with every earlier entry it names and turns each `file:` glob into one entry per matching file before the workflow reads the list. The helper's `**` never enters a hidden folder or a folder reached through a link, so a link back up the tree cannot make it loop, and it never loads a `project-context.md` from the source clones a halted run keeps under `_bmad-output/.skf-run/`; Campaign's kickoff used to follow a linked folder, so a `project-context.md` it reached only through one is no longer loaded. Each file is listed once, and an entry the helper cannot resolve, such as a `file:` path that names no file, stays as written with a `persistent_facts:` line on stderr instead of failing the resolve. In a project with SKF alone and no override file for the workflow, the helper resolves the bundled list itself. In any other case where BMAD core's resolver cannot run, the workflow reads the bundled list as written and loads each file its glob matches itself, again none under `_bmad-output/.skf-run/`. Campaign's kickoff script loads Campaign's own facts into each skill's kickoff with the same code, and when the resolver is missing or fails, Campaign now passes `--facts-toml` with the bundled `customize.toml` to the kickoff script, which reads the list itself instead of the model copying it into a JSON file. ([#1207](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1207); issue [#1106](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1106))
- **skf-analyze-source:** Analyze Source's step-by-step brief step now checks its briefs' names and sources with one `skf-validate-brief-schema.py batch` call: a name another brief of the run or an existing skill already has, and a `source_repo` that is neither an existing folder nor a project path whose scan root exists. It no longer checks the forge tier, a check that could stop a correct headless run with exit `4` (`write-failed`) when `tier_override` set a tier other than the one in `forge-tier.yaml`, and no longer checks the language, a check that named no list of languages. A Python package whose version is computed at build time now gets its version from `skf-extract-public-api.py --resolve-version`, and the brief preview names where that version came from (a version file or a release tag). The brief steps read the parts of the brief schema they use instead of loading all of it, and the recommendation step no longer loads it. ([#1211](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1211); issue [#1127](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1127))
- **skf-analyze-source:** A step-by-step Analyze Source run that resumes an unfinished report now continues in the run folder of the session before it, so its result keeps the decisions and warnings recorded before the resume, and that folder is deleted when the analysis ends. Before, every session made a new run folder, so a resumed run's `headless_decisions` and `warnings` held only what the last session recorded, and the earlier folder stayed behind in `_bmad-output/.skf-run/`. When the earlier folder is gone, or the report names none (a report an older SKF wrote), the run goes on in its new folder and its result carries a `resumed-without-run-folder` warning. The brief step now fetches a gone scan root again for each project path its briefs come from, before it checks their sources and reads the path's manifests, and the resume announces its next step in one line. ([#1211](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1211); issue [#1124](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1124))
- **skf-analyze-source:** When `AN[auto]` splits a monorepo into one brief per package, `skf-shape-detect.py` now classifies each package from its own manifest and file list (its new `--member` option), so each package's shape and scope type come from the script instead of the model's reading. A package with no source file in a language `skf-detect-language.py` reads (so also one whose code is all `.vue`, `.svelte` or C files) is left out by that count, and the run's warnings name it. A published root package with code of its own beside its workspace, such as a Cargo root `[package]`, is one of the split's packages too, its scope leaving the other packages out. A package the script cannot classify (a `setup.py` package with source files, for example) gets a `full-library` brief. When the script fails on a package whose files git tracks, the run stops with exit code `3` (`resolution-failure`) and names the package. Shape detection also prints `scope_type`, the scope type its shape maps to, and `source_file_count`, the number of source files in the file list it was given. ([#1211](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1211); issue [#1128](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1128))
- **skf-analyze-source:** The step-by-step Analyze Source chain now takes each unit's export record, scope globs and component-library evidence from SKF's helpers instead of working them out by hand. Java, Kotlin and Swift units are counted by the parser over every source file of the unit, its tests left out (`strategy_used: "parser"`, `confidence: "T1"`), where before their exports were read by eye. Each unit's export record is written by a script from the extractor's output, so the model no longer copies the extractor's JSON into it, and a subagent is launched only for a unit that has something left to read (an extraction gap, a file the parser could not fully read, or a unit read by eye) or when the ccc search runs. The recommendation card and each brief carry the `scope.include` and `scope.exclude` globs that `skf-detect-language.py scope-patterns` computes for the unit (for a composite, the union of its constituents'), in place of suggested includes and excludes inferred by hand. Component libraries are classified from the demo-file count and the scored registry candidates of `skf-detect-registry.py`. ([#1211](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1211); issue [#1125](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1125))
- **skf-analyze-source:** The step-by-step Analyze Source chain now keeps its units in `analyze-source-units-<project>.json` beside the report. A script writes that file from the helpers' output (each boundary's disqualification record, its derived name, and its language and scope globs) and the model's judgments (boundary type, scope type, confidence, status and the signals behind them), and prints the report's unit tables from it. The export and import mapping reads its units from that file, and builds each project path's import-graph input with `skf-count-imports.py units-from` instead of a units list retyped from the report. The report's manifest and service configuration catalogs and its import matrix are printed by the helpers too (`skf-scan-manifests.py scan --format markdown`, `skf-count-imports.py summary --format markdown`). A report an older SKF left after unit identification, export mapping or recommendation resumes at unit identification, which writes the file and the scope patterns the recommendation and brief steps read, and the steps after it run again. ([#1211](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1211); issue [#1126](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1126))
- **skf-analyze-source, skf-create-skill, skf-create-stack-skill, skf-refine-architecture, skf-rename-skill, skf-verify-stack, skf-quick-skill:** A headless Analyze Source, Create Skill (one brief, not `--batch`), Stack Skill, Refine Architecture, Rename Skill or Verify Stack run now ends on its result line: the run hands its `SKF_*_RESULT_JSON` line to the shared health check, which displays it after everything else, so `claude -p` prints the envelope as the final message instead of the health check's closing `Workflow complete.` line. A headless Verify Stack run also drops its closing "Feasibility report saved to" message, and displays the line after `health-check unavailable at <path>` when its health check cannot be loaded. A headless Rename Skill `--dry-run` now displays its line after it deletes its run folder, so it ends on that line too. Interactive runs are unchanged, and a halt still ends on its own line. A Create Skill or Quick Skill `--batch` run now clears any result line an earlier workflow of the session bound before its one health check, so the batch never ends on that line. ([#1206](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1206); issue [#1113](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1113))
- **skf-audit-skill:** A CLEAN drift report now says in its Workflow Recommendation that the skill is ready for `[EX] Export Skill` unless upstream has moved, and the summary Audit Skill shows at the end of a run closes with each recommendation the report wrote, instead of working one out again from the drift score. ([#1210](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1210); issue [#1133](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1133))
- **skf-audit-skill:** An Audit Skill run on a skill updated since its last export, where the export manifest still names the older version and the `active` link names the new one, now audits the link's version and goes on with one Info note, as Test Skill and Export Skill do. The note names both versions, `[EX] Export Skill` to reconcile the manifest, and the `skill_path` that audits the manifest's version instead. The run no longer stops on the manifest-vs-symlink question there, and a headless run records no `init.manifest-lags-link` decision. The question, with its `[N]`, `[M]` and `[X]` choices and its decision record, now comes only when the link's version has no provenance map and the manifest's version has one. ([#1210](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1210); issue [#1132](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1132))
- **skf-audit-skill:** A Deep-tier drift report's Semantic Drift section now shows a table only for each category that has findings, filled from the rows the semantic diff saves, the Before and After columns of a changed convention and the dependency columns of a dependency shift included, and it has no New Patterns table any more. The Documentation Drift, Constituent Freshness and Provenance sections are now printed from the files the run saved, so a `|` in a documentation URL, a fetch failure's reason or a path no longer breaks a table, and the Documentation Drift table's Detected At column shows the run's timestamp. The Workflow Recommendation now recommends `[US] Update Skill` whenever the run's `next_workflow` is `update-skill`, a run whose upstream moved included, and then names `--target-ref` with the ref upstream moved to; its line calling minor drift optional now shows only when no update is recommended. The run's result is now built from the drift report's frontmatter and the saved classification: when the frontmatter is not valid YAML, names no `skill_name`, or records `upstream_moved: true` with no `upstream_ref`, and one fix does not settle it, the run stops with exit code 4 (`write-failed`). ([#1210](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1210); issue [#1130](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1130))
- **skf-audit-skill:** A changed signature now gets the same category and severity on every run of the same diff, because Severity Classify settles it from the changed fields. A change of spacing only grades LOW, a removed or retyped parameter or a changed return type CRITICAL, a new required parameter or a changed default HIGH and a new optional parameter MEDIUM; only a change no field settles, such as a changed kind, reordered parameters, a parameter renamed where no caller passes it by name or a signature it cannot read, is left to judgment. That judgment, and a removed and an added export of one ambiguous name judged to be one move, are now flags on the command that writes the findings (`--set-category`, `--pair-move`), never hand edits of `findings.json`, and the command's summary line lists, by index, each finding left to judge. The relocation check lists the files that may hold a removed export in one helper call (`relocation-candidates`) instead of a search per name and a candidates file written by hand. The snapshot build now records a module or package entry the recipe runner leaves out as an export itself, where before a by-eye reader had to turn its file path into a dotted name. ([#1210](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1210); issue [#1131](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1131))
- **skf-audit-skill:** A `tier_override` that names none of Quick, Forge, Forge+ and Deep, given as Audit Skill's input or in `preferences.yaml`, is now ignored with a `warn:` line and a `tier_override_ignored` entry in the result envelope's `warnings`, which names the value and where it came from; the preferences override, else the detected tier, applies instead. A valid input override still wins over the preferences one. `skf-forge-tier-rw.py effective` takes the input's value as `--tier-override` and reports it in `invocation_override` and `invocation_override_rejected`. ([#1210](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1210); issue [#1132](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1132))
- **skf-brief-skill:** The summary an `[auto]` Brief Skill run shows, as the `forge-auto` pipeline runs it, no longer shows a `Pipeline: forge-auto (<tier> tier)` line, which repeated the `Forge Tier` line above it; the `SKF_BRIEF_RESULT_JSON` envelope is unchanged. The tier glosses at the start of an interactive run now read as the brief review's do, such as "text-only extraction; AST and semantic discovery off" for `Quick`. The brief review no longer adds a note that the scripts and assets intent fires no scan for a `docs-only` or `public-api` scope. ([#1213](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1213); issue [#1135](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1135))
- **skf-brief-skill:** Brief Skill's analysis summary now shows the export count the scope-type recommendation uses, so a name two entry files export counts once in both instead of twice in the summary. For Java, Kotlin and Swift, whose public declarations are public in whatever file they sit, the analysis now parses every source file but the tests (`--all-sources`), as Analyze Source does, instead of the first five Java or Kotlin source files or a read by hand of a Swift package, and counts each file's declarations, so two packages' `Builder` classes count twice, the same number Analyze Source records for the unit. `skf-extract-public-api.py --mode quick` now writes `export_count`, `dependency_count` and `reexport_files` (the files the entry files pass names on from), and `skf-recommend-scope-type.py --extract-file` takes the file's `export_count`. The tier-A authoring surface of a monorepo package, and the files a headless `public-api` run includes, now come from the recipe runner's own `--print tier-a-candidates` and `--print public-files` output (`skf-extract-public-api.py --mode full -o <file> --print <set>`) instead of a filter typed into the shell. At Quick tier, or when the runner cannot run, the tier-A list is the analysis's `reexport_files` instead of a read of the package's barrel file by hand, and an empty list leaves `scope.tier_a_include` unset with a warning that says so. The analysis traces re-exports in Python, JavaScript and TypeScript only, so at Quick tier a package in another language now gets no tier-A list instead of one read by hand. ([#1213](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1213); issue [#1138](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1138))
- **skf-brief-skill:** An interactive Brief Skill run asks fewer questions. A target you name when you start it, such as `@Ferris BS https://github.com/colinhacks/zod`, skips the target prompt, and a `skill-brief.yaml` path named there starts the review of that brief. The offer to resume an in-progress draft now comes right after the target, before any other question. The version, supplemental documentation URLs, source authority and skill name are no longer asked one at a time: the summary shown before the analysis marks each value you did not give with `(default)` (the authority comes from your GitHub login, as in a headless run), and you change any of them there. A first brief shows one example description beside the proposed one instead of asking whether to show examples first. Scope definition shows the scope type's defaults and what it detected in one message and no longer asks whether the scope looks right, so the brief review is the one scope confirmation: it shows the scripts and assets intent as `detect (default)`, and when no version was detected it marks the 1.0.0 version `(default)` and, for a GitHub repository, notes that Create Skill at Forge tier or above will look for tag `1.0.0` or `v1.0.0`. Headless and `[auto]` runs read, write and halt as before. ([#1213](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1213); issue [#1136](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1136))
- **skf-brief-skill:** The Brief Skill review menu, shown before the brief is written, no longer offers `[A] Advanced Elicitation` or `[P] Party Mode`, whose results never reached the brief. It now reads `[R] Revise Scope`, `[C] Approve and Write` and `[X] Cancel and exit`, and you still change any field by saying what to change. Analyze Source's recommendation menu still offers both. ([#1213](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1213); issue [#1137](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1137))
- **skf-brief-skill, skf-verify-stack, skf-refine-architecture, skf-export-skill, skf-drop-skill, skf-rename-skill, skf-quick-skill, skf-test-skill, skf-campaign, skf-analyze-source, skf-create-skill:** The summary a workflow shows just before its closing health check no longer says the workflow is complete, so the health check's `Workflow complete.` is the only completion line a run prints: a summary that read as the end made agents stop there and skip the health check. Brief Skill and Verify Stack drop their closing "complete" line, Test Skill drops its closing **Test report finalized.** line, Refine Architecture drops its closing message (its summary already shows the saved path, and the re-run hint moves into its next steps) and opens with **Refine Architecture: Refined Document Ready**, and Export Skill, Drop Skill, Rename Skill, Quick Skill, Test Skill and Campaign open with a summary title (**Export summary** in place of **Export Complete**). Export Skill's dry-run note is headed **Dry Run: Nothing Written**, Campaign's note when its report fails reads **The campaign report could not be generated** in place of **Campaign finished, but the report could not be generated**, Analyze Source's message when no unit was confirmed no longer says the analysis is complete, and the line Create Skill shows after a `--batch` run's `batch_summary` event opens with `Batch summary:` in place of `Batch complete:`. ([#1206](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1206); issue [#1115](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1115))
- **skf-campaign:** Campaign Setup now looks for the architecture document when none is given, in an interactive run and a headless one: `docs/architecture.md`, then `_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/architecture.md`. The draft it shows names the document it found, or says none was found, so Verification and Refinement will be skipped, and the path it found is saved in the state. The Capstone now passes a found document to `skf-create-stack-skill` as well, as it did one you gave, so the stack skill maps the integrations between the skills and orders its layers from it; a recorded document whose file is gone is left out, where Create Stack Skill used to stop on it. Verification and Refinement no longer stop mid-run to ask for a missing architecture document: when the state holds none they look in the same two places, and with none they skip themselves and log it as an `event` in every run, where an interactive run used to ask and saved nothing when you declined. ([#1214](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1214); issue [#1143](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1143))
- **skf-campaign:** Campaign Setup now writes into `campaign-brief.yaml` only the quality gate values set by the brief the campaign was seeded from, and keeps the whole gate in `_campaign-state.yaml`. It used to write the whole settled gate, the customize.toml values included (and the brief template held 90 and 80), so a campaign seeded again from that brief kept the old values and a later `quality_gate_soft_target` or `quality_gate_soft_fallback` override did nothing. Setup logs each value the seeding brief set as an `event` in the decision log, `campaign-state.py init` returns them as `gate_from_brief`, and `campaign-quality-gate.py check` lists their keys as `from_brief`. A brief an earlier version wrote still holds all three values, and each still wins over customize.toml: remove from its `quality_gate` the values meant to come from customize.toml. ([#1214](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1214); issue [#1142](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1142))
- **skf-campaign:** `campaign resume` no longer warns "No backup file found" when there is no `_campaign-state.yaml.bak`, which is the normal state after Setup. It still warns when the backup exists but fails validation, and then goes on with the primary state. ([#1214](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1214); issue [#1140](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1140))
- **skf-campaign:** `campaign status` now names the exits it takes. With no `_campaign-state.yaml` it says no campaign has started and stops with exit code `2` (`invalid-input`). A state that fails validation stops it with exit code `3` (`invalid-state`), as every state load does, and when `_campaign-state.yaml.bak` exists it points to `campaign resume`, which can recover the state from that backup. Each of these stops at phase `status`. It used to name only exit code `0`, or `9` for a state it could not recover, against the rule that a state failing validation stops with `3`, and said nothing of a missing state. ([#1214](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1214); issue [#1142](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1142))
- **skf-campaign:** Campaign's Strategy stage now shows the plan that `campaign-deps.py --render` prints from the state: each skill in execution order with its tier, its pin (or `latest`) and what it depends on, then the quality gate and the tier counts. The separate dependency map is gone, since each row names its dependencies. When the plan has a cycle, `campaign-deps.py --compute` now lists each dependency between the skills it could not order (`cycle_edges`), and Strategy names those edges when it stops with exit code 4. ([#1214](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1214); issue [#1141](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1141))
- **skf-campaign, skf-create-skill:** Campaign's skill loop now records a Tier A skill's folder (`skill_path`) as soon as Create Skill finishes, before Test Skill runs, so a skill whose test fails keeps its path in the state. Create Skill's doc-rot step now writes the corrections it kept to `doc-rot-corrections.json` in its staging folder, and Campaign records them in the skill's `workarounds_applied` from that file with `campaign-state.py append-workarounds --doc-rot-file`, right after Create Skill, instead of copying them from the conversation after the test. A file it cannot read stops nothing: Campaign logs it as an `event` and goes on to Test Skill. A directive problem (an override line the gate script cannot read, or a Skip List or Quality Overrides name that is no campaign skill) now reaches the decision log as one `Directive:` line, logged once per campaign however many skills report it (Export reports the same line), through the new `campaign-state.py log --once`, which counts only the lines stamped since the campaign started, so a campaign seeded again over the same log logs the line again. ([#1214](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1214); issue [#1141](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1141))
- **skf-create-skill:** An interactive `--batch` run of Create Skill no longer stops at the extraction review for every brief. A brief whose extraction showed neither the zero-export nor the head-cap warning goes on by itself, and the run records that decision as gate `review-gate`, so it reaches the brief's `headless_decisions` and the evidence report's Auto-Decisions table. A brief with either warning still stops and offers `[R] Refine the brief`, and a run without `--batch` still stops at the review. ([#1222](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1222); issue [#1149](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1149))
- **skf-create-skill:** Create Skill loads less on each run: the remote-source steps, the Tessl Review collect steps and the component-library, reference-app and whole-language assembly rules now load only on the runs that need them, and every halt, gate, report line and generated file stays as it was. ([#1222](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1222); issue [#1147](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1147))
- **skf-create-skill:** Create Skill's helpers now compute what its steps used to work out by hand. Step 5a records `doc_sources` in the staged `metadata.json` with one `skf-detect-docs.py record-sources` call, which keeps each detected page's hash, adds the README entry and leaves every other field as it was. Step 6 fixes drifted `stats` and `confidence_distribution` values and records `validation_status` through `skf-render-metadata-stats.py --check --fix --validation-status`, checks the frontmatter with `skf-validate-frontmatter.py` when skill-check is unavailable, and step 5 sanitizes the description with `skf-description-guard.py sanitize`. The report's headline confidence is the helper's `primary_confidence` (the largest bin, the weaker label on a tie). Registry entries and recorded auto-decisions get their `created_at`, `indexed_at` and `timestamp` from the helpers' clock, as the full UTC time to the second (for example `2026-11-14T10:00:00+00:00`) where a run used to write the date, and the cache and embed checks read `skf-forge-tier-rw.py read --fresh-within-hours`, so a collection's age is measured, not guessed. The doc-rot scan no longer scans `issues.md` and `targeted-issues.md` (it lists them in `scanned_skipped`), so changelog and release-note candidates the cap used to drop for issue lines are kept. The ccc index check reads `skf-merge-ccc-exclusions.py --check-index`, which calls an index verified when the source language has at least 10 chunks, or at least 5% of a smaller index, so some runs report a different index verdict than before. ([#1222](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1222); issue [#1145](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1145))
- **skf-create-skill:** Create Skill now counts co-imports and component stats with its helpers instead of by hand, so the numbers at Gate 2, in SKILL.md and in `metadata.json` can differ from before and stay the same from run to run. At Forge tier and above, for a library other than a component library, step 3 pipes `skf-scan-manifests.py scan` into `skf-count-imports.py count --threshold 2`, which matches imports on module boundaries (`react-dom` no longer counts as `react`) and leaves out the files the brief's `scope.exclude` names, and `co_imports` lists each dependency imported by 2 or more files with its file count; when the count cannot run, `co_imports` is empty and a warning says why. For a component library, the new `skf-detect-registry.py components` sorts the exports into Props contracts, components, shared types and shared exports, links each Props contract to its component (`naming-convention`, `co-location`, `generic-param` or `none`), maps the registry entries to the catalog with their variants, files and canonical contract, and counts the `component_stats` that `metadata.json` records. Only the variant props notes, a missing category and the integration point suggestions are still the model's. ([#1222](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1222); issue [#1146](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1146))
- **skf-create-skill:** Create Skill's closing report no longer prints the skill's context snippet with an instruction to paste it into `CLAUDE.md`. It now ends by pointing at `@Ferris EX` (Export Skill), after `@Ferris TS` (Test Skill) if you want the quality gate. Export Skill writes the managed section of `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md` or `.cursorrules`, so a later export no longer lists a pasted skill twice, and a drop or rename no longer leaves a pasted line behind. If you pasted a snippet from an earlier report into one of those files, delete that line: `@Ferris EX` writes the skill's own line in the managed section. ([#1222](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1222); issue [#1149](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1149))
- **skf-create-skill:** Create Skill now checks that `python3` and `uv` are on your PATH as it starts, before it runs anything through `uv`, and stops with `helper-missing` (exit code `3`) when either is missing, naming the tool and where to install it. Before, a run without them printed only a warning, then failed when it checked the brief, with no result line and no typed exit code. When only `uv` is missing, the halt prints its `SKF_CREATE_SKILL_RESULT_JSON` line on stderr with phase `on-activation:runtime`, under `--batch` too; with no `python3` it shows the message alone. Nothing is written in either case. ([#1222](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1222); issue [#1149](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1149))
- **skf-create-stack-skill:** A Deep-tier Stack Skill run now writes the deprecation, migration and version findings it reads from a library's QMD temporal collection into that library's reference file, under a new `## Migration & Deprecation` section, each finding with its T2-past or T2-future label and its `[QMD:...]` citation, and the library's summary in `SKILL.md` (or `references/stack-catalog.md`) gains a `**Deprecations:**` line that counts its T2-future findings; before, the run read those findings and wrote none of them. A headless compose run, the Campaign capstone's included, now renames each provenance entry whose export name the package does not write to the identifier it does write, as an interactive run already did, instead of dropping it, so Test Skill still counts it toward Export Coverage. Each `## Conventions` bullet and each summary's Usage pattern line now cites what shows it: the file and line in code mode (`(src/app.ts:12)`, several comma-separated), the constituent skill in compose mode (`[from skill: react]`). A convention no extraction shows is left out, and `skf-validate-output.py --skill-type stack` reports a Conventions bullet with no citation as a `low` issue, which the validation step lists as a warning, so a house-style copy of the stack template keeps each bullet's citation. ([#1215](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1215); issue [#1155](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1155))
- **skf-drop-skill:** Drop Skill's skill list, its version details and its final report now state the facts they show instead of following a fixed layout, so their headings, column names and line order can differ from one run to the next. Each still shows what it showed before: the list marks the active version with `*`, versions only on disk and the skills it does not offer; the report keeps each `rm -rf` fix for a folder it could not delete, the steps that reverse a deprecate, and the manual fix for each failed check. The version details of a skill with no manifest entry no longer carry the note that only a purge applies; the run still says so when it forces the purge. When the sizing helper fails after a purge, the report now shows the disk space freed as `unknown`. ([#1216](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1216); issue [#1159](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1159))
- **skf-drop-skill, skf-rename-skill:** A version purge now repairs the `active` link only when it names the version it deleted: a link that names another version, such as a newer one you have not exported yet, stays as it is, and a link it repairs points at the version the export manifest lists as active, else the newest one the manifest does not list as deprecated, else it is removed. The drop report lists only the versions in the export manifest, so a stray folder in the skill folder no longer shows as a version. The context-file rebuild, the headless purge guard and the final-state checks now run through SKF's helpers, so each context file keeps the skill root of its own IDE, and Rename Skill rebuilds each context file with its own skill root too, where it used to pass one that nothing set. ([#1216](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1216); issue [#1158](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1158))
- **skf-export-skill:** Export Skill's context file preview now comes from the new `diff` action of `skf-rebuild-managed-sections.py`, where the model used to compare the old managed section with the new one by eye. For each target file it shows the `[SKF Skills]` header line before and after, each skill row added, removed or changed (with its old and new version, and its old and new `root:` path when that moved), and a unified diff of the section, or `No change to the section.` when the section stays the same. `diff` takes the context file and the staged section in `--content-file`, writes nothing, and prints `case`, `header`, `rows` and `unified` as JSON. A preview the helper cannot build stops the run with exit `4` (`context-rebuild-failed`) before any file is written. ([#1209](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1209); issue [#1165](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1165))
- **skf-export-skill:** Export Skill's first confirmation now shows what the run will publish before you answer: one table with a row per skill that names its version (`v3.23.8`, `migrated from the flat layout` when the run just moved a flat skill, or `flat layout, would migrate` in a dry run) and its package status (`READY` or `WARNINGS`), with a warnings line under the table for each `WARNINGS` skill, then the export settings once and one question. It used to show neither, and reported the package status only after you had confirmed. A batch and a single skill now share that one table. The export gate reads the fields the table shows from `metadata.json` itself and prints them as a `package` object, and it counts every file under `references/`, as the token report does, where the count used to take only `.md` files. The separate Package stage is gone, so the stages are now numbered 1 to 6, and the context-file confirmation shows one preview per target file and asks once, naming each file with its case (create, append or regenerate). ([#1209](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1209); issue [#1162](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1162))
- **skf-export-skill:** With `passive_context: false` in your preferences, Export Skill no longer asks where the managed section should point your skills, and a headless run records no `load-skill.snippet-root-layout` or `load-skill.snippet-root-probe` decision: such a run writes no snippet and no managed-section row, so it has no `root:` path to choose. It used to ask the layout or mismatch question all the same, and answering [S] or (a) stopped an export that would never have written the root. Export now reads `passive_context` once, as it starts. ([#1209](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1209); issue [#1163](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1163))
- **skf-forger:** A pipeline chain now takes each workflow's inputs from its journal instead of working them out from the contract tables. `pipeline-journal.py start`, `step` and `reopen` print a `next` entry, the workflow to run next with its `skill`, `description` and resolved `inputs`: its bracket target, the value an earlier step handed on, or the alias arguments for the first workflow, with `pin`, `threshold`, `auto` and `flags`. Several briefs that Analyze Source hands straight to Create Skill reach it as one `--batch` run, and Refine Architecture takes the document Verify Stack was given. Each `parse-pipeline.py` plan entry also names its `skill` and `description`, and Ferris no longer loads `pipeline-contracts.md` for every chain and resume. The journal file and the pipeline result keep their shape. ([#1212](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1212); issue [#1167](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1167))
- **skf-forger:** When you pick a workflow after another one already ran in the same session, Ferris now recommends a fresh session and gives this advice once per session, where he used to offer a fresh session and an in-place chain as equal options, naming neither one's trade, on every such pick. The command he gives you to paste carries the rest of the chain, such as `@Ferris TS[cocoindex] EX`, and he says what each option trades: a fresh session starts from a clean context, where one workflow pasted alone keeps its own questions and a chain takes its workflows' default answers, while the rest of the chain run now as a pipeline, offered when more steps follow your pick, keeps this session's context and takes the default answers. He runs your pick in place, with its own questions, only when you ask, and every later pick in that session runs in place without the advice. ([#1212](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1212); issue [#1171](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1171))
- **skf-forger:** `maintain` no longer re-tests and re-exports a skill that is already current. When Audit Skill finds no drift and the source did not move, and the skill's active version passed its test and is the exported one, with no drift on record, and neither `forge-tier.yaml` nor `preferences.yaml` (whose `tier_override` sets the tier a test runs at) has changed since that test, the chain passes over Update Skill, Test Skill and Export Skill and says why; run `@Ferris TS <name>` to test it again. `pipeline-gate.py` takes `--forge-data-folder`, `--skills-output-folder`, `--sidecar` and `--skill` for this, and its `skip` names `US TS EX` with the reason `current`. `pipeline-journal.py step` takes the three folders and records each step a gate passes over, matching the skip's codes to the steps after the audit in their order, and only steps for the audited skill, so a chain such as `AS[x] US SS` or `AS[x] US TS[y] EX[y]` passes over US alone. The same rule now holds for every skip, so a CLEAN audit no longer passes over an update whose bracket names another skill: `AS[x] US[y] TS EX` runs `US[y]`. `skipped` is now a list, empty when the gate passed over nothing. ([#1212](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1212); issue [#1170](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1170))
- **skf-forger:** A pipeline chain now records each step from the envelope line its workflow printed, in one `pipeline-journal.py step --envelope` call, instead of Ferris running the gate and copying each status, handoff value and output path out of the envelope by hand. For Analyze Source, Test Skill, Audit Skill and Verify Stack the call runs `pipeline-gate.py`'s rules with the next code in the plan and AN's plan `min`; for every other workflow it reads the envelope's `status`, and after a Create Skill `--batch` run the line of every brief: the step completes only when every brief compiled, else it stops with the first failed brief's reason, and it hands each brief's skill on. An Export Skill `dry-run` stops the chain with `dry-run`, where it used to go on; Update Skill's `no-changes`, `detect-only` and `dry-run` go on. In a chain such as `VS[docs/arch.md] RA SS TS EX`, Create Stack Skill now composes from the document Refine Architecture refined, and Test Skill and Export Skill take the stack skill it wrote, where they used to start with no skill. A step that completes without the value it hands on stops with `handoff-missing` and leaves no resume, since running it again names no value either: start the steps left as a new chain, with that value in the first one's bracket, such as `TS[<skill>] EX`. `step` prints the gate's decision as `gate`, and `step --reason -` and `finish --halt-reason -` read the reason on stdin from a quoted heredoc, so a reason no longer needs its quotes replaced. The journal file and the pipeline result keep their shape, and `step --gate`, `--status`, `--set` and `--output` still work. ([#1212](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1212); issue [#1168](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1168))
- **skf-forger:** Ferris now says why a stopped chain stopped. After an error halt the greeting names the step's code and halt reason beside the recommended route, and a chain cut off mid-step comes as a question instead of a recommendation, with the time its journal was last written, since it may still be running in another session. `pipeline-journal.py resume` prints that journal's `started_at` and `updated_at`, and dropping the offer of a chain cut off mid-step asks once first. ([#1212](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1212); issue [#1169](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1169))
- **skf-forger:** A chain's missing-brief and missing-audit warnings now read the forge state on disk instead of the order of its codes alone, so Ferris no longer asks you to confirm a chain whose skill already has what the warning names. `CS[cocoindex] TS EX` raises no `cs-without-brief` when `cocoindex/skill-brief.yaml` is in the forge data folder, and `US[cocoindex] TS EX` no `us-without-audit` when the active version of cocoindex has an audit on record. `parse-pipeline.py` takes the folders as `--forge-data-folder` and `--skills-output-folder`; without them each warning reads the order of the codes, as before. ([#1212](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1212); issue [#1170](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1170))
- **skf-quick-skill:** A Quick Skill `--batch` file with a line whose words after the target are not a valid `language=<lang>` or `scope=<path>` modifier (a misspelled key such as `lang=javascript`, an empty value, a modifier given twice) is now refused before any target runs, with exit code `2` (`input-invalid`) and a message that names each such line, the first five with their fault, and gives the fix, instead of failing only when the batch reaches that line.
