A word that starts with `#` after a line's target now opens a comment that runs to the end of the line, so `lodash scope=src/ # the core` is valid. `skf-quick-batch.py parse` marks each such line with an `error`. ([#1223](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1223); issue [#1175](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1175))
- **skf-quick-skill:** Quick Skill now recognizes an input that names several packages or GitHub URLs, such as `lodash axios zod` or `lodash, axios, zod`: it says it compiles one target per run and points you at `--batch <file>`, instead of saying the input looks like a description. A headless run stops on such an input with exit code `3` (`resolution-failure`) and the reason "Quick Skill compiles one target per run." `skf-resolve-package.py parse-target` gains the `targets` key, which lists the targets of such an input and is null for any other. ([#1223](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1223); issue [#1175](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1175))
- **skf-refine-architecture:** When the architecture document names none of the generated skills, Refine Architecture no longer goes on in silence with every skill in scope. An interactive run now shows the scope confirmation with every skill in scope and asks you to check that the document is the one you meant, with the same choices: `C` keeps every skill, a `-<name>` takes a skill out, and `X` cancels with exit `6` (`user-cancelled`). A headless run still keeps every skill in scope and records the `scope_fallback_all_skills` warning, and now also records the scope decision that picked that default. ([#1219](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1219); issue [#1179](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1179))
- **skf-refine-architecture:** Refine Architecture now analyses only the skills in the document's scope. Once the scope is set, gap analysis reads the API surface of the in-scope skills only and judges only the pairs of two in-scope skills, so a run no longer lists out-of-scope compatible pairs: it names the out-of-scope skills once and points at `--scope-skills` to bring any that belong into scope. Improvement detection compares each in-scope skill's surface with what the document says it does in one pass, and no longer looks for improvements that pay off only with an out-of-scope skill. Issue detection sets a claim that names an out-of-scope skill aside unchecked, beside the [VS] verdicts that involve one, which both stay listed for awareness only. The refined document's Refinement Summary now counts the in-scope skills, the only ones the run read, as the skills it used. ([#1219](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1219); issue [#1177](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1177))
- **skf-setup:** A `/skf-setup` run under `--headless`, `-H`, `--quiet` or a Ferris pipeline no longer runs the workflow health check, whose findings it only queued where nothing read them. Setup now saves the `SKF_SETUP_RESULT_JSON` line in its run folder when it builds it, and its last command prints that saved line and removes the folder, so the line a pipeline reads is the one the emitter wrote. Run `/skf-setup` without these flags to get the health check. ([#1218](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1218); issue [#1183](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1183))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's split-body cross-check, at the Forge tier or above, now settles two more kinds of pair. When the source declares a name more than once and, on a pair that is not a method's, one form matches one or more of those declarations while the other matches none, the `split-body-mismatch` gap's Source and the Reference Consistency table's Contradicted Side name the side that matches none, and its remediation names that side to edit and the form to take, citing each matching declaration by file and line. Update Skill's `--from-test-report` run takes only that form: it adds no citation. A pair of a method's forms whose owner neither declares nor binds the method is now settled by the member of the first class in its method resolution order to declare or bind it, a base class in the source tree. Before, both pairs said no source settled them and had Update Skill copy the other side's form into the reference file, even over a reference form the source agrees with. The gap stays High and blocks as before. A pair still stays unsettled, with that copy, when the owner has no record in `surface.json`, when a method of that name is declared for the owner outside its class body (a Go receiver method, a function assigned to `prototype`), when the first class in that order to declare the method is another package's, when the method is overloaded (in Java, Kotlin, C# and Swift, by a base too), or, for a name declared more than once, when the surface was built without the runner's extraction (`otherDeclarations` `null`). ([#1101](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1101); issue [#1062](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1062))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's coherence check now loads only the instructions of its mode: the naive checks live in `references/coherence-naive.md` and the contextual ones in `references/coherence-contextual.md`, and `coherence-check.md` routes to one of them, then writes and records the Coherence Analysis section as before. A stack skill's integration points, its code or compose mode and each entry's wiring evidence now come from the new `skf-scan-skill-md-structure.py integration-scan`, which reads the stack template's Cross-Cutting Patterns and Library Pair Integrations entries and leaves out the Hub Library Connections list, so a stack whose integration patterns were miscounted by hand can get a different coherence score. Only a library pair needs wiring evidence now: Create Stack Skill writes a cross-cutting pattern with no `file:line` citation or `[from skill: ...]` line, so the check no longer marks every one incomplete. `aggregate-coherence.py` refuses (exit 2) an `integration.json` whose `incomplete_patterns` do not number `patterns_documented - patterns_complete` or lack a `pattern`, an `issue` or a line, and copies them into `coherence.json` as `incompletePatterns`. `gap-ledger.py` records each incomplete integration pattern from there (`--from coherence`) and each split-body mismatch from the inventory and a settlements file (the new `--from split-body --settlements`), with fixed titles and Sources, where the model used to type both into the ledger. The naive branch's findings JSON, which nothing read, is gone. ([#1217](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1217); issue [#1187](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1187))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's discovery check now says how each subagent that picks a skill for a test prompt is started without file or shell tools: on Claude Code, with an agent type that has none of them (`web-fetch` where it is listed), never the default `general-purpose` type, which has every tool, and on a host whose spawn call or agent definition sets a subagent's tools, with none of them. Before, a run could start these subagents with every tool, and one that read the run lock `.test-skill.lock` or the in-progress report, which both name the skill under test, could pass the discovery check for a description whose triggers misroute, so the report lacked the Medium or High `discovery` gap it should have shown. Where no such subagent can be started, the check is now skipped with `subagents unavailable, routing test requires isolated context` and an Info `discovery` gap, where a run used to report a discovery PASS, WARN or FAIL. On Claude Code that is the usual result, though the run starts other subagents, since most sessions list no agent type without file or shell tools: to keep the discovery check, define one once in `.claude/agents/` with `name`, `description` and `tools: WebFetch` in its frontmatter, as the gap's remediation says. A discovery gap still blocks nothing and changes no score or verdict. ([#1100](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1100); issue [#1079](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1079))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's external validators step now reads skill-check's score, its error and warning counts, the description check and the external-validator gaps from the saved skill-check and Tessl Review results with scripts, so the same results give the same score, report and Gap Report on every run. The step saves both results in the run folder (`skill-check.json`, `tessl.json`), and `combine-external-scores.py` writes what the later steps read to `external.json`: skill-check's score for the tested skill by the rule Quick Skill uses (the top-level `qualityScore` of an older skill-check build included), the counts, the diagnostics, whether skill-check reported a description rule, and the Tessl Review findings. In the Gap Report, each skill-check gap is now titled `skill-check: <rule id>`, names its file relative to the skill folder as its Source (`SKILL.md:12`, say), and takes skill-check's own suggestion as its remediation when skill-check gives one; a Tessl Review description suggestion's gap says to edit the SKILL.md frontmatter description, and the brief too when the skill has one. The report step's description hints now follow the same check. When `combine-external-scores.py` fails twice, the run stops with `helper-failed` at phase `external-validators:score`. ([#1205](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1205); issue [#1120](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1120))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's signature comparison and fallback per-file scan now hand their subagents files in batches, one judge a batch, where they dispatched one per file: `score-signatures.py plan` writes `batches[]` (at most 10 files and 25 checks each, a file with more checks alone) and its summary their number, and the fallback scan saves its batches to `fallback-batches.json`. Each judge returns one JSON array, saved one file per batch in batch order. A response that leaves out a file its batch was given is refused: `score` with `--plan`, and `surface` with the new `--batches`, exit 2 naming the batch, the response file given at its position and the file, and that batch's judge is dispatched again, where the file's checks used to count as matching or its exports dropped out of the surface. A batch with no response file, or a response file past the last batch, is refused the same way. ([#1217](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1217); issue [#1188](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1188))
- **skf-test-skill:** `score-signatures.py score`, `reconcile-coverage.py`, `verify-declared-numerator.py`, `aggregate-coherence.py` and `combine-external-scores.py` now print only a summary when they are given `--output`, since Test Skill reads each result from the file it writes in the run folder. `score`, `reconcile-coverage.py`, `verify-declared-numerator.py` and `aggregate-coherence.py` print each field of their result as the file holds it, with a list as its number of entries (the compared names, missing types, mismatches, gap records, warnings and open readings of `score`; the documented, missing and stale names, the warnings, the incomplete items and the open readings of the coverage reconciliation; the present and absent names of the numerator check; the invalid references of the coherence aggregate), and the path they wrote as `output`. `combine-external-scores.py` prints `externalScore`, `toolsUsed` and the path. An input a helper refuses, or a subagent result that breaks the schema, prints its error or its violations as before. They used to print the whole result as well, so every run put a second copy of the signature mismatches, the gap records and the coverage name lists into the agent's context. Without `--output` each still prints the whole result, as does `score` given `--gaps-output` alone, and no score, verdict or gap changes. ([#1097](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1097); issue [#1063](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1063))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's report records more of its counts by script. The Coverage Analysis section's `Denominator:` line, the provenance-map fold summary and the Denominator Candidates block of a stratified-scope or multi-entry skill now come from `reconcile-coverage.py render`, which takes `coverage-inputs.json` as `--coverage-inputs` for a stack's basis and a reference app's pattern-surface count (`load-coverage-inputs.py metadata` now keeps that count as `patternSurfacesDocumented`). In contextual mode, the Coherence Analysis counts and the Reference Validation and Coherence Score tables come from `aggregate-coherence.py render`, and the Integration Pattern Completeness table now comes last, under them; in naive mode the Structural Findings rows the scans find come from `gap-ledger.py render --from structure`. The model writes only the rows it judged, and a coherence render that fails halts the run `helper-failed` at the new phase `coherence-check:render`. The Completeness Score's Result line now says `PASS_WITH_DRIFT` for a pass under a workspace drift override, as the result file does, and its Scoring Notes say why. Its Weight Distribution line says `contextual (redistributed)` when a contextual run's weights were redistributed, where it said `full`. The Denominator Candidates block names the clause it audits, where a multi-entry skill's said `stratified-scope`. ([#1217](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1217); issue [#1186](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1186))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill now renews its run lock just before each subagent starts (or, in an environment without subagents, before the main thread starts the work a subagent would have done), for 180 minutes, and the lock helper `skf-run-lock.py` keeps that window in the lock file, so a second run honours it. Nothing can renew the lock while one subagent runs, and the lock went stale 60 minutes after its last renewal whatever window the run asked for, so one subagent, such as the one that reads a large skill to list its exports, could run past the hour: a second run of the same skill version started then took the lock over, and the first run halted `another-run-active` with no result written. A second run now stops at the start with `another-run-active` while that subagent works, and the next renewal after it returns sets the window back to 60 minutes. A run cut off while a subagent runs now leaves a lock that blocks a new test of that skill version until 180 minutes after that renewal, not 60; the message names the lock file to delete when no run is active. Every lock record the helper writes, Update Skill's and Rename Skill's included, now carries a `stale_after_minutes` key, which an older helper ignores, and a refused `acquire` reports, in `stale_after_minutes` and `stale_at`, the window the holder stored when it is longer than the caller's own. ([#1100](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1100); issue [#1086](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1086))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill now takes its source access state and its access degradation notice from a script. Unless the run is docs-only, the new `load-coverage-inputs.py access` counts the provenance map's entries and `confidence` labels and the metadata exports, and writes the State (1 to 3, or null for the workflow to settle at State 4 or 5) and a `degradation` of `all-t1`, `mixed` or `low` to `access.json`, which the source access protocol and the Completeness Score's Access Degradation Notice read; a skill with no metadata.json leaves `--metadata` out and goes on as before. A metadata.json or provenance map that cannot be read now halts the run `helper-failed` at `coverage-check:access`. The notice follows a fixed rule where it said "all or most": at `provenance-map` every entry T1 is `all-t1`, none is `low` and any other map is `mixed`, so a map the model called mostly T1 can now read `mixed` and recommend a local clone for its other entries, each label written after its count and an entry with no label counted as `unlabeled`; every other access takes the `low` notice. States 2 and 3 no longer read the entry point remotely, since nothing scored what that read found. ([#1217](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1217); issue [#1188](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1188))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's `default_threshold` now ships empty, and a value a team or personal override sets outranks a pipeline's default, so it now reaches `forge` and `forge-quick` runs, where the per-pipeline table used to win; `forge-auto` and Campaign pass `--threshold` and keep their own. A run takes `--threshold`, else the override, else its pipeline's default, else 80. The report's `thresholdSource` reads `workflow override (N%)` for the override and `bundled default (80%)` when nothing set a threshold, where a standalone run read `workflow default (80%)`. A value above 80 never turns a PASS into a FAIL: the threshold fallback still accepts a run scoring 80% or more that no cap failed. ([#1217](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1217); issue [#1189](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1189))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's Reference Consistency section now names each split-body mismatch that Exports Cross-Checked does not count, and why, on a new `**Not Cross-Checked:**` line: its two places are in one file, a file of its pair is not one the inventory reads, or a file of its pair does not write it. `validate-inventory.py --skill-package` writes these mismatches into the inventory as `crossChecked.uncounted`, and its `warnings` name each one. Before, the section could show Exports Cross-Checked 0 beside Mismatches Found 1 and say nothing about it. The validator still never refuses an inventory for such a mismatch, and `crossChecked` gives no `uncounted` key when the count leaves none out. ([#1095](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1095); issue [#1067](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1067))
- **skf-update-skill:** When you start an interactive Update Skill run without naming a skill, it now asks only which skill to update, by number, name or folder path, or by name with `--from-test-report` to repair it from its test report, and points to `--dry-run` for a preview that writes nothing and to the invocation contract for the other flags. It no longer lists every flag, the headless-only `--allow-degraded` among them. Each flag still works as before when you pass it. ([#1220](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1220); issue [#1195](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1195))
- **skf-verify-stack:** Verify Stack's coverage step now hands the other technologies it finds in the architecture document's prose to the shared mentions helper (`--technologies`), which matches a name equal to a skill's name or alias once case, spaces, hyphens, dots and underscores are dropped, so `Tailwind CSS` covers a `tailwindcss` skill by script. The step judges by a common alias only the names the helper leaves unverified (`PostgreSQL` for a `postgres` skill), and a skill name found only inside a longer name is no match by itself (`React Native` is not a `react` skill). A skill matched either way that the document does not name directly still has its integration pairs checked. ([#1208](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1208); issue [#1199](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1199))
- **skf-verify-stack:** Verify Stack's report now lists each requirement recommendation once, under `### Prioritized Recommendations`, so its `## Recommendations` section holds as many recommendations as its recommendation count: the requirements section keeps its coverage table and the gap of each partly fulfilled requirement, and no longer repeats their recommendations. The final step shows the verdict, then that list in its order (about five of each kind, with how many more the report holds), then the suggested next workflow, instead of walking the findings twice. A Risky pair's recommendation names the bridge for that pair, one already in the stack or a named library, codec or adapter, and where the architecture document records it or must add it, or says no bridge could be named, and a Blocked pair's names the replacement or the bridge, in place of a stock sentence. The summary table shows a requirements count of 0 as 0, and `N/A (no PRD)` only when the requirements pass was skipped. The requirements step reads the PRD path from the report's `prdDoc`. ([#1208](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1208); issue [#1201](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1201))
- **skf-verify-stack:** Verify Stack's coverage, integrations, requirements and synthesize steps now write their part of the feasibility report through a new helper, `skf-report-update.py`, which edits only the frontmatter keys, table rows or section a call names, so a later step no longer rewrites what an earlier one wrote and no frontmatter count or rendered table row is copied by hand. The `## Evidence Sources` rows are rendered from the skill inventory (`skf-coverage-tally.py --kind evidence --render`), and a skill whose evidence tier is off the scale stops the run (exit `7`, `inventory-unreliable`, phase `synthesize:report`) instead of reaching the next run's delta. The report gains four subsections: `### Integration Details` below the canonical verdict table, `### Requirements Coverage` and `### Prioritized Recommendations` under `## Recommendations`, and `### Input Documents` below the Evidence Sources table. Synthesize now stops (exit `5`, `schema-violation`, phase `synthesize:rollup`) when the frontmatter's pair counts disagree with the canonical verdict table. A `report_template_path` copy with no table under `## Evidence Sources`, which synthesize fills, now stops step 1 (exit `5`, `schema-violation`, phase `init:report-template`) before any analysis runs, and text such a copy keeps under `## Executive Summary` or `## Coverage Analysis` is replaced by the step that writes that section. When the helper refuses a section or rows file the step wrote, the step fixes the file and runs the call again; when it refuses the report itself (a section, table or subsection the call names is missing or there twice), the run stops with exit `5` `schema-violation`, and only a write of the report that fails stops it with exit `4` `write-failed`. ([#1208](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1208); issue [#1198](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1198))
- **skf-verify-stack:** Verify Stack's first step now checks the skills folder and stops on fewer than two skills before it asks for or checks any document, in a headless run too, so a forge with too few skills no longer has you type paths first. A previous report it finds is now the Enter default of the prompt's previous-report line, offered once instead of a second time after the prompt, and `none` there, or `--previous-report none`, runs without a comparison. A PRD or previous-report path that is not found is asked for again once; a headless run goes on without it and lists `prd_not_found: <path>` or `previous_report_not_found: <path>` in the envelope's `warnings`. A PRD that was not found keeps its path in the report's `prdDoc`, and the requirements section says that PRD was not found instead of saying none was given. ([#1208](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1208); issue [#1200](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1200))
- **skf-verify-stack:** When the integration step cannot use a skill's API-surface summary (no reply, a reply that is not JSON, or a key missing or of the wrong type), Verify Stack now reads that skill's `SKILL.md` once more before it counts the read as failed. A skill it still cannot read no longer drops out of the run unseen: each of its integration pairs gets a `Risky` row with the rationale "API surface unreadable: re-run [VS]" and a recommendation, the envelope's `warnings` list `skill_summary_unreadable: <skill>` once, and the requirements section names the skill as not read. Those pairs used to have no row, so readers saw them as unrated. Now each counts as a `Risky` pair, though no compatibility check ran: the run's verdict is `CONDITIONALLY_FEASIBLE` at best, Refine Architecture raises a Major issue for each such pair, and Stack Skill annotates it `[VS: Risky]`, until a re-run reads the skill. Exit `7` (`inventory-unreliable`, phase `integrations:api-surfaces`), which a first malformed reply used to count toward, now counts a skill a subagent read only when its second read fails too, and its message no longer asks you to wait for the skills to stabilize: it says the reads failed, the skills themselves may be fine, and to re-run [VS]. ([#1208](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1208); issue [#1197](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1197))

### Fixed

- **all workflows:** Every workflow's SKILL.md but Create Stack Skill's said every bare path resolves from the skill root, while its stages hand off by a file name beside them (`nextStepFile: 'execute.md'`), so an agent that read the rule as written looked for the next stage at the skill root, where it is not. The rule now names, for each workflow, the frontmatter keys that point at a file beside the stage (`nextStepFile` everywhere, plus keys such as Test Skill's `blockedStepFile` and Update Skill's `gapDrivenStepFile`), and every other bare path resolves as before. Quick Skill's `[S]` option at the compile review and Update Skill's `--dry-run` route to the report now load their stage by its `references/` path, Brief Skill points at its JSON schemas under `shared/scripts/schemas/`, which an installed SKF holds, instead of the dev-only `src/shared/`, and Refine Architecture's SKILL.md names the files its stages load. ([#1204](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1204); issue [#1112](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1112))
- **skf-analyze-source, skf-audit-skill, skf-brief-skill, skf-create-skill, skf-create-stack-skill, skf-export-skill, skf-quick-skill, skf-refine-architecture, skf-rename-skill, skf-test-skill, skf-update-skill, skf-verify-stack:** The override examples in each workflow's `customize.toml` now work when you copy them: the `persistent_facts` example that stops loading `project-context.md` starts with the `[workflow]` line it needs, since a setting above that line is ignored without a warning, and Rename Skill's `force_source_authority_in_headless` comment, its headless halt message and the docs say to write it under `[workflow]`. The template and folder settings of Test Skill, Stack Skill, Quick Skill, Export Skill and Refine Architecture say to keep your copy outside the skill folder, which every update replaces, and to name it as `{project-root}/<path to the copy>`; Test Skill, Stack Skill and Export Skill show their bundled default instead of an empty string. Export Skill runs its `on_complete` command from your project root, with `{project-root}` in it replaced by that folder, as its example writes it. ([#1207](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1207); issue [#1108](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1108))
- **skf-audit-skill:** Audit Skill now counts the provenance map's age from the map's `last_update`, which each Update Skill run writes, as Update Skill does, and from its `generated_at` only when no update ran. An audit right after an update no longer shows the age of the map Create Skill wrote as the days since the last extraction, and no longer stops to recommend the Update Skill run that just happened because the map is more than 90 days old. ([#1220](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1220); issue [#1193](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1193))
- **skf-audit-skill:** The Version preservation note in Audit Skill's drift report no longer sends readers to other skills' step files for its guarantee: one pointer named a section Update Skill does not have, and another an Export Skill file that never mentions `archived`. The note now states the guarantee itself: Update Skill keeps the audited version, writes the new one in a folder of its own beside it and repoints the `active` link at it, and the next export marks the prior version's manifest entry `status: archived`, its files kept for rollback. The New public API note no longer cites an Update Skill section either, so the drift report depends on no other skill's numbering. ([#1210](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1210); issue [#1133](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1133))
- **skf-brief-skill:** A headless or `[auto]` Brief Skill run that halts now prints its `SKF_BRIEF_RESULT_JSON` line on stderr, with the skill name (`unknown` before the run resolves one), the `mode` and every warning the run raised. Each halt used to leave those values to rules the run might no longer have in view, and one missed value, or a validator warning passed on as an object, made the emitter refuse the payload and print no line at all. Brief Skill now records each warning in its run folder as it is raised, and each halt is one `skf-emit-result-envelope.py emit-halt --halt-reason` call that reads the rest from the run folder. The shared emitter now turns a `{field, message}` warning into one `field: message` line, in `emit`, `emit-halt` and `record --warnings-file` alike. `skf-emit-brief-result-envelope.py` stays as an alias. ([#1213](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1213); issue [#1134](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1134))
- **skf-brief-skill:** An interactive Brief Skill run now finds the draft an earlier run saved for its target however the target is written (letter case, a trailing slash, `.git`, `owner/repo` or a relative path), where it used to miss a draft whose target was written another way. A new brief gathered from the target and written over an existing `skill-brief.yaml` now keeps that file's `scope.amendments`, the log of scope changes Create Skill and Update Skill write, instead of dropping them: the overwrite question says how many it holds, and a headless run that overwrites with `force` keeps them too. An entry whose change the new scope does not hold, such as a promoted path the new `scope.include` leaves out, is dropped with a warning, there and when a revised brief's scope leaves it out, so Update Skill offers that path again instead of treating it as in scope. A change made at the brief review is now saved to the draft, so an interrupted run resumes with it, and a rename moves the draft instead of leaving the old one to be offered again. An aside you mention while giving the target or the intent, which was noted but never reached the brief, is now shown in the summary and added to the brief's scope notes, where you can drop it at the review. ([#1213](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1213); issue [#1137](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1137))
- **skf-brief-skill:** Brief Skill no longer warns that a documentation URL cannot be reached when its server refuses HEAD requests or redirects it to a working page. The new `skf-check-urls.py` checks the doc URLs of a docs-only target given at the first prompt, the supplemental doc URLs shown at scope definition and a headless run's `doc_urls` argument, with HEAD requests that follow redirects and a GET when the server answers 403, 405 or 501, and prints one `{url, ok, status, error}` entry per URL; `curl` runs only when the helper is missing. An `[auto]` run whose source is a local folder or a repository outside GitHub, as Analyze Source passes for a local project, now skips documentation detection with an info line instead of carrying a "Doc detection failed" warning in its envelope. At Deep tier the check for existing briefs that look like the one being written, and the check that a registered brief's QMD collection holds its file, now each run as one `skf-qmd-portfolio-similarity.py` call (`similar` and `verify-collection`) instead of `qmd` commands the model ran, capped and merged. A query that times out or fails is named in the run's warning while the other close briefs still show, and a first Deep-tier brief, with no other brief to compare, records no warning. ([#1213](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1213); issue [#1139](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1139))
- **skf-campaign:** Campaign's Refine stage now scopes Refine Architecture (`--scope-skills`) by the skill folder of each completed skill, the name Refine Architecture's inventory knows, instead of the campaign target name. A Tier B skill whose folder Quick Skill named after the library (target `cognee-lib`, folder `cognee`) no longer drops out of the refinement scope. The names come from the new `campaign-status.py --export-names`, which prints them on one comma-separated line; when no skill completed, Campaign leaves `--scope-skills` out. ([#1214](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1214); issue [#1141](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1141))
- **skf-create-skill:** Create Skill's doc-rot scan now leaves the compiled SKILL.md's own migration section out of the correction candidates only under the exact level-2 heading `## Migration & Deprecation Warnings`, the heading Create Skill emits and Test Skill's Deep-tier migration check counts as Section 4b. Before, it also left out a section whose heading differed in case or had more text after it, such as `## Migration & Deprecation Warnings (pre-1.0)`, while Test Skill reported that skill's Section 4b as missing, so the two read one heading two ways. ([#1095](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1095); issue [#1069](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1069))
- **skf-create-skill:** Create Skill now writes the provenance map before it assembles `SKILL.md`, so a function whose signature extraction left unread is read and patched first, and `SKILL.md` and `references/` give its parameters and return type instead of leaving them out. The run's source (its ref, commit, tag resolution, source tree and resolved source path), the version it reconciled and its run folder are now recorded in the extraction inventory right after the source is resolved, and a component library's aggregate counts are kept there too, so a run whose context was compacted still writes the right `source_commit`, `source_ref`, `source_root` and `version` into `metadata.json` and `provenance-map.json`. When the run folder itself is lost, compile stops with exit `4` (`staging-unreadable`) before anything is promoted, and the report writes no result contract, instead of an evidence report and a result that claimed the run took no auto-decisions. A component-library extraction that loses the extract stage from context now goes back to building the inventory instead of having no resume point. ([#1222](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1222); issue [#1144](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1144))
- **skf-drop-skill, skf-update-skill, skf-audit-skill, skf-test-skill, skf-rename-skill:** A Drop Skill or Update Skill stage took the shared helpers it runs (the result emitter, the manifest and context-file helpers, Update Skill's run-state and run-lock helpers) only from what an earlier step resolved, so after a long run's context was compacted it could lose one and have nothing in its own file to find it again: the run then wrote no result files and printed no result line, an Update Skill run stopped at the run-lock renewal before it published the new version, and an Update Skill halt could not undo what the run wrote or release its run lock. The report steps of Drop, Update, Audit, Test and Rename Skill likewise read `on_complete` only from activation, so a lost value skipped a team's hook as if it were the empty default. Each of those stages now lists where each helper it runs lives (the installed SKF path, then the development tree's) and resolves a lost one from that list, every Update Skill halt runs the run-state helper itself, and each report step reads a lost `on_complete` again through the customization resolver, or from the bundled `customize.toml` when the resolver cannot run, before it decides whether the hook runs, as Create Skill already does. ([#1204](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1204); issue [#1116](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1116))
- **skf-export-skill:** Export Skill's token report now measures what the run produced. A dry run used to delete its stage folder before the report, which then measured the snippet and managed section already on disk, not the ones the run would write; now the stage folder lives until the report, which measures the staged draft and the section the run would write, and deletes it. `skf-count-tokens.py` gains `--snippet <path>`, which measures that file as the snippet row, `--section-file <path>`, which measures a staged section body as the block `insert` writes around it, and `--no-snippet`, which leaves the snippet row out of the package total. A run with passive context off passes `--no-snippet` and no context file, so a snippet create-skill left in the package no longer counts, and the report shows the snippet and managed-section rows as N/A (disabled). The token report also states the helper's JSON once instead of three ways. ([#1209](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1209); issue [#1166](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1166))
- **skf-export-skill:** Export Skill's skill menu no longer offers a skill whose active version `.export-manifest.json` marks deprecated, as the docs say: a deprecated skill still on disk used to come back through the folder scan. The menu and `--all` now list the skills through one `skf-skill-inventory.py exportable` call, which leaves out deprecated skills and folders SKF did not generate, and the run names the skills each rule left out once, on a `Skipped (deprecated in the export manifest)` line and a `Skipped (not SKF output)` line. The list fails closed: when the helper cannot read the export manifest, including one that is not a JSON object or whose `exports` is not an object, the run stops with exit `3` (`resolution-failure`). ([#1209](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1209); issue [#1163](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1163))
- **skf-export-skill:** Export Skill now clears an orphaned context file only after you confirm the writes. When a context file such as `CLAUDE.md` still holds an SKF managed section but no IDE in `config.yaml` maps to it, answering (a) clear used to remove that section at once, before the orphaned-rows question, the change preview and the [C] confirmation, so a cancel or a halt after it left the file changed while the run said no context file was written, and the result did not list the file. Now (a) only lists the file: the change preview and the confirmation name it as `CLAUDE.md` (clear), and the run clears it after it writes the target files. A cleared file is listed in `context_files_updated` and in a `clear_orphan_context` entry of the result's `deviations`. A clear that fails stops the run with exit `4` (`context-rebuild-failed`). ([#1209](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1209); issue [#1165](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1165))
- **skf-export-skill:** Export Skill now fills a stack skill's `|stack:` line from the `libraries` of its `metadata.json`, each with the version its `references/<library>.md` gives, and its `|integrations:` line from `integration_pairs`, the fields Stack Skill writes and the export gate counts. The snippet step named `components` and `integrations`, fields a stack's `metadata.json` does not have, so a re-export could drop both lines or copy them from the prior snippet by hand. ([#1209](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1209); issue [#1164](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1164))
- **skf-export-skill, skf-update-skill:** Export Skill now keeps the `()` the prior `|api:` line gave each name it lists. SKF 5.0.0 through 10.0.0 set each name's `()` from the provenance map's `export_type`, which does not say how the line marks a name: an ast-grep recipe labels a const arrow function `function` where a by-eye read can label it `const`, and a component declared with `function` is labeled `function` though the line wrote it bare. So a re-export of a surface that had not changed could drop the `()` from a hook or helper and add one to a component. A name the prior line lists is now written with `()` or bare as that line wrote it, whatever its kind, and the map's `export_type` sets `()` only for a name new to the line. A line an export from those releases already wrote keeps its marks, so check the `|api:` line in the `context-snippet.md` of the active version of each skill they exported: to change a name's mark, edit that line and export the skill again, and later exports keep the edit while the name stays on the line and no Create Skill or Quick Skill run writes the skill a new snippet. A name that leaves the line, because the 300-token trim, a tier's smaller limit, a deprecation or its removal from `exports` drops it, comes back as a new name and takes its mark from its kind again. Update Skill regenerates the snippet by the same rule and no longer counts a listed name's kind change as a change to the line. If `snippet_format_path` points Export Skill at your own copy of `snippet-format.md` made before this release, that copy still tells Export Skill to give `()` to every name whose kind is a function: replace its `|api:` placeholder with the bundled file's wording, and delete its Line 4 bullet and its api line rule, which the bundled file no longer has. ([#1099](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1099); issue [#1093](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1093))
- **skf-export-skill, skf-update-skill:** On a re-export, Export Skill now keeps a prior `|gotchas:` pitfall without the `[CARRIED]` marker while the current SKILL.md still states the pitfall's main claim anywhere, in any wording, its frontmatter description, Overview and other prose included, and no place in it contradicts that claim with another version or name. Before, such a pitfall counted as no longer stated unless a T2-future annotation in the evidence report, a gotchas-type section, a deprecated or removed `## Key API Summary` row or a Quick Start `await` call stated it, so a skill whose SKILL.md has no gotchas-type section had its whole gotchas line marked `[CARRIED]` and then dropped on the export after, under a warning that said SKILL.md no longer stated them. New gotchas still come only from those places, so the line stays the same from export to export, and a pitfall the old rule already dropped comes back only through them. A prior pitfall that joins several warnings, as a gotchas bullet often does, stays while one T2-future annotation or one of those bullets, rows or Quick Start calls states it whole, and is written once. One that SKILL.md states only in parts or only in other prose, such as an older line read whole, is still carried at most once, while a slot is free, and then dropped. The prior pitfalls still stated take the line's 3 slots before any new gotcha, so a prior pitfall stated only in other prose now also ranks first, where before every new gotcha came before it: a new gotcha, such as a breaking change an Update Skill run adds to a gotchas-type section, can now be left off a line that already holds 3 such prior pitfalls. A new gotcha left without a slot, because prior pitfalls still stated come first or earlier new gotchas fill the line, is now named in a warning: to give it a slot, remove from the `|gotchas:` line in the `context-snippet.md` of the skill's active version a prior pitfall that SKILL.md states only in other prose, then export the skill again. Update Skill regenerates a snippet by the same rule. ([#1099](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1099); issue [#1092](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1092))
- **skf-export-skill, skf-update-skill:** Export Skill now reads a prior `|gotchas:` line back as the pitfalls it was written with. Before, it split the line on every `; `, so a pitfall that held one became two pieces: a `[CARRIED]` marker could land inside that pitfall, and a real pitfall could be dropped under a warning whose reason was untrue. A `; ` now separates two pitfalls only outside parentheses and code spans (so a pitfall that leaves a `(` open, or holds an odd number of backticks, is read together with the pitfalls after it), and a line that still splits into more than 3 pieces, such as one an older export wrote, is read as one pitfall that no current source states whole, and its still-true pitfalls are derived again from a T2-future annotation in the evidence report or from the current SKILL.md's gotchas-type sections, deprecated or removed `## Key API Summary` rows and Quick Start `await` calls. When Export Skill writes the line, and when Update Skill regenerates a snippet, a `; ` inside a pitfall, a kept or carried prior one included, is now written as `, `, while a code span keeps its `; `. A line that holds such a pitfall is rewritten once, on its next export or snippet regeneration. ([#1099](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1099); issue [#1091](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1091))
- **skf-export-skill, skf-verify-stack:** Export Skill and Verify Stack now run your `activation_steps_append` entries at the end of start-up, after its own checks and just before the first stage loads, as their `customize.toml` says. They used to run them earlier, so a run that then stopped at start-up on a missing helper, an unwritable skills folder or a missing result emitter had already run them. The first stage's own checks, such as Verify Stack's write probe of its output folder, still run after them. ([#1207](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1207); issue [#1111](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1111))
- **skf-forger:** A headless run of one code through Ferris that fails or is cut off, such as `/skf-forger TS cocoindex --headless`, now ends on the workflow's result envelope line (`SKF_TEST_RESULT_JSON: ...` and the like), printed verbatim as the last line after a one-line acknowledgment, or on its halt reason when it printed none, instead of on the menu, so a `claude -p` caller reads the result from the last line. A headless chain that halts ends on its pipeline summary, with no menu after it. An interactive run still summarizes the failure and shows the menu again. ([#1212](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1212); issue [#1171](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1171))
- **skf-quick-skill:** Quick Skill now reports skill-check's quality score and the validation issue counts by one fixed rule, so the same validator results give the same `summary.quality_score` and `summary.validation_issues` on every run. Step 5 saves what skill-check, the frontmatter validator, the output validator and the security scan print in the run folder, and a new shared helper, `skf-summarize-validation.py`, writes the score, the counts and the issues behind them to `validation-summary.json` there; the result envelope copies both values from that file, and the step 5 report lists exactly the issues the counts count. `quality_score` now also reports the top-level `qualityScore` that older skill-check builds print, where it was null. When the helper goes missing after the run started, step 5 stops with exit `3` (`resolution-failure`, `details.cause` `validation-summarizer-missing`) and asks you to re-install SKF. ([#1205](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1205); issue [#1120](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1120))
- **skf-refine-architecture:** Refine Architecture now checks whether a claimed export exists with a script instead of looking it up by hand. Issue detection stages each API claim that names an export in `claimed-names.json`, and `skf-check-preservation.py exports` looks it up in the skill's export list from the saved skill inventory by its last name, after one fixed normalization: `Doc::new`, `cognee.add()`, the signature `query(sql: str) -> Rows` (backticked or not), `useQuery<Data>()` and `mod/fn` look up `new`, `add`, `query`, `useQuery` and `fn`, matched case-sensitively and never inside a longer name, so `get` is not found in `getAll`. A method of a type the list holds but whose methods it does not list (`member-unlisted`), and a skill whose list is empty or of unknown source, are judged from the skill's API surface and never reported missing for that alone. A skill inventory that can no longer be read at that point stops the run with exit `8` (`recovery-failed`, phase `issue-detection:exports`). ([#1219](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1219); issue [#1176](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1176))
- **skf-refine-architecture:** A long Refine Architecture run that lost its context could lose its headless mode, its output folder, its refinement rules, its record of findings dropped at an earlier review and its `on_complete` hook, since the run record in the RA state file (`ra-state-<project>.md`) kept only the run folder, the timestamp, the document and its project name. That record now also holds the document's content hash, the headless mode, the output folder, the refinement rules path and whether the document held an earlier pass, one `key=value` per line, so a path with spaces reads back whole, and every step names that record where it reads a binding back. The report step reads a lost `on_complete` hook from your customization again instead, so a personal hook in `_bmad/custom/skf-refine-architecture.user.toml`, which can hold a token, is never written to the state file in the forge data folder. Gap analysis now saves the document's scope to the state file before it reads any skill, and each round of API-surface reads as the round returns instead of once every round is done, so a context loss in the middle keeps the scope and what was read, and on a runtime that cannot launch subagents it reads the skills itself, one at a time, saving each before the next. ([#1219](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1219); issue [#1178](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1178))
- **skf-refine-architecture:** The Refinement Summary's Changes Made rows are now written by the preservation script, so a run can no longer type a tier count, leave a tier out of a breakdown or type the evidence rows. The rows name every severity and value tier of the refinement rules in order with its count, `0` included, and the VS Coverage row reads the coverage of the [VS] report the run used (`80%`, or `not recorded` when that run never measured it) and names the report by its file name only. A summary that does not leave these rows to the script is refused with `summary-count-typed` before the draft is built. ([#1219](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1219); issue [#1176](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1176))
- **skf-refine-architecture, skf-verify-stack:** Refine Architecture and Verify Stack now build the names they find each skill by, its own name and the repository and folder it was built from, with `skf-enumerate-stack-skills.py terms` instead of by hand, so an alias dropped while copying the inventory no longer moves a skill out of scope or hides it from the coverage check. Refine Architecture writes these terms once at the start and splits the skill pairs by scope with `skf-enumerate-stack-skills.py scope --inventory`, which reads every skill from the saved inventory, so no skill name is left out of a hand-joined list. In Refine Architecture a failure of either call stops the run with exit `3` (`resolution-failure`) at phase `init:inventory`, `gap-analysis:split` or, when gap analysis or issue detection writes the terms again, `gap-analysis:comention` or `issue-detection:vs-report`; in Verify Stack a failed `terms` call stops the coverage step as a failed mentions call does (exit `3`, phase `coverage:mentions`). ([#1219](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1219); issue [#1177](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1177))
- **skf-rename-skill:** A headless Rename Skill run with `--dry-run` that reaches the confirmation now ends there with status `dry-run` and exit `0`, before the confirmation is recorded and before anything is copied. Before, the headless auto-confirm could come first, so the run went on to the copy step and stopped with `halted-for-concurrent-run` (exit `5`) on the run lock a dry run never takes. ([#1221](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1221); issue [#1181](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1181))
- **skf-rename-skill:** Rename Skill's headless halts no longer have the model escape a helper's error into a hand-typed JSON payload. Each halt now passes its phase, halt reason, path and skill names to `skf-emit-result-envelope.py emit-halt` as options and its message on stdin through a quoted heredoc, and a halt that quotes a failed command's error first saves that command's stderr in the run folder (`call.err`) for the emitter to read. A traceback, a quote, a backtick, `$( )` or a Windows path in the error no longer breaks the `SKF_RENAME_SKILL_RESULT_JSON` line or runs as a command: the emitter puts the error's diagnostic line on it, folded to one line (a JSON error's `message`, else the first line, such as a traceback's), and the whole stderr stays in `call.err`. A halt call the emitter refuses is fixed once and run again. A run lock the halt could not release is still named in the envelope's `warnings` (`run-lock-not-released: <lock>`). `emit-halt` takes `--phase`, `--halt-reason`, `--reason` (`-` reads it on stdin), `--path`, `--stderr-from`, `--old-name` and `--new-name`; without `--phase` it reads its payload on stdin as before. ([#1205](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1205); issue [#1119](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1119))
- **skf-setup:** Setup now reads its flags with a helper script, `skf-setup-args.py`, instead of splitting the command line by eye. `--require-tier --headless` (no tier given) used to take `--headless` as the tier and lose quiet mode, so a `claude -p` run ended on a prose reason: it now stays quiet and ends `blocked` at `step 1:detect-tools` with its envelope. An `--orphan-action` other than `keep` or `remove` still stops Setup at `on-activation:orphan-action-invalid`, with the reason the helper writes. A Setup install whose helper cannot read the flags stops at `on-activation:helper-missing` once `uv` is found. ([#1218](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1218); issue [#1183](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1183))
- **skf-setup:** When the customization resolver fails, Setup Forge now saves its error in the run folder (`resolver.err`), and every later halt and the final report pass that file to the emitter with `--customization-resolver-unavailable-from`, which takes the reason, folds it to one line and escapes it. The reason no longer goes through a hand-escaped shell argument or a hand-built `report-context.json`, so a backtick, `$( )`, a quote or a backslash in it can no longer break the `SKF_SETUP_RESULT_JSON` line or run as a command. The report also passes the orphan decision as `--orphan-action`, `--headless` and `--quiet`, and the emitter derives its `source` (`orphan-action-flag`, `headless-default` or `quiet-default`) from them. `emit`, `render-report` and `emit-blocked` of `skf-emit-result-envelope.py` gain `--customization-resolver-unavailable-from FILE`, and setup's `emit` and `render-report` read an empty stdin as an empty payload: the report runs them with `< /dev/null`, so neither reads or waits on a stdin the host left open. ([#1205](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1205); issue [#1119](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1119))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's signature rules now compare a documented form bound to an overload set with the whole set, its stubs and its implementation, as they compare a form bound to nothing. A form is bound when its own citations name one declaration of its name, and the extraction records an overloaded name at its first `@overload` stub or TS bodiless signature, so such a form is bound to that stub. A bound form that matches the implementation, any stub or, position by position, the unions of the stubs' parameter types is no mismatch, and a mismatch is still reported at the bound declaration's file and line. A form of cognee's `export` returning `GraphSnapshot | ExportResult`, bound to its first stub (`-> GraphSnapshot`), therefore matches the implementation's `-> ExportResult | GraphSnapshot`. A form bound to a name overloaded in one Java, Kotlin, C# or C++ file reads the same and matches when it matches any of those overloads. Before, the rules compared a bound form with its bound declaration alone and never said whether that left out the set's own overloads. Read against the first stub alone, the cognee form is an untagged Critical `signature-mismatch` gap that would fail the hard gate; oms-cognee 1.6.2's judge listed it as undecided, and the skill's 99% pass rested on reading it through the implementation. ([#1096](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1096); issue [#1081](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1081))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's signature rules now read a container written in words one way in every language and with every word for its items. A list written in words states the source language's list or array type with that type argument, so `list of Nodes` is `list[Node]` in a Python skill and `Node[]`, the same type as `Array<Node>`, in a TypeScript or JavaScript one. A generic noun for the items, such as `objects`, `instances`, `items`, `values`, `entries` or `records`, is description, so the type name before it is the type argument and a documented `list of DataPoint objects` states `list[DataPoint]`, while a generic noun alone, as in `list of objects`, writes no type argument, which is then not compared. A type name made plural, such as `dicts` or `strs`, still names that type. Before, a judge could read `objects` as the type `object` and raise a Critical `signature-mismatch` gap on `list of DataPoint objects` against a source's `list[DataPoint]`, or read `list of Nodes` as Python's `list[Node]` against a TypeScript source's `Node[]` and raise one there, failing the hard gate, while another judge passed the same skill. ([#1098](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1098); issue [#1083](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1083))
- **skf-test-skill:** A placeholder Cross-Cutting Patterns bullet such as `None detected` no longer counts as an integration pattern, so it no longer lifts a stack skill's Coherence score. ([#1224](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1224); issue [#1187](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1187))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill can now record the documentation errors a Deep-tier run asks for: an import path whose module does not export the name, and a type member that differs from its declaration. The coverage check asked for an Info `Not checked by script: {name}` observation for each such error, but no one held both the skill's import lines or documented members and the source: the parent never loads the skill, each signature judge got only a check's `params`, `return_type` and `usage_signature` forms, and a name the skill documents only by members got no check at all. On oms-cognee 1.6.2, 12 such names, `SearchType` and `RememberResult` among them, got no check, and all 39 judge results had no place for such an error. At the Deep tier `score-signatures.py plan --doc-errors` now gives each check the skill's import statements of its name (`imports`: a fenced Python `from M import` or TS/JS `import { } from` statement; other forms, such as a CommonJS `require` or a Rust `use`, give none) and its documented `fields`, `properties` and `methods` (`members`), and gives a name documented only by these a check that Signature Accuracy never counts when a surface record of it names a file. The judge compares them with the source by a new `signature-comparison-rules.md` paragraph and returns each that differs in `doc_errors`, and `score` records each as the Info observation at the documenting line, so no record is written by hand. A member documented beside a form the skill's citations bind to another declaration of the name is compared with that declaration, and a documented method is looked up as a method form's member is, so an object's method is read on its class. A malformed item is dropped with a warning. Forge-tier plans, every score and the fallback per-file scan are unchanged. ([#1102](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1102); issue [#1084](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1084))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill no longer sends a signature judge a documented name it cannot locate in any file, such as an extraction gap the runner did not locate. `score-signatures.py plan` used to file that name's check under the empty file name `""`, where no judge has a file to read: a judge result for it broke the result schema, so `score` exited 2, and a second one halted the coverage check with `helper-failed`. The plan now gives such a name no check and lists it in a new `notCompared` key, and `score --plan` leaves it out of Signature Accuracy and names it under the report's Scoring Warnings, where before, with no judge result, it was counted as a matching signature. A method form whose owner is such a name, checked under `{owner}.{name}`, is left out and named the same way. A name whose form the skill's own citations bind to one declaration is still compared at that declaration. ([#1102](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1102); issue [#1061](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1061))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill no longer records a Medium `stale-documentation` gap for a name the source declares in several files when the name's own documented form cites one of them and other lines write the name only as a type argument of another export. The gap ledger picked the declaring file from the citations on every SKILL.md or references line that wrote the name, so a row such as `App[P, R]` added the file of the export it documents, two declaring files were cited, and the report asked the author to update or remove correct documentation. It now reads first the citations of the name's forms at the places the validated inventory gives them, each read as the signature check reads it, and reads the lines that name it only when those forms cite none of the declaring files (a package and its same-named module still counting as one), so forms citing two declaring files between them keep the Medium gap whatever those lines cite. For oms-cocoindex, `R`, whose form `R = TypeVar("R", default=Any)` cites only `python/cocoindex/query_handler.py`, is now an Info `Documented extra: R` at that file, its issue saying which forms cite it, instead of a Medium `Stale documentation: R`. A documented extra the lines naming it placed at another file moves to the file its forms cite, and when a brief scopes out a namespace's member named like the namespace, that file also decides whether the name is the member, which keeps its Medium gap, or the documented module. ([#1104](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1104); issue [#1077](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1077))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill no longer cites a sentence saying the skill does not cover a name as the line that documents a stale name. The gap ledger read every code span of a heading or a prose line for the line that documents a name, so a disclaimer such as "`load_env_file`, `describe_resolution` and `setup_logging` are among them but out of scope for this skill." could rank before the line that writes and describes the name, and a stale gap's Source, Issue and remediation sent the author to remove the accurate scoping sentence. A sentence that says "out of scope for this skill" or "not covered here", in any case and outside its code spans, now documents nothing unless it is a place the inventory floor lists, as `inventory-contract.md` already says; the other sentences of its line, and the other cells of its table row, still document their names. For oms-cognee 1.6.2, the scoped-out `Stale documentation: setup_logging` gap now cites `SKILL.md:183`, the `cognee.logger` row that binds `logger = setup_logging()` and describes it, instead of `SKILL.md:28`. A name written only in such a sentence is cited at the place the validated inventory gives it, else at `SKILL.md`, as any undocumented name is. Severity, score, gate and gap count stay the same. ([#1104](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1104); issue [#1080](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1080))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill now also renews its run lock as each of its steps before the health check starts and each time it finishes reading source files by eye, not only as a subagent returns. The lock goes stale 60 minutes after it was taken or last renewed, and between two subagents the run could read a skill's source by eye for a long time, such as every entry point of a skill in another language at the Quick tier, then check coherence, run the external validators and score the skill before its next renewal. A second run of the same skill version started then took the lock over instead of stopping with `another-run-active`, and the first run halted later with no result written. A second run now stops at the start with `another-run-active` while the first one reads. ([#1100](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1100); issue [#1064](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1064))
- **skf-test-skill:** Every Test Skill stage that writes a section of the test report (Detect Mode, Coverage Check, Coherence Check, External Validators, the hard gate, Score and the Gap Report) now writes its prose in the configured `document_output_language`, where only the Gap Report step named it, so the other sections could be written in `communication_language` instead. ([#1217](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1217); issue [#1189](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1189))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill now scores a run from flags it reads back from the test report, not from what a long run still remembers. The report gains a `docsOnly` key, which the coverage check writes when it decides whether the skill is docs-only, and a docs-only run writes `analysisConfidence: 'docs-only'` at once. The score step reads `tier` from `forgeTier`, `docsOnly` and `analysisConfidence` from the report, and the State 2 flag from `analysisConfidence`, and it passes `surface.json` to `compute-score.py` on every run that wrote one. `compute-score.py` now refuses (`INVALID_INPUT`, exit 2) a `docsOnly` that disagrees with `coverage.json`'s `denominatorSource` and a `state2` that is not true beside a `surface.json` holding State 2 counts, so a lost flag can no longer skip the docs-only cap or the State 2 deduction. The Coverage Analysis section's Tier line now names the tier the run tested at, through a value init binds, where it named one no step bound. ([#1217](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1217); issue [#1185](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1185))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill no longer stops a finished run over a copying slip in its verdict. The score step used to type `testResult`, `score`, `threshold`, `nextWorkflow` and the threshold fallback fields into the report by hand from the scoring output, and the result step then refused any field that did not match, so a score of 87.37 written as `87.4%` halted the run before it published its report. `build-result-context.py settle` now writes those fields into the report frontmatter from the scoring output, keeping every other line and the file's line endings, and prints the Completeness Score section (the Score Breakdown table and the Result lines) for the step to write unchanged. A refused or unreadable input, or a report the hard gate blocked, stops it with one `error:` line and the report left as it was, and the run halts `helper-failed` at the new phase `score:settle`. ([#1217](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1217); issue [#1186](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1186))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill no longer records a blocking Critical `fabricated-signature` gap for a name whose provenance map entry cites the line of an `export *` or `export type *` from another package that no script reads, such as `Mock` cited at `export type * from '@vitest/spy';` in a storybook `spy.ts`. The fabricated-signature test found no definition of the name on that line and marked it fabricated, so the gap ledger recorded `Fabricated signature: Mock` before its check for names passed on by another package's `export *` ran, though the star passes the name on. That test now notes the module such a line names on the entry, its verdict unchanged, and the gap ledger reads an entry whose file and module match a star in the run's `surface.json` `unresolvedStars` like that star: an Info `observation` titled `Not checked by script: Mock (another package's export *)` at the line that documents the name, whose issue and remediation say the provenance map cites it at the star statement, with the entry's file and line, and ask no change unless that package lacks the name. This holds with or without the skill folder, and for a name that was not fabricated; when the skill's own citations also place the name at that file, the record is the one they already gave, when they place it at another star's file the record names that star and the entry's, and a name the brief scopes out keeps its Medium gap. The Info `Provenance line not verified for Mock` gap at that entry now stays in the Gap Report beside it, and with classify-stale's result its issue and remediation say that the line is an `export *` from that package, so no line of the file defines the name, and ask no change unless the package lacks it, in place of confirming that the line defines it. An entry at a relative `export *`, at any other line or at a star the surface does not list keeps a fabricated name Critical. ([#1104](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1104); issue [#1070](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1070))
- **skf-test-skill, skf-quick-skill:** Test Skill's headless stops that come before its run folder exists and quote a helper's error, such as a config `skf-preflight.py` cannot load, a flat skill `migrate` could not move or a `forge-tier.yaml` it cannot read, no longer have the model type that error into a JSON payload. Each passes its phase, halt reason and skill name to `skf-emit-result-envelope.py emit-halt` as options, the skill name through the new `--skill-name`, and its message on stdin through a quoted heredoc, so a Windows path or a quote in the error no longer stops the `SKF_TEST_RESULT_JSON` line from printing. Quick Skill's stop for a run folder it cannot create now gives `Quick Skill cannot start: the run folder could not be created.` as the message of its `SKF_QUICK_SKILL_RESULT_JSON` line and shows the error it got only on screen, so that line always prints. ([#1205](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1205); issue [#1119](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1119))
- **skf-update-skill:** A plain Update Skill run that finds a failed test report whose FAIL a cap forced (the report's **Cap:** line, such as a frontmatter validator that timed out) no longer offers to repair its gaps first. No skill edit lifts a cap, so it names the cap and offers to check the source for changes first. Its no-change report, its report of a repair from a capped test report and its next steps say to restore the tooling the cap names and run Test Skill again, and to repair the gaps only when that test fails too. Before, it offered the repair and recommended `--from-test-report`, which left the FAIL in place. ([#1220](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1220); issue [#1194](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1194))
- **skf-update-skill:** A degraded Update Skill run, the full re-extraction a skill with no provenance map takes, now reports `update_mode` `degraded` in `categories.json`, in the Mode rows of the baseline summary and the report, and in the `SKF_UPDATE_RESULT_JSON` line, where before it reported `normal`. ([#1220](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1220); issue [#1193](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1193))
- **skf-update-skill:** Scope reconciliation now reads the newest drift report whose audit finished, so a partial report that a halted or stopped Audit Skill run left no longer hides the last finished one and its new public API outside the scope. A version folder that holds only unfinished drift reports now reads as having no report, and reconciliation is skipped. ([#1210](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1210); issue [#1129](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1129))
- **skf-update-skill:** Update Skill's write step now runs in the order it is written: it first prepares what the provenance map and `metadata.json` are written from (a repair's metadata patches, the version, the generation date and the source commit the map records), then writes the provenance map with one `apply` run, then computes the stats from that map, relabels the entries they flag and writes `metadata.json`. Before, the section that wrote `metadata.json` came first but needed `apply` to have run, while `apply` read values that section bound, so a model that followed the numbering could run `apply` twice, and the second run overwrote the relabels. A repair's structural fixes, metadata patches (with whether each field was applied, left out or dropped by the recount) and exports found internal now reach you: they are recorded in the run folder's `evidence-records.jsonl`, and the evidence report's new Repairs Applied block and the update report's **Repairs applied:** line list them, where before they were noted "in the update report", which had no place for them. The run's flags, lock owner, source-tree bindings and skill paths are written to the run folder's `run-context.json` as step 1 ends, updated with the new version's paths after the merge, and read back from there when a long run loses one from its context; merge's metadata patches go to `metadata-patches.json` in the same folder. The write step no longer writes `not-public.json`, which nothing read. ([#1220](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1220); issue [#1192](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1192))
- **skf-update-skill, skf-create-skill:** Update Skill now writes its promote, skip and headless-deferral decisions on newly found documents and out-of-scope paths, and a repair's rescopes, to the skill brief with `skf-write-skill-brief.py amend` instead of editing the brief by hand. A promoted path no longer narrows an empty `scope.include`, which already covers every file. `amend` now takes `exclude` paths and skips a decision that is already the latest one for its path (`skipped_duplicates` counts them), so a re-run records nothing twice while a changed decision is still recorded, in Create Skill too, which records its own scope decisions with the same `amend`. A decision the brief cannot record adds a `brief-not-amended` warning and leaves that document untracked, so the next run asks again, and a repair whose rescopes cannot be written stops with `halted-for-write-failure` (`error.phase` `merge:brief-amend`) and is undone. ([#1220](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1220); issue [#1193](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1193))
- **skf-update-skill, skf-create-skill:** In a JavaScript or TypeScript monorepo, the source version that names Update Skill's new version folder could come from a sibling package's `package.json`. `skf-extract-public-api.py` now picks the version file itself with its new `--package-name`: the `package.json` whose `name` is the skill's name, as given or as a skill name, whole or without its `@scope/` (`@acme/foo` matches `acme-foo` and `foo`), else one with a `bin` field, else the root one. It reports the file it read as `manifest_file`, with the `rule` that chose it, and passes over a `package.json` that is not JSON, such as a template's placeholder. Create Skill reads the source version the same way for a source it reads from a local folder or a clone; for a remote source read without a clone, it still picks the file from the repository's file listing. ([#1220](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1220); issue [#1193](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1193))

### Documentation

- The campaign directive docs now list only the two sections Campaign's scripts parse, `## Quality Overrides` and `## Skip List`. `## Pipeline Flags` and `## Notes` are no longer listed, since nothing parsed them: any other heading is read as general guidance, which changes no sub-skill's flags or inputs.
