([#1214](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1214); issue [#1140](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1140))
- Verifying a Skill and the README now quote strict SKF 10.0.0 tests of the version each of oh-my-skills' four reference skills ships, run as Test Skill is designed, with its subagents: oms-cocoindex, oms-storybook-react-vite and oms-uitripled pass at 100%, and oms-cognee at 99%. The page says that 10.0.0 settles four of the calls the 9.0.0 passes turned on (#999, #1045, #1050, #1003), that its first tests listed lines whose other reading would block in all four skills, one of them a real error, that oh-my-skills fixed it, rewrote the correct lines in three of the skills and re-tested each skill once, and which readings that would block the published reports still list. `docs/_data/pinned.yaml` records the 10.0.0 run ids. ([#1090](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1090))
- Verifying a Skill and `docs/_data/pinned.yaml` now quote oh-my-skills' latest strict SKF 10.0.0 test of oms-uitripled (20261110T153107Z-82714bca), still at 100%, which tests the gotchas section oh-my-skills added so that Skill Forge 10.0.0's export kept the snippet's three pitfalls instead of marking them `[CARRIED]`. The page counts its 70 listed readings, none blocking, and says that three 10.0.0 readers listed 35, 10 and 70 readings on text that differed in two passages. ([#1094](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1094))
- The README's reference-output paragraph no longer gives the SKF 4.0.0 results, under which oms-uitripled and oms-storybook-react-vite were blocked. It now quotes the strict results Verifying a Skill quotes: run as Test Skill is designed, with its subagents, all four oh-my-skills reference skills pass, with oms-cocoindex, oms-storybook-react-vite and oms-uitripled at 100% and oms-cognee at 99%. ([#1075](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1075))

## [10.0.0](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/compare/v9.0.0...v10.0.0) (2026-11-09)

### Breaking changes

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's signature rules now say which declaration a type name means when the source file imports a type under another name and reuses the original name for a local alias. A type name a documented form writes means the type the skill documents or the package exports under that name, and the source file's own declaration of it only when there is none or when the file declares the name other than as an alias, while a name the source writes is read in its own file, a local alias through the type it names. A documented `ThemesParameters['themes']` therefore matches a return of the local `type ThemesParameters = Parameters['themes']` declared over `import type { ThemesParameters as Parameters }`; before, a judge that read the documented name in that file raised a Critical `signature-mismatch` gap on the correct form and failed the hard gate. A mismatch's `source_sig`, which the gap's remediation asks the form to copy, now writes a local alias that reuses a documented or exported name as the type it names, by its exported name. A form that copies the local alias name as the source writes it (`=> ThemesParameters` there) now reads as the exported type and is a Critical gap, so a skill some runs passed can now stop at the hard gate. ([#1056](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1056); issue [#1050](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1050))

  **Migration:** If a skill now stops at the hard gate on a `signature-mismatch` gap whose source declares a local alias under a name the package exports, write the type the alias names in the package's exported names, as the gap's `source_sig` gives it (for example `ThemesParameters['themes']`), then run Test Skill again.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's signature rules now read a return written as a type followed by other types it names as alternatives, in a parenthetical or a list and each with an optional condition, as the union of every type it names, while the words that name no type, such as `with dry_run=True` or `for "pydantic"`, state nothing. A documented `RememberResult (DryRunEstimate with dry_run=True, PresortReport with dry_run="presort", or dict)` therefore matches the source's `Union["RememberResult", "DryRunEstimate", "PresortReport", dict]`, and `GraphSnapshot for "pydantic", ExportResult for "cogx"` states both types. Before, a judge that read the parenthetical as a description, as `HTML str` is read, compared only `RememberResult` and raised a Critical `signature-mismatch` gap on the correct form, failing the hard gate, while another judge passed the same skill. A type a parenthetical names other than as an alternative (`Response (see Request)`) stays a description. Because the named alternatives now count, a documented alternative the source never returns makes the documented return differ from the source's, a Critical gap that some runs passed, so such a skill can now stop at the hard gate. ([#1056](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1056); issue [#1042](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1042))

  **Migration:** If a skill now stops at the hard gate on a `signature-mismatch` gap whose documented return names a type the source never returns, remove that alternative from the return, or reword it so it names no type, then run Test Skill again.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill now reads what a documented form that writes no parameter list claims about parameters from the form itself when it grades a mismatch the signature judge tags `annotation-contradicted`. A form with no `params` and no usage form claims nothing about parameters, so such a mismatch whose other facts check is an Info `observation` titled `Annotation contradicted: {name}` however the judge writes the form, `-> Environment` or `() -> Environment`, and whatever parameters the source takes. Before, the judge's text was compared with the source's parameters: written by its return alone it had no parameter group, and the mismatch was a Critical `signature-mismatch` gap that failed the hard gate on a correct form. A form with `params: ""` or `[]` claims the export takes none and is compared as `()`: Info against a declaration that takes none, and Critical against one with a required parameter even when the judge copied the source's parameters into its `documented_sig`, which used to pass. A name the skill writes both ways with one return, with `params: ""` in one place and no `params` in another, is compared as the form that claims none, whichever the inventory lists first. The signature rules now say what a form with no `params` key claims, and that its contradicted return is tagged too. ([#1056](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1056); issue [#1025](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1025))

  **Migration:** If a skill now stops at the hard gate on a `signature-mismatch` gap for a form whose `params` is `""` or `[]` while the source takes a required parameter, write the parameters the source declares (the gap's `source_sig`) in the skill's signature for that name, then run Test Skill again.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's inventory floor now pins the form a floor table's row writes in a column whose header joins Signature to another word at `/`, such as `Signature / Purpose` or `Props / Signature`, as it pins a `Signature` cell: the code span the cell opens with, a description after it left out, labelled partial when the Signature part carries the label, as `Signature (simplified) / Purpose` does. Before, the floor read a form column only when its whole header was one listed word, so these forms stayed the reader's and two runs could record different forms there, or none: for storybook, 18 forms such as `fn<T>(implementation?: T): Mock<T>` and `argsHash(args: Args): ArgsHash` were never pinned. `validate-inventory.py --floor` now refuses an inventory whose entry there does not carry the form. A `Props / Usage` or `Props / Type` column and an `Arguments`, `Args`, `Usage`, `Syntax` or `Example` column are still not read, and the inventory contract now says so. An inventory that passed can now be refused. ([#1057](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1057); issue [#1030](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1030))

  **Migration:** If Test Skill halts with `inventory-invalid` on a form from a `Signature / Purpose` or other compound Signature column, run it again: the skill needs no change for it. If a run now stops at the hard gate on a `signature-mismatch` for a form such a column now pins, correct the form in the skill (the run's `inventory-floor.json` gives each origin's file, line and `signature`), then run Test Skill again. If a `signature` misreads the cell, report it as a bug with the line and the `signature`.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's inventory floor now reads an export table whose first header cell is `Query` or `Queries`, or is words split at `/` whose first names exports and each other names exports or props, such as `Component / Props` or `Function/Type`. Before, the floor read a table only when its whole first header cell was one listed word, so these tables gave no floor names and a reader could leave their exports out unchecked: for storybook, 73 names of a `Queries` and a `Component / Props` table were missing from the floor, and leaving them out recorded missing-export gaps and a lower Export Coverage with nothing flagging the drop. `validate-inventory.py --floor` now refuses an inventory that leaves out such a name, and a row that writes its name's signature in a fixed form pins it as any floor row does. A props table such as `Prop / Type` and a keyword table such as `Symbol / keyword` still give none. A `stale-documentation` gap now cites such a row, in a nested reference too, as the line that documents its name. An inventory that passed can now be refused. ([#1057](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1057); issue [#1004](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1004))

  **Migration:** If Test Skill halts with `inventory-invalid` on a name from a `Queries`, `Component / Props` or other compound export table, run it again: the skill needs no change for it. If a run now stops at the hard gate on a gap for such a name, or on a `signature-mismatch` for a form such a row now pins, document the name or correct the form in the skill (the run's `inventory-floor.json` gives each origin's file, line and `signature`), then run Test Skill again. If a name there is not an export, change that table's header rather than document it, and if a `signature` misreads the row, report it as a bug with the line and the `signature`.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's inventory floor now pins the form a `Key params` or `Key parameters` cell writes, the column Create Skill's Key API Summary gives, on a row whose `Kind` cell names a function, method, class, generator or hook, such as `sync fn` or `abstract class`, when the cell opens with the row's name and its parameter group, such as `Mem0Source(data, mode="re-derive")`. Each such form is pinned with `signature_form` `"partial"`, since the header says the cell lists key parameters only. Before, the floor never read that column, so readers recorded different forms there, or the same form with and without the label, which decides Info against Critical for a left-out optional parameter: for cognee, 11 forms such as `read_manifest(directory) -> COGXManifest | None` were never pinned. A table with no `Kind` column, a row of another kind such as `tuple` or `type alias`, a cell that writes a value, an import or a type, such as `("json", None)`, `import { z } from "zod"` or `A | B`, a cell that writes a second form of the name and a compound `Key params / shape` column still pin nothing, and a cell whose form prose qualifies stays the reader's. `validate-inventory.py --floor` now refuses an inventory whose entry there does not carry the form with its label. An inventory that passed can now be refused, and a skill that passed can now block at the hard gate. ([#1057](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1057); issue [#997](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/997))

  **Migration:** If Test Skill halts with `inventory-invalid` on a form from a `Key params` cell, run it again: the skill needs no change for it. If a run now stops at the hard gate on a `signature-mismatch` for a form such a cell now pins, correct the form in the skill (the run's `inventory-floor.json` gives each origin's file, line and `signature`), then run Test Skill again. If a `signature` misreads the cell, report it as a bug with the line and the `signature`.

- **skf-test-skill:** At every place Test Skill's inventory floor pins a form, the partial label is now the floor's. The floor now also pins `signature_form` `"partial"` on a form whose parameter group holds an ellipsis item, a `...` or `…` that is a member of its own standing in for members the skill does not show, in a `Signature` cell, an export table's first cell, a heading or a cited declaration, such as cognee's `add(data, dataset_name="main_dataset", user=None, node_set=None, ...)` heading; a rest `...args`, a `*args` and a `...` inside a nested type or object, such as `useForm({ defaultValues, ... })`, pin no label. `validate-inventory.py --floor` now refuses an entry that labels a pinned form `"partial"` where the floor pins no label, at that place or with no `at`, while a labelled copy at another line that writes the name stays valid. Before, the validator read an entry's label only where a column header such as `Signature (simplified)` gave one, so one reader could label a complete pinned form partial and turn a left-out optional parameter's Critical `signature-mismatch` into an Info observation while another reader did not. The inventory contract now says so. An inventory that passed can now be refused, and a skill that passed can now block at the hard gate. ([#1057](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1057); issue [#1029](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1029))

  **Migration:** If Test Skill halts with `inventory-invalid` on a `signature_form` the floor does not pin, run it again: the skill needs no change for it. If a run now stops at the hard gate on a `signature-mismatch` for a pinned form the skill presents as partial only in words, put the label in its column header, such as `Signature (simplified)`, or write the full form, then run Test Skill again.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's inventory reader now reads only the skill under test: its `SKILL.md`, the `references/*.md` files, `inventory-floor.json`, the inventory contract and the signature rules. It never opens another run's folder under `_bmad-output/.skf-run/`, a test report, a `test-findings-*.json` ledger or a `skf-test-skill-result-*.json` file. A halted run keeps its folder, and a reader that opened it could copy that run's inventory and cross-check mismatches into a run meant to test the skill afresh, so two runs could agree only because one copied the other. The reader also runs no SKF script, reads no script's code, and writes or deletes no file but `inventory-response.txt` in its run folder. A reader that ran `validate-inventory.py` itself could fix its draft until the validator accepted it, settle a reading by what the scripts accept rather than by the contract, and leave or delete files outside the run folder; validation is now the parent's alone, with the one retry it allows. The rules sit in the inventory contract the reader reads itself, so they hold whatever the reader's prompt says. Readings that were copied from an earlier run, or settled by the scripts' code, may now differ, and a first reading the validator refuses now takes that one retry instead of a fix made out of sight: when the validator refuses the second reading too, the run halts with `inventory-invalid`, which a hidden fix loop used to head off. ([#1055](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1055); issues [#1036](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1036), [#1046](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1046))

  **Migration:** If Test Skill now halts with `inventory-invalid` on a skill that passed, read the violations the halt names, correct the SKILL.md or reference lines they point to (or report the reading as a Test Skill issue when the skill is right), then run Test Skill again.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's `validate-inventory.py` now refuses an inventory whose export entry carries a key the inventory contract does not define, such as `usage` written for `usage_signature`. Before, such a key passed with no violation and no warning, and the signature check reads only `params`, `return_type` and `usage_signature`, so the form that entry recorded was never compared and a wrong call form could pass the hard gate. Each such entry is now a violation naming the entry, its unknown keys and the keys an entry carries (`name`, `kind`, `description`, `params`, `return_type`, `usage_signature`, `signature_form`, `at`, `owner`, `methods`, `properties` and `fields`), so the reader is dispatched again once with them, and the run halts `inventory-invalid` the second time. An inventory that passed can now be refused. ([#1057](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1057); issue [#1001](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1001))

  **Migration:** If Test Skill halts with `inventory-invalid` on an entry key the contract does not define, run it again: the skill needs no change for it. If the form the entry now carries stops the skill at the hard gate on a `signature-mismatch`, correct that form in the skill, then run Test Skill again.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's inventory contract now says when a method gets an entry of its own and what a class's form leaves out. A method a place writes with a form of its own, such as a class body, a methods list, a row's cell or running text, gets a `method` entry there besides its class's `methods` item, an untyped call such as `execute(args, kwargs, next_batch_size=None)` recorded as a usage, as a function's is, and so does a method the skill calls through an instance or its class, such as `builder.provide(KEY, value)`, with that class as `owner`; such a call is never a usage of a same-named function, so `canvas.getByRole('button')` can no longer be compared with a `getByRole` function and raise a false Critical `signature-mismatch`. A constructor the skill writes, such as `def __init__(self, ...)` in a class body or `__init__(...)` in a methods list or a row's cell, is its class's `params`, never a `method` entry, at the `class` line or else the nearest line of that place that writes the class's name, and a class's `params`, a `method`'s and each `methods` item now leave out a leading `self` or `cls`. Before, oh-my-skills rehearsal readers gave a class's methods entries on one run and none on the next, so the split-body cross-check compared them only sometimes. This can block a skill that passed: a method whose form two files write differently is now compared on every run, and each such difference is a High `split-body-mismatch` gap. ([#1060](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1060); issues [#1035](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1035), [#1045](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1045))

  **Migration:** If Test Skill now stops at the hard gate on a `split-body-mismatch` for a method, make the two files write the method's form alike (the gap's Source names the side the source contradicts), then run Test Skill again.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's `validate-inventory.py` now refuses an inventory whose split-body mismatch names no export the inventory lists. A `cross_check_mismatches` entry's `export` was checked only for being present, so a name no entry has, an empty string or a number passed and became a High `split-body-mismatch` gap titled with it, which Update Skill then took as the export to edit. Its `export` must now be an entry's `name` (a `method`'s bare name, or `{owner}.{name}` for a method entry that gives an `owner`), and any other is a violation naming the value, so the reader is dispatched again once with it, and the run halts `inventory-invalid` the second time. The section's Mismatches Found line, which read a count no step defined, now gives the number of `cross_check_mismatches` entries in the validated `inventory.json`, or 0 when its `references` is empty, as coverage-check then records no split-body gap. An inventory that passed can now be refused. ([#1057](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1057); issue [#1033](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1033))

  **Migration:** If Test Skill halts with `inventory-invalid` on a mismatch `export` that names no inventory entry, run it again: the skill needs no change for it.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's documented inventory now gives each form of a place that writes several forms of one name, such as two overloads in one row, an entry of its own with that same `at`, so the signature check compares each form on its own and a form that matches an overload is no mismatch. A list `params` now holds the members of one parameter list, one per item, never one form per item, and `validate-inventory.py` exits 2 on a list of two or more items one of which holds several parameters or writes a whole form (such as `(...handlers: T[])` or `actions(...handlers: T[])`), or two of which name the same parameter, naming the entry and the items, so the reader is re-dispatched with that violation. A generic function type (`fn: <T, U>(x: T) => U`), a numpy docstring member's `, optional` marker and a Rust lifetime (`&'a str`) are read as part of one member, and the violation also offers the whole list as one string. Before, the inventory contract said to list a name once per place and never defined a list `params`, so a reader could record oms-storybook-react-vite's two `actions` overloads as one entry whose items the scripts joined into one parameter list that matched neither overload: a Critical `signature-mismatch` that failed the hard gate and told Update Skill to rewrite correct documentation. A run whose reader writes such a list twice now halts `inventory-invalid`. ([#1058](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1058); issue [#1043](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1043))

  **Migration:** If Test Skill halts `inventory-invalid` on a list `params` it refused, run Test Skill again: the skill under test needs no change.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's inventory now records a table that documents one function's, method's or class constructor's parameters (`| Param | Type | Default | Description |`, or with a Required column) as an entry of its own, at the heading or caption above it that writes the name, its rows one parameter list of `param: Type` members in row order with no default, Required or `?` mark. A table under a heading that already writes the name's form adds no entry there, so that heading keeps one form, bound to the declaration its citation names. The split-body cross-check now reads such a table as a typed form, and so does the scored signature check for a function's or a class constructor's table (it compares no method, so a method's table is recorded but never scored): a parameter the source lacks, a contradicted type or a required parameter left out is a mismatch, and an optional parameter the table leaves out is an `omitted-optional` difference, Critical unless the table is labelled partial in its column header, its caption or the nearest heading above it (such as `### Key parameters`); optionality is not compared. Before, the inventory contract named only props tables, so one reader compared such a table and another recorded nothing for it, and two strict runs of the same skill could reach different verdicts. This can block a skill that passed. ([#1058](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1058); issue [#1002](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1002))

  **Migration:** If Test Skill now stops at the hard gate on a parameter table, correct the parameter names or types the source contradicts, add the required parameters it leaves out, and add the optional parameters it leaves out or label the table partial in its column header or the heading above it (for example `### Key parameters`), then run Test Skill again.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's inventory contract now says how far a table column's partial label reaches, as the inventory floor reads one. A label labels every form its column's cells write, a usage form and another name's form included, but only when it is the whole header, such as `Key params`, or stands in parentheses after its word, such as `Props (simplified)`, so a `Purpose and key params` column labels none. A form that writes only a return type carries no label, and an ellipsis labels a call partial only as an argument of its own, never as an argument's value such as `api_key=...`. Before, oh-my-skills rehearsal readers labelled the same forms partial on one run and full on the next, which decides whether a left-out optional parameter is an Info observation or a Critical `signature-mismatch`. This can block a skill that passed: a form in a column headed with other words around its label, such as `Purpose and key params`, which readers often labelled partial, is now full, so an optional parameter it leaves out is a Critical `signature-mismatch` instead of an Info observation. ([#1060](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1060); issues [#997](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/997), [#1029](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1029))

  **Migration:** If Test Skill now stops at the hard gate on a `signature-mismatch` for a form in such a column, head the column `Key params` or put the label in parentheses after its word, such as `Purpose (key params)`, or write the form in full, then run Test Skill again.

- **skf-test-skill:** Where a skill states members several names share once and places one of a name's own members before or among them (`leading`, `first`), Test Skill's inventory now records that name's whole parameter list in the skill's order at a place the inventory floor pins too, as it already did everywhere else. Before, the pinned parameters stayed after the shared text and `; `, which the signature rules read with the shared members first, so a correct order could be reported as a Critical `signature-mismatch` that blocks the hard gate. `validate-inventory.py --floor` now carries a pinned `params` when the members of the entry whose `at` is that place, cut at the commas outside brackets and strings, hold each pinned member in its order, with other members before, among or after them. A list that reorders, changes or drops a pinned member is still refused, a longer list the skill writes at another place, or one with no `at`, is another form that never carries the pin, the shared text then `; ` is still carried, and a pinned `usage_signature` is still carried only as given or after the shared text and `; `. A skill that passed can now block when it places an own member first at a pinned place while the source declares it after the shared members. ([#1057](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1057); issue [#1028](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1028))

  **Migration:** If a run now stops at the hard gate on a `signature-mismatch` for a pinned form whose own member the skill places before or among the shared members, correct the order in the skill to the one the source declares, then run Test Skill again.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's inventory contract and signature comparison rules now read four shapes of a call in running text or a table's description cell one way, where oh-my-skills rehearsal readers split. A placeholder call `name(...)`, which passes no argument, is a mention, as `name()` is. An empty call followed by a return type, such as `run_migrations() -> list[str]`, is a signature with an empty parameter list. A list that writes a bare `*` or `/`, such as `register_memo_key_function(typ, key_fn, *, state_fn=None)`, stays a parameter list, since no call writes one. A call after `await`, `new`, an assignment, a receiver or a module path stays a call when a return type follows it, so cocoindex's `await coco.mount([subpath,] processor_fn, *args, **kwargs) -> ComponentMountHandle` is no longer read as bare parameter names, which made `[subpath,]` a parameter the source lacks and could raise a Critical `signature-mismatch`. A usage is now recorded as the inventory floor writes one, its assignment, `await`, `new`, receiver or module path kept through the call's closing parenthesis, never an `@` or a `with`, and a field the floor pins blank is left out when the place writes none. Two of these readings can block a skill that passed: `run_migrations() -> list[str]` in prose now claims the export takes no parameter, so a required parameter the source takes is a Critical `signature-mismatch`, and a list with a bare `*`, such as `register_memo_key_function(typ, key_fn, *, state_fn=None)`, is now compared by its parameter names, so a name the source spells otherwise, or an optional parameter it leaves out, can be a Critical gap where a call was no difference. ([#1060](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1060); issues [#1014](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1014), [#1016](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1016))

  **Migration:** If Test Skill now stops at the hard gate on a `signature-mismatch` for a form a skill writes in running text or a description cell, such as `name() -> T` or a list with a bare `*` or `/`, write the parameters in that form as the source declares them, or drop the return type after an empty `name()` that only mentions the export, then run Test Skill again.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill now reads a documented table row's own citations in its cells alone. The signature plan read the `[AST:]` and `[SRC:]` citations on the line after a form's place unless that line wrote the same name, so a row also took the citations of the next row, which documents another export: a row that cited its own declaration could name two declarations and be left unbound, and a row with no citation was bound to the declaration the next row cites and compared with it alone, which could record a false Critical `signature-mismatch` gap. A table row outside a fenced block now reads no line after it, a line after the table included, while a heading, a prose line and a form in a fenced block read the next line as before. For cocoindex, the `Settings` row that cites its declaration in `_internal/setting.py` is now bound to it, where the `ServerSettings` row's citation, which falls in the same-named `cocoindex.setting.Settings` class, left it unbound. This can block a skill that passed: a row whose own citation names one declaration no longer matches through another. ([#1057](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1057); issue [#998](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/998))

  **Migration:** If a skill now stops at the hard gate on a table row compared with the declaration its own citation names, correct the form, or the citation when it points at the wrong declaration, then run Test Skill again. A row that relied on a citation written on the line after it, or after its table, takes that citation into one of its cells.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's Type Coverage now counts a public name the recipes give no kind at its file, such as one no recipe found (an extraction gap, listed in the surface's `extractionGaps`), when the skill's provenance map gives that name a type kind at that file, as it already did for a name the stale-scope guard restored. Before, such a name had no kind and Type Coverage left it out with no warning, so the type count depended on how a name reached the surface: on oms-cocoindex, once the brief's include globs were fixed, six type aliases the guard had restored became extraction gaps, and Type Coverage counted 36 types instead of 42 on an unchanged skill. The Type Coverage warning the report lists now names each extraction gap still without a kind, and any other name the extraction records with none, beside the restored names it already named, in place of the warning that the source has no types. The names of a fallback per-file scan are read as before. An undocumented type among these names now lowers Type Coverage and is reported as a Medium `missing-type` gap instead of a `missing-export` one, so a run that passed can fail. ([#1053](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1053); issue [#1020](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1020))

  **Migration:** Re-run Test Skill at Forge or Deep tier, then document in SKILL.md each type a new `Missing type` gap names.

### Added

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's inventory reader and its signature judges now record each reading the inventory contract or the signature comparison rules leave open in an `undecided` list (`export`, `at`, `rule`, `reading`, and `other_gap`, what the other reading would give), and the Coverage Analysis section lists them under Borderline Calls, so a report names each open reading its PASS or FAIL rests on. `validate-inventory.py` and `score-signatures.py` check the list: an item that is no object, or one with a blank `export`, `rule`, `reading`, `other_gap` or `at`, is dropped and named in their `warnings`, never a reason to send the reader or judge back or to halt the run. `inventory.json`, `coverage.json` and `signatures.json` carry the list, and the stack branch's reconcile command now reads `inventory.json` too. Before, a verdict that rested on such a reading was published without naming it, and only a run told to list them by hand showed them. The list changes no gap or score. ([#1058](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1058); issue [#1021](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1021))

### Changed

- **all workflows:** A health-check finding's fingerprint now includes a defect key: one to four lower-case words that name the thing the fix would change, such as a function, a flag or a rule, in the step file's or the code's own words (`floor-check`, `orphan-action`), or for a missing rule the case it should cover. The fingerprint hashed only the severity, workflow, step file and section, so two different defects of one severity in one section got the same fingerprint, and the dedup Action closed the later report as a duplicate of the earlier one: Test Skill's `inventory-contract.md`, which has a single heading, had only three fingerprints in all, one per severity. Each issue now records its section, its defect key and its section fingerprint (the same hash without the key), so anyone can recompute it. Opening a new issue anyway at an exact match now means naming the defect more specifically, since an issue under the same fingerprint would be closed. When no open issue has the same fingerprint, the health check searches for the section fingerprint, which finds issues filed by an SKF version whose fingerprints carry no defect key and reports from the same section under another key, and it still reads seen-cache records written by such a version. Such a match is a possible match only: the health check shows the issue with the usual choices to react, comment, open a new issue or skip, and never skips a finding or upvotes an issue on that match alone; a fixed issue found that way is linked in a `## Regression` section as a possible regression, without the REGRESSION title marker. Independent reports of one defect often name it by different keys, so the dedup Action also reads the section fingerprint: when a new issue matches no open issue's fingerprint but another open health-check issue records the same section fingerprint under a different key, or was filed without a key and carries it as its label, the Action links each one in a comment and adds a `possible-duplicate` label, and closes nothing. The key drops every character that is not an ASCII letter or digit, so `reader's own code` and `readers own code` give one key. ([#982](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/982))
- **skf-quick-skill, skf-create-skill, skf-update-skill, skf-create-stack-skill:** Quick Skill, Create Skill, Update Skill and Create Stack Skill now report what the security scan finds. skill-check 1.2.0 runs the scanner without `--ci`, writes its `--format json` output before the scan starts and counts as findings only codes like `[E001]`, which snyk-agent-scan 0.6 never prints for a risk, so a scan that found a prompt-injection risk read `pass`, and so did one whose analysis failed on a rejected token (HTTP 401) or the daily limit (HTTP 429). The four workflows now run skill-check with `--no-security-scan` and run the scan through the new `skf-security-scan.py`, which, when `SNYK_TOKEN` is set, runs `uvx snyk-agent-scan@0.6.11 --json --skills <package>` and reads the scanner's own JSON report. Each risk it reports is recorded as an advisory warning with its score and evidence, and `security_result` reads `warn`. `pass` now means the scanner analysed the package and reported no risk. An analysis error, a scanner that fails or runs past 110 seconds, or no `uvx` reads `skipped` with the reason. The scan now runs whether or not skill-check is available, so with `SNYK_TOKEN` set the skill package is sent to Snyk's analysis server in that case too. Create Stack Skill's `skill-check-unavailable` warning no longer says the scan was skipped, Create Skill no longer suggests putting `SNYK_TOKEN` in `.env`, which neither tool reads, and the CLI tool report lists `snyk-agent-scan` as `optional, runs through uvx`. ([#1052](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1052); issue [#892](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/892))
- **skf-test-skill:** After a fallback per-file scan, Test Skill's split-body cross-check no longer settles a pair by the one declaration the scan recorded. That scan never looks for a same-named declaration no entry point exports, yet its `surface.json` wrote `otherDeclarations` as `[]`, which the split-body Source read as "there is none", so a correct form documenting another function of the same name (such as cognee's lightweight `run_pipeline`) could be named the contradicted side, with a remediation citing the recorded declaration as settling it. `surface.json` now writes `otherDeclarations` as `null` when no runner extraction looked for them (no extraction, or one the fallback scan replaces, with or without the runner's JSON), and the one declaration decides only when the list is a list. Such a `split-body-mismatch` gap stays High, with its Source at the reference line and a remediation that says no source settled it, as a full extraction of the same tree already gives. A full extraction still writes a list, `[]` when it finds none. ([#1054](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1054); issue [#1026](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1026))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's split-body cross-check reads the forms one file writes for one name as an overload set (Python `@overload` stubs or TS bodiless signatures, with the implementation after them when the file writes it) as one documented set, the way it reads an overload set in the source: a form in the other file that matches the implementation or any stub, or whose parameter types are, position by position, the unions of the stubs' types, is no mismatch, and the set's own forms are never compared with each other or with its implementation. Before, a correct SKILL.md form that defaults a parameter could be compared with one documented stub that requires it and read as a High `split-body-mismatch` gap, which blocks the hard gate and tells Update Skill to rewrite a correct stub, so two runs on an unchanged skill could disagree. ([#1054](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1054); issue [#1017](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1017))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's split-body cross-check no longer compares a leading receiver (`self`, `cls`, `&self`, `&'a self`, `&mut self`, `mut self`, `this: T`) that one documented form writes and the other leaves out: neither form is the source, so each form's own leading receiver is dropped before the two are compared, and `execute(args, kwargs, next_batch_size=None)` matches `execute(self, args, kwargs, next_batch_size=None)`. Before, a method written with its receiver in one file and without it in another could read as a High `split-body-mismatch` gap, which blocks the hard gate and tells Update Skill to edit a correct reference file, so two runs on an unchanged skill could disagree. Each form is still compared with the source, where a receiver the source does not take stays a mismatch. ([#1054](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1054); issue [#1045](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1045))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's documented inventory now leaves out a name the skill presents only as a local import alias of another name (such as `GridCellType` in "which `grid-cell.tsx` imports as `GridCellType`"), or says the source does not export, unless the skill also writes it in an export table's first cell, a heading, a fenced declaration or a place the inventory floor lists. A code span in prose or a description cell no longer gives such a name an entry, so accurate prose no longer records a Medium `stale-documentation` gap for an alias or an Info documented extra for an unexported type, and two readers of the same skill record the same gaps. ([#1058](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1058); issue [#1008](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1008))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's inventory contract now says that a call or JSX element a fenced example writes, such as storybook's `defineMain({ ... })` or `withThemeFromJSXProvider({ ... })`, gives the name no inventory entry when the skill also writes that name's form outside its examples, in a heading, a table row, a props table, running text or a fenced declaration, unless the nearest heading above the example names a usage, such as `## Usage`, where a bold label line such as `**Usage:**` is no heading. Before, the contract did not say, so one reader recorded such a call as a usage form of its own and the next did not, and two runs of one skill compared different forms. Such an example is no longer compared, so an example that drops a required argument is no longer a `signature-mismatch` gap of its own, and a name whose only forms are in fenced examples keeps them. ([#1057](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1057); issue [#997](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/997))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill no longer records a Medium `stale-documentation` gap, with advice to update or remove the documentation, for a name the skill documents at a file whose `export *` or `export type *` from another package no script reads, such as a `@vitest/spy` type cited at a file that holds `export type * from '@vitest/spy'`. The run met each such star in the recipe runner's output, in quick mode's `unlisted` records or in a per-file result's `unresolved_stars`, but listed it only in Coverage Analysis, so the gap ledger could not tell a name passed on through it from a removed one. The run's `surface.json` now lists each such star in `unresolvedStars`, and a stale name that no source file declares and that the skill's citations place at a file holding one is an Info `observation` titled `Not checked by script: {name} (another package's export *)`, at the line that documents it, which names the star and asks no change unless that package lacks the name; a Deep-tier hand-written `Not checked by script: {name}` at that line stays a gap of its own. A name cited at any other file, one the brief scopes out and a fabricated signature keep their gaps. ([#1059](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1059); issue [#1005](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1005))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's Coverage Analysis section now lists the public names no recipe found (the surface's `extractionGaps`) on an `Extraction Gaps` line of its Coverage Summary, each at its file and line, and lists one with no file (the runner's trace reached no file for it) as `not located`. The Forge tier's coverage check no longer asks the run to read these declarations by eye: the signature comparison already judges each one with a file that the skill documents with a form, and nothing used the by-eye read. A documented gap with no file still has no file for its judge to read, as before. Before, a run that followed the step read every gap declaration (16 on oms-cocoindex) without changing any score, and a gap with no file reached the report only when the run chose to list it. Scores do not change. ([#1053](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1053); issue [#1048](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1048))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's documented inventory now gives a `const` that a place writes only as the call that builds its function, such as `const badgeVariants = cva(…)`, with no parameter list, function type or return type of its own, no `params`, `return_type` or `usage_signature` at that place, so that place is never compared: the call is the factory's form, not the const's. A call expression is now a usage form only of the name it calls, so `cva(…)` after an assignment is never recorded as the const's usage. A component keeps the declaration form the skill writes for it, and a const written with its own parameter list, function type or return type keeps its function form. Two strict runs on the same skill now compare the same names, and such a const is no longer compared as one that takes no parameter, which recorded a false Critical `signature-mismatch` when the function it holds takes one. ([#1058](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1058); issue [#1019](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1019))
- **skf-test-skill:** `score-signatures.py plan`, `validate-inventory.py` and the `census`, `floor`, `metadata` and `surface` commands of `load-coverage-inputs.py` now print only a summary when they are given `--output`, since Test Skill reads the plan, the inventory, the floor and the surface from the files they write in the run folder. `plan` prints the number of signatures it compares, the number of files and checks, the number of documented signatures and the path it wrote. `validate-inventory.py` keeps `valid`, `violations`, `warnings`, its counts, `spotCheck` and `floor`, leaves out the inventory and its `completeness`, and gives the path of `inventory.json` as `output`, or null when it refuses the inventory. `surface` prints the number of records, `denominator`, the `extraction` fields `readByEye`, `unread` and `fallback`, the `extractionGaps` it lists for a by-eye reading and the path; `census` prints `docsOnly`, `floor` prints its `summary`, and `metadata` the skill type, the inflation signature and a stack's denominator, each with the path. They used to print the whole result as well, so every run put a second copy of the inventory and the floor into the agent's context, and every source-based run one of the plan and the surface too, several hundred KB on a large skill, which ran past the tool output limit. Without `--output` each still prints the whole result, and no score, verdict or gap changes. ([#1055](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1055); issues [#1018](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1018), [#1040](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1040))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's documented inventory now leaves out a name the skill writes only in a sentence saying the skill does not cover it, such as "out of scope for this skill" or "not covered here", whatever form that sentence writes the name in. Any other place that documents the name, such as prose or a description cell that calls or describes it, or a place the inventory floor lists, still gives it an entry. An accurate scoping sentence no longer records a Medium `stale-documentation` gap telling update-skill to remove it, and two readers of the same skill record the same gaps. Where Export Coverage counts the inventory's names (the barrel branch, and the scalar branch when it counts its set or looks the documented names up), a name the source exports and the brief keeps in scope now counts as undocumented when only such a sentence names it. A stack skill's count and the verified count of a padded declared count still look names up in the skill's text, so there such a name still counts as documented. ([#1058](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1058); issue [#1013](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1013))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's documented inventory now records a function or a class the skill writes as a call with arguments in running text or a description cell, such as `add(componentName, options)` with no `await`, `new`, assignment or receiver before it, whole in `usage_signature`, and the signature check reads it as a call: each argument stands for the parameter at its position, so its names are not compared with the declaration's. Before, no rule placed such a call, so one reader recorded it as a usage and another as a list of bare names in `params`, which gave an argument named differently from its parameter a Low `signature-mismatch` gap in a TS/JS export and a Critical one, failing the hard gate, in a Python export. A call there that writes a parameter type, a return type or a `?` is still a signature, recorded in `params`. A `const` holding a function written as such a call is recorded the same way, and a class's parameter list in a Signature cell, such as `Note(content, title=None)`, stays in `params`. ([#1058](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1058); issue [#1016](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1016))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill no longer compares a function or class an example defines with the library export of the same name when its fenced block decorates it with that export, passes it to that export or registers it through it, whatever else the block defines, as in oms-cocoindex's `@coco.lifespan` over `async def lifespan(builder: coco.EnvironmentBuilder):`, unless the inventory floor pins a signature there: that definition is the reader's own code, so its entry carries no form and records no gap. A decorator that is an attribute of the export, such as a property's `@x.setter`, still leaves the definition a form. The reader's-own-code rule now lists these triggers and the block that also defines names the skill does not document as its only ones, so one reader no longer leaves such a definition out while the next records a Critical `signature-mismatch` that fails the run. ([#1058](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1058); issue [#1010](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1010))
- **skf-test-skill:** The Remediation Summary in Test Skill's Gap Report now fills each row's Estimated Effort from the gaps that row counts: each of their categories, in the order its first gap comes, as `{category} ({count}): {action}`, where it used to give one fixed text per severity. A Medium row whose only gap was a `metadata-drift` gap asked to add type definitions, interface docs or the missing section, while the gap itself asked to re-run Create Skill; that row now reads `metadata-drift (1): re-run Create Skill or edit the brief's scope, as each remediation says`, with a note that counts which differ only by `Type::method` entries need no fix. A row with no gaps still reads `None`, the column header and each gap's own entry are unchanged, and no verdict, score, gap or Update Skill routing changes. ([#1059](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1059); issue [#1047](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1047))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's documented inventory now gives no entry to a form the skill marks as removed or as the form of a version before the one it covers, such as an old call in a migration table's old-version column or a cell labelled gone, removed, before or old, whether or not the covered version still exports the name: the current form beside it is that place's entry, and the old form is never compared. Before, the inventory contract did not say whether such a cell was a form of the current export, so one reader left out oms-cocoindex's `Settings(database=...)` in a `v0.3.37 (gone)` column while a reader following the contract literally could record it, a call passing a keyword the 1.0.0 class lacks: a Critical `signature-mismatch` that fails the hard gate, or, for a name the covered version no longer exports, a Medium `stale-documentation` gap that tells Update Skill to delete an accurate historical row. Such an old form beside the current one is no longer read as a second form that unbinds the current one from its citation. A form marked only deprecated and still present in the covered version is still compared, and so is a form the inventory floor pins. ([#1058](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1058); issue [#1038](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1038))
- **skf-test-skill, skf-update-skill:** When Test Skill's split-body cross-check flags two forms of a name the source declares more than once (in a second file, or as a same-named declaration no entry point exports), such as core's and the React renderer's `composeStory`, and each form matches a different one of those declarations, the `split-body-mismatch` gap's remediation no longer has Update Skill copy one side's form over the other. For each side it names the form's file and line and the declaration that form matches, and asks for that declaration's `[SRC:]` citation beside the form, with its module or owner named, so the next run tells the two forms apart. Update Skill's `--from-test-report` run adds those citations and changes neither form. The gap stays High, with its Source at the reference line and the Reference Consistency table's Contradicted Side `not settled`, and every other pair keeps its remediation. Before, Update Skill rewrote a form that was right for its own declaration to match the other declaration's. ([#1054](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1054); issue [#1027](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1027))

### Fixed

- **all workflows, skf-forger:** Every workflow, and Ferris, now keeps its subagents in the foreground in Claude Code: the rule tells the agent to pass `run_in_background: false` on every Agent call, since Claude Code runs a subagent in the background when the flag is left out. The rule used to say only "never with `run_in_background`", so an Agent call that followed it word for word could start its subagent in the background, and the run then spent turns polling for the result to keep a headless `claude -p` turn from ending before the subagent did. ([#1055](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1055); issue [#1037](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1037))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill now reads and keeps an inventory entry's blank `params` (`""` or `[]`) one way. The signature comparison rules read it as an empty list of bare names: it claims the export takes none, so a required parameter the source takes is a mismatch, while an optional one is no difference, as for a heading's empty call such as `### connect()` against `def connect(host="localhost", port=5432)`. Before, the rules said only that it claims the export takes none, so a judge could grade that heading a Critical `omitted-optional` mismatch that another judge, and `score-signatures.py`, read as a match. `score-signatures.py plan` now also keeps a blank `params` over an entry with no `params` whatever either's `signature_form` label, so a partial `f() -> R` beside a full return-only form of `f` is compared; before, the return-only form stood and the claim that `f` takes no argument was never checked. ([#1060](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1060); issue [#1025](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1025))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's signature rules now say what a Python call's unpacking argument passes: a `*items` argument can pass every parameter a caller may pass by position from its position on, and a `**mapping` argument every one a caller may pass by name, so a documented `Settings(**config)` matches a constructor `__init__(self, host, port)`. The rules said only what a JSX spread or a TS/JS `...args` passes, so a judge that read `Settings(**config)` literally found no required parameter passed and raised a Critical `signature-mismatch` gap on the correct form, failing the hard gate. The arguments a call writes beside an unpacking are still compared, so `Settings(**config, debug=True)` is still a mismatch when the constructor takes neither `debug` nor `**kwargs`, and a `*items` never passes a keyword-only parameter, nor a `**mapping` a positional-only one. A call written with placeholder names, such as `coco.mount([subpath,] process_fn, *args, **kwargs)`, reads its `*args` and `**kwargs` the same way. ([#1056](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1056); issue [#1024](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1024))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's signature rules now read a type name with or without the module or namespace path it is written through, when both name one declaration: a documented `Environment` matches the source's `environment.Environment` written after `from . import environment`, as `ZodType` matches `z.ZodType` and `ndarray` matches `np.ndarray`. The rules named only a `typing.`, `collections.abc.` or `React.` prefix, so a judge that read that list as closed raised a Critical `signature-mismatch` gap on a correct form and failed the hard gate. Two declarations that only share a name stay two types. Test Skill's scoring script reads a type's own name with or without its module path too when it checks the facts of a mismatch tagged `annotation-contradicted`, so such a mismatch whose parameters write a type through a module path on one side only is now an Info `observation` instead of a Critical gap; it compares two different module paths, a `Literal[...]` value and a Rust `::` path as written, and inside a callable's arrow type it still drops only those three prefixes. ([#1056](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1056); issue [#999](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/999))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's signature rules now read overloaded constructors and variadic parameters in Java, Kotlin, C# and C++ as they read Python's and TS/JS's. A class in one of these languages is compared with every constructor it declares, as one overload set, so a documented `new Client("localhost", 8080)` matches `Client(String host, int port)` beside `Client(String host)`, and overloaded methods and functions there are one set too. Java's `T...`, C#'s `params T[]`, Kotlin's `vararg` and a C or C++ `...` now take the extra arguments a call passes, as Go's `...T` does, and each of them, Go's included, is optional, so `new Command("ls", "-l", "-a")` and `new Command("ls")` both match `Command(String name, String... args)`. The rules named only the forms of Python, TS/JS and Go, so a judge of the fallback per-file scan, which reads these languages, could raise a Critical `signature-mismatch` gap on a correct form and fail the hard gate. ([#1056](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1056); issue [#1023](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1023))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's `score-signatures.py score` now reads a Kotlin `vararg` parameter and a C or C++ `...` in the source as optional, as the signature comparison rules do, when it checks the parameter fact of an `annotation-contradicted` mismatch. A list of bare names such as `log(name): String` against `fun log(name: String, vararg args: Any): Any` writes the same parameters, so a correct tag is now graded Info. Before, the scorer read `vararg args` as one required parameter and failed the fact, so the mismatch stayed a Critical `signature-mismatch` that blocks the hard gate. ([#1060](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1060); issue [#1023](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1023))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's signature rules now read a parameter's or prop's type written with `/` between types as the union it spells, since a table's Type cell cannot hold a bare `|`: `str / list[str] / None` matches the source's `str | list[str] | None`, while a `/` written alone in a parameter list stays the positional-only marker. A parameter's or prop's type written as a description is read as a return type already was: a description followed by a type (`Pydantic BaseModel`) states that type, and text that names no type (`Union (many)`) states none, so it is not compared. Before, a judge that read either cell as written raised a Critical `signature-mismatch` gap on a correct table and failed the hard gate. Test Skill's scoring script reads a `/` between types as `|` too when it checks the facts of a mismatch tagged `annotation-contradicted`, so such a mismatch whose parameters write a union with `/` on one side only is now an Info `observation` instead of a Critical gap; it still compares a type written as a description as written. ([#1056](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1056); issue [#1003](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1003))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's split-body cross-check now settles a pair of a method's forms by the method itself. The reader gives the pair the method's `owner` (`agents` for `agents.get`), and the Source reads the member of that name the owner's class body declares, from the owner's record in `surface.json`, or the function a namespace object binds it to (`session.add_feedback`, a keyword of the `types.SimpleNamespace(...)` call that builds `session`), so a `split-body-mismatch` gap cites the side that declaration contradicts and its remediation cites the member's file and line. Before, `surface.json` records no class member, so every method pair said no source settled it and had Update Skill copy the other side's form, even over a reference line that matches the source, and a root export of the same bare name (`cognee.delete` beside `agents.delete`) could settle the pair against the wrong declaration. A record of the bare name never stands in for the member: with no record of the owner, no such member it declares or binds, or no `owner` on a pair of a name the inventory lists only as a method, the pair stays unsettled. Methods of one name on different owners (`agents.get`, `datasets.get`) are two methods, and their forms are never a pair. ([#1054](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1054); issue [#1035](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1035))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's split-body cross-check now reads the several declarations a reference file writes for a name overloaded in Java, Kotlin, C# or C++ as one documented overload set, as the signature comparison rules already read such declarations in the source. A reference that writes `Client(String host)` and `Client(String host, int port)` beside a SKILL.md body's `new Client("localhost", 8080)` is no mismatch. Before, the split-body paragraph read such forms as one set while the documented-set sentence named only Python `@overload` stubs and TypeScript bodiless signatures, so one reader compared the call with each constructor alone and recorded a High `split-body-mismatch` that blocks the hard gate, and another recorded nothing. ([#1060](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1060); issues [#1017](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1017), [#1023](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1023))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's split-body cross-check now reads a parameter type one documented form writes that names some of the members of the other form's union as agreeing with it, in either direction, as such a type agrees with the source's union: a table's `node_name: list[str]` matches a fenced `node_name: list[str] | None = None` of the same export. The rules stated that reading only against the source, so a judge that read it as no rule between two documented forms raised a High `split-body-mismatch` gap on a consistent pair and failed the hard gate, while another passed the same skill. Return types are compared as before. ([#1056](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1056); issue [#1015](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1015))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's documented inventory now records a name that a row or a paragraph lists bare beside members it states once for several names, such as `.get` in a namespace row that lists `.create`, `.get` and `.delete`, each with an optional `user`, and links to their signatures, as a mention at that place: its entry leaves `params`, `return_type` and `usage_signature` out, and the split-body cross-check compares no form of it there. Before, the inventory contract did not say whether such a name took the shared text as its form, so one reader gave each name the shared phrase alone, a partial form that leaves out every required parameter, and recorded High `split-body-mismatch` and Critical `signature-mismatch` gaps that failed the hard gate, while another recorded none on the same skill. The shared text still goes to each name the place gives members of its own, and the name's forms at other places are compared as before. A whole parameter list, call or signature a place writes once for every name it lists, such as one Signature cell for a row whose first cell lists `get` and `head`, is no shared text: it stays each name's own form there and is still compared. ([#1058](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1058); issue [#1034](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1034))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill no longer records a Medium `stale-documentation` gap for a documented name that the source declares once inside the brief's scope when a copy of its file lies outside it, such as a docs app in a monorepo that keeps its own copy of a provider file. `classify-stale` in `skf-verify-provenance-completeness.py` had no brief input, so when the provenance map spans several packages its walk read the whole repository and counted the copy that a `scope.exclude` glob matches, or that no `scope.include` glob covers, as a second declaration; with no single declaring file, the report asked the author to update or remove accurate documentation. With its new `--brief` flag, which Test Skill now passes when the skill has a brief, a file the brief scopes out no longer counts as a declaration when a file in the brief's scope declares the name, so the name is an Info `Documented extra: {name}` at its one declaration in scope. A file the provenance map cites for the name still settles it wherever it lies, a rename that clears a fabricated signature is still found in any file, and a name declared only in files the brief scopes out keeps those declarations, so its gap is the same as without the flag. ([#1059](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1059); issue [#1007](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1007))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's discovery check now routes only prompts that describe the task in a user's own words: a prompt taken from the skill's `SKILL.md` or written by the check when `SKILL.md` has too few names no export, no skill name and no library or package name, and the short "run the ... thing on this data" pattern now takes a plain word for the job, such as memory or indexing. Before, only the prompts taken from `SKILL.md` were asked to leave out the skill name, and a written prompt could name an export that the skill's catalog description lists, so the router picked the skill on that literal name and Discovery could score `3/3 PASS` or `2/3 WARN` for a description that misroutes realistic requests. Such a description now records the Medium or High `discovery` gap it should. A discovery gap still blocks nothing and changes no score or verdict. ([#1055](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1055); issue [#1049](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1049))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's discovery subagents now pick a skill for each prompt from the catalog alone: they are spawned without file or shell tools where the platform allows it, and their instruction tells them to read no file and use no tool. They used to keep the default file and shell tools at the project root, where the run lock `.test-skill.lock` and the in-progress report `.skf-test-report-{skill_name}-{run_id}.md` in the skill's version folder both name the skill under test, so a subagent that looked around could route every prompt to it and score Discovery `3/3 PASS` for a description whose triggers misroute. Such a description now records the Medium or High `discovery` gap it should. A discovery gap still blocks nothing and changes no score or verdict. ([#1055](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1055); issue [#1039](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1039))
- **skf-test-skill:** A stale name's gap in Test Skill's Gap Report now cites the line that documents the name when the skill writes it only as a module path, such as `cognee.exceptions` for `exceptions`: a code span, a heading or an export table's first cell that is a dotted path whose last segment is the name, after a call's `(` is cut (`pkg.connect(url)`), and whose first segment is a module the skill's code blocks import (`import cognee`, `from cognee.x import y`, `import a.b as c` or `import * as ns from`), now documents it. Such a name's Medium gap used to cite a bare `SKILL.md` and ask to update or remove its documentation there, and each of its gaps had an Issue that read "the skill documents"; its Source, Issue and remediation now name that line, and the Issue of a documented extra opens with it too: oms-cognee's `exceptions` and `migration`, documented extras at their packages, now have Issues that open with their module headings, `SKILL.md:286` and `SKILL.md:185`. Such a code span ranks below one that is the name itself and above a declaration in a fenced code block; a path that ends in another name, one written among other words, and one through a receiver or a type (`client.connect(url)`, `Client.connect`, `store.state`) still document nothing. Scores, the hard gate and the gap count are unchanged. ([#1059](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1059); issue [#1011](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1011))
- **skf-test-skill:** A stale name's gap in Test Skill's Gap Report now cites the line that documents the export when the skill writes it module-qualified, not an earlier line whose code span only mentions the bare name, such as a confidence note or a "not covered here" disclaimer. A heading or an export table's first cell whose code span or text is a dotted path from a module the skill's code blocks import, ending in the name (`cognee.run_migrations`), once a leading `new ` and everything from `(`, `<` or `[` are cut, now ranks with a heading of the name, and a code span that calls the name after an assignment, `await`, `new` or such a module (`await cognee.wait_for_background_tasks()`, `x = get(key)`) ranks with a code span of the name. oms-cognee's `run_migrations` and `wait_for_background_tasks` gaps used to cite a Confidence bullet in `SKILL.md` and a disclaimer in `references/full-api-reference.md`, and their remediations asked to remove the documentation there; their Source, Issue and remediation now name the `cognee.run_migrations` Key API row (`SKILL.md:148`) and the row that writes `await cognee.wait_for_background_tasks()` (`SKILL.md:157`). Within each rank the first file, then the lowest line, still wins, and a call with a space or type arguments before its `(`, a type's method row (`Client.connect()`) and an instance's call (`client.connect(url)`) still document nothing. Scores, the hard gate and the gap count are unchanged. ([#1059](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1059); issue [#1041](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1041))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's inventory contract now settles three places oh-my-skills rehearsal readers read two ways. A heading names a usage when its text holds the word usage, whatever qualifies it, such as `### Usage pattern` or `### Per-test-file usage`, so a fenced call under it is compared on every run. A call or JSX element of a component that a props table row's cell writes, such as `<Canvas of={ButtonStories.Primary} />`, is an example of that prop, not a usage of its own. A comment line in a fenced block is no place and states no form or return type, so a typed form or a return written only in a comment, such as `# returns the dataset's PipelineRunInfo`, is no longer compared by one run and skipped by the next. ([#1060](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1060); issue [#997](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/997))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's inventory contract now gives a name the skill writes with no form one place. An entry with no compared form, such as a type or class entry, gives its place as `at`, as one with a form does (a `method` and a form that writes only a return type aside), so a stale name's gap cites the line that documents it on every run: oms-uitripled's `UILibraryContextValue`, written only as `type UILibraryContextValue = {` in a fence, cited `references/setup.md:90` on one run and a bare `SKILL.md` on the next, depending on whether the reader added an `at` the contract did not ask for. A place that writes a name with no form, members or fields, such as a mention, an import or a heading, now gives no entry when another place gives the name one, unless the inventory floor gives that place, and of several such places of a name the skill documents, where no other place gives it an entry, the first alone gives one, so readers no longer list such places differently. This does not change which names count as documented. The contract's example now shows a class and a type entry with an `at`. ([#1060](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1060); issue [#1006](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1006))
- **skf-test-skill:** `validate-inventory.py --floor` no longer refuses the partial label of a second form a pinned row writes. A `Signature` cell such as `run(task: Task)` or `run(task: Task, ...)` is pinned by its first form, with no label, and the inventory contract gives the row one entry per form, the second labelled `"partial"` by its own `...`. The validator read that longer list as a copy of the pinned form and refused its label as one the floor does not pin, so a reader that followed the contract was re-dispatched and a second refusal halted the run with `inventory-invalid`. A list that a `...` makes longer than the pinned form, and that the entry labels `"partial"` where the pin gives no label, is now another form, which keeps its own label and never stands in for the pinned form's copy. Unlabelled, such a list is still the pinned form's copy, the whole list in the skill's order with the shared members spelled out and a `...` among them, and a labelled copy of the pinned form itself is still refused. The inventory contract now says so. ([#1060](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1060); issues [#1043](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1043), [#1028](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1028), [#1029](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1029))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill no longer records a Medium `stale-documentation` gap for a Python package the skill documents by its import path when the skill's citations name both the package's `__init__.py` and the module of the same name inside it, such as `pkg/errors/__init__.py` and `pkg/errors/errors.py`. The two files are the one module that path names, but the gap ledger settled a name declared in several files only when the skill cited exactly one of them, so the report asked the author to update or remove correct documentation, and re-running Test Skill could not clear it. Citations of only a package's `__init__.py` and modules named like it directly in its folder (`NAME.py` or `NAME.pyi`) now settle on the package: the name is an Info `Documented extra: {name}` at the package's `__init__.py`, and two cited files in different packages still keep the Medium gap. ([#1059](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1059); issue [#1012](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1012))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's documented inventory now reads a function written with empty parentheses in running text or a description cell as a mention whatever comes before its name, such as `await cognee.disconnect()` after `await` or through a module path, so its entry leaves `params` and `usage_signature` out. Before, the inventory contract also recorded any call after `await`, `new` or an assignment, or through a receiver or module path, as a usage, so one reader recorded no form and another an empty call, which gave a function with a required parameter a Critical `signature-mismatch` gap on one run and none on the next. In running text or a description cell, a call expression is now a usage only when it passes an argument. An empty call in a heading, an export table's first cell, a call or signature column or a fenced example is still a form, compared as before. ([#1058](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1058); issue [#1014](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1014))
