- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill now renews its run lock each time a subagent returns (or, in an environment without subagents, each time the main thread finishes the work a subagent would have done), and again before its discovery subagents start, not only just before it writes its results. The lock goes stale 60 minutes after it was taken or last renewed, and the inventory reader, the signature judges and the discovery subagents all ran before that one renewal, so on a large skill the lock could go stale partway through a run: a second run of the same skill version started then took the lock over instead of stopping with `another-run-active`, and the first run halted at the end with no result written, losing about an hour of work. A second run now stops at the start with `another-run-active` while the first one works. A run whose lock is taken over anyway, because one subagent or step ran past 60 minutes, halts with `another-run-active` as soon as that work ends while the other run still holds the lock, with an `error.phase` such as `coverage-check:run-lock`, rather than at the end; when the other run has already ended, or let its own lock go stale, the renewal takes the lock back and the run goes on. ([#1055](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1055); issue [#1044](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1044))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's Deep-tier migration check now counts Section 4b as present only when SKILL.md has the level-2 heading `## Migration & Deprecation Warnings` exactly, the heading Create Skill emits and the other Section 4b gates match. A section under any other heading, such as `## Migration from v1`, is not Section 4b whatever it holds: with `t2_future_count: 0` it records no `migration-section` gap, and with a count above 0 the skill gets the Medium Case 1 gap for a missing Section 4b. Before, the check named the section without saying whether a retitled migration section counted, so two runs of the same skill could record different `migration-section` gaps and send Update Skill different structural fixes. ([#1058](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1058); issue [#1000](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1000))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill no longer lets the import order decide whether a documented module is scoped out by the brief when two of the package's namespaces pass on the same function from a file the brief scopes out and one of them is the module named like that function. The recipe runner wrote the function's one `entry_point_diff.outside_scope` row with whichever namespace the entry point imported first, so when the other one came first the module got a Medium `stale-documentation` gap that says to widen the brief's scope or remove correct documentation. The row now names the namespace of the function's own name when one of them has it, else the first as before, so the module is an Info documented extra in either order, and a name the source declares in the scoped-out file itself still keeps the Medium gap. ([#1059](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1059); issue [#1031](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1031))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's inventory contract now keeps the skill's prose out of a form and settles two more readings oh-my-skills rehearsal readers split on. The shared text several names' entries carry before `; ` is the members the place states once, without the words that introduce them: the contract's own example wrote `each with the base fields id, scope=Scope(); content, title=None`, which a reader copied, so the signature judge read prose as a parameter. A `type` alias, even one the skill writes as a function type, now carries no parameters or return type, and a name the skill declares with `const`, a fenced `export const` included, is a `constant` when the skill gives it no kind label. ([#1060](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1060); issues [#1034](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1034), [#1019](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1019))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's Forge-tier signature judges now know what to do with a check, a candidate or a bound declaration that the signature plan gives a null `line` and `signatureLine`, as it does for a name read by eye alone in its file (a per-file result lists names only): the judge finds the declaration in that file and gives the line it found on its mismatch. Before, the step told the judge to read the declaration at `{file}:{line}` and to copy `file` and `line` onto the mismatch, so a judge that copied the null broke the result schema: `score-signatures.py score` exited 2, the run sent that judge back once, and a second such result halted the coverage check (`helper-failed`). The documentation of `score-signatures.py` now says when `plan` writes these fields as null. Scores do not change. ([#1053](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1053); issue [#1022](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1022))
- **skf-test-skill:** The Estimated Effort cell of Test Skill's Remediation Summary no longer contradicts a split-body gap whose two forms document different declarations of one name. Such a gap's remediation names no form to take and asks for each form's citation and module or owner instead, while the row asked to correct the file the Source names until both files document the export alike, which reads as copying one form over the other. The `split-body-mismatch` action now names both fixes: correct the file each Source names, or, where the two forms document different declarations, add beside each form the citation and module or owner its remediation names. ([#1060](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1060); issues [#1047](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1047), [#1027](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1027))
- **skf-test-skill:** A stale name's gap in Test Skill's Gap Report now cites the line that documents the name when the skill writes it only in a shape the gap ledger's line search does not read, such as a TypeScript declaration without `export` in a fenced code block. The ledger now also reads the run's validated `inventory.json` and, when no line is found, takes the first `at` the inventory gives that name (`SKILL.md` first, then by file path, then the lowest line). Such a name's Medium gap used to cite a bare `SKILL.md`, a file that never writes the name, and asked to update or remove its documentation there; its Source, Issue and remediation now name that line. The Issue of a documented extra opens with it too: oms-uitripled's `UILibraryContextValue`, which the brief's scope now settles as a documented extra, has an Issue that opens with `references/setup.md:90`, where `type UILibraryContextValue = {` opens. A line the search finds still comes first, a name the inventory gives no `at` keeps `SKILL.md`, and scores and the hard gate are unchanged. ([#1059](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1059); issue [#1006](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1006))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill now reads a restored name (a root export the stale-scope guard brings back when a `scope.include` glob matches no file) as a function when the skill's provenance map records it as an `async_function`, a `decorator` or a React `component`, as it already did for `function`. Before, such a name got no kind, so Type Coverage's warning named it as a name that may be a type, and the report dropped the warning that the source has no interface, type alias, enum or class even when that was true. The score does not change: Type Coverage counts the same types. ([#1053](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1053); issue [#1032](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1032))
- **skf-test-skill, skf-update-skill:** Following Test Skill's Medium `brief-scope-stale` remediation no longer shrinks the Export Coverage denominator. When a `scope.include` glob in the skill brief matches no file, the coverage surface restores the root exports defined in a file no include glob covers, but only while some include glob stays stale. The remediation asked only to fix each glob and to add to `scope.exclude` any restored file the brief meant to leave out, so fixing the glob dropped every restored export from the surface, and each one the skill documents came back on the next run as a Medium `stale-documentation` gap. The remediation now says a restored export stays only while an include glob matches no file, lists each file that defines one once, and asks for a `scope.include` glob that covers it when the skill documents its exports, or a `scope.exclude` glob when the skill leaves them out. With nothing restored it asks for the glob edit alone. Update Skill's not-routed reason for the gap says the same. ([#1059](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1059); issue [#1009](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/1009))

### Documentation

- Verifying a Skill now quotes strict SKF 9.0.0 tests of the version each of oh-my-skills' four reference skills ships, run as Test Skill is designed, with its subagents: oms-cocoindex, oms-storybook-react-vite and oms-uitripled pass at 100%, and oms-cognee passes at 99% now that 9.0.0 compares each form with the declaration its own citation names (#918) and oh-my-skills added the citation one form lacked. The page says that oh-my-skills' first 9.0.0 runs took Test Skill's no-subagent fallback, that re-run with subagents two passes became blocked runs on readings of correct text (#1034, #1043) until oh-my-skills rewrote those lines, and which open calls each pass still rests on (#999, #1045, #1050, #1003). `docs/_data/pinned.yaml` records the 9.0.0 scores and run ids (`test_score: 99.0` for oms-cognee). ([#1051](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/1051))

## [9.0.0](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/compare/v8.1.0...v9.0.0) (2026-11-08)

### Breaking changes

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's inventory floor now reads a table's `Signature` column whose header carries a partial label, `Signature (simplified)`, `(partial)`, `(key parameters)` or `(key params)`: each form it pins there also carries `signature_form: "partial"`, and `validate-inventory.py --floor` refuses an inventory unless the entry at that row (its `at`) carries the form and the label, and no entry gives the form unlabelled at that row or with no `at`. Before, such a column was not read, and whether the form was labelled partial, which makes an optional parameter it leaves out Info rather than Critical, was the reader's choice and could change between runs. An inventory that passed can now be refused, and a form written in such a column is now pinned. ([#993](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/993); issue [#888](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/888))

  **Migration:** If Test Skill halts with `inventory-invalid` because the inventory leaves out a partial label the floor pins from a table's `Signature` header, or copies that form unlabelled with no `at`, run it again; if the label is wrong, remove it from the skill's column header.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's inventory floor now also pins the form in a table's `Props`, `Params` or `Parameters` cell that is exactly one code span, as `params` (with `signature_form: "partial"` under a partial label such as `Props (simplified)`), and a usage form, a call written after `await`, `new` or an assignment or through a receiver or module path, or a JSX element that sets a prop, as `usage_signature` and `return_type`. `validate-inventory.py --floor` refuses an inventory whose entry at that place does not carry it. Before, the reader chose how to record these forms, and two runs could compare different ones. An inventory that passed can now be refused. ([#995](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/995); issue [#888](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/888))

  **Migration:** If Test Skill halts with `inventory-invalid` because the inventory changes a form the floor now pins from a `Props`, `Params` or `Parameters` cell or a usage form, run it again; if the pinned form is wrong, correct it in the skill. If a run now stops at the hard gate on a `signature-mismatch` for a form the floor now pins, correct that form in the skill (the run's `inventory-floor.json` gives each origin's file, line and `signature`), then run Test Skill again. If that `signature` misreads what the skill writes at that line, the floor is wrong: report it as a bug, with the line and the `signature`.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill now always compares the function form a skill writes for a `const` whose value is a function, such as storybook's `withActions`, typed `<T extends Renderer>(storyFn: PartialStoryFn<T>) => T['storyResult']` in a description cell. Readers compared the same form in one run and skipped it in the next. Such a constant keeps its `constant` kind and carries the form as `params` (`[]` when it takes no arguments) and `return_type` wherever the skill writes it; a bare `name()` in a description cell is still a mention. This can block a skill that passed: a wrong function form on a constant can now be a Critical `signature-mismatch` gap. ([#991](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/991); issue [#970](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/970))

  **Migration:** If Test Skill now stops at the hard gate on a constant that holds a function, correct the function form the skill documents for it, then run Test Skill again.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill now compares a documented signature with the declaration its own citation names. The signature check compared every documented form of a name with the declarations the package's entry points export, so a skill that documents two functions sharing one name got the second one's correct forms reported as Critical `signature-mismatch` gaps against the first, which blocked the hard gate. The documented inventory now gives each form its place, `at` (`"<path>:<line>"`, a line of SKILL.md or a listed reference that writes the name). A missing or bad place never stops the run: validation drops it, lists it as a warning, and the report's Coverage Analysis section names the forms left without one, which are compared as before. The signature plan reads the `[AST:]` and `[SRC:]` citations at that place (its line; the next non-blank line, unless that line writes the name or, in a fenced block, is a comment; for a form in a fenced block, the comment lines just above it and, when the block holds no other place of the name, a comment on the block's first non-blank line and the first non-blank line after the block, unless that line writes the name) and binds the form to the one declaration of its name they name, at a line or in a range that holds its line or a later one before the next declaration the extraction records in that file (a citation with no line names every declaration in its file): an exported one, or a same-named one no entry point exports, which the surface now lists in `otherDeclarations`. For a name declared more than once, a place that writes two of its forms that differ, such as a table row that quotes another declaration's form as a contrast, gives none of them a citation, so each is bound only by its other places. A bound form is compared with that declaration alone, and its mismatch is recorded there; a form whose citations name no declaration, or two, is compared as before. For cognee, the lightweight `run_pipeline` that `from cognee.pipelines import run_pipeline` loads through a lazy re-export is compared with its own declaration once its form cites it, not with the dataset orchestrator the `pipelines` namespace exports. This can block a skill that passed: a form whose citation names one declaration no longer matches through another. ([#956](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/956); issue [#918](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/918))

  **Migration:** If a skill now stops at the hard gate on a form compared with the declaration its own citation names, correct the form, or the citation when it points at the wrong declaration, then run Test Skill again.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's scoring script now keeps a signature mismatch at the documented form the judge names when its `documented_sig` quotes no form's text, instead of moving it to the first form. Two mismatches of different forms of one name at one declaration were both titled `(form 1 of n)`, so the gap ledger, which tells gaps apart by title, Source and `export`, kept only one, and a mismatch of a form bound to its own declaration was recorded at the first form's declaration. Each now keeps its own form's title, Issue and declaration, with a warning; a mismatch that quotes another form's text still moves to that form. A `documented_sig` that writes the name or a dotted receiver before the parameters, such as `run_pipeline(tasks, data)`, or `()` for a form with no parameters, now quotes that form. This can block a skill that passed: a mismatch of a name documented in several forms that quotes no form is graded as a full form, so a partial label no longer lowers it from Critical to Info, and a gap the ledger dropped as a duplicate is now its own. ([#992](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/992); issue [#919](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/919))

  **Migration:** If a skill now stops at the hard gate on a mismatch a partial label used to lower, correct the form the gap names, or mark it partial where the skill presents it as partial, then run Test Skill again.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's inventory now records a table that documents one component's props (`| Prop | Type | Default | Description |`, or with a Required column) as an entry of its own, at the heading or caption above it that writes the component's name, its rows one object type of `prop: Type` members with no default, Required or `?` mark. The scored signature check now compares it with the component's props: a prop the source lacks, a contradicted type or a required own prop left out is a mismatch, and an optional own prop the table leaves out is an `omitted-optional` difference, Critical unless the table is labelled partial; optionality is not compared. Before, one table could give a false Critical, a match or no check, by how the reader flattened it. This can block a skill that passed. ([#990](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/990); issue [#931](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/931))

  **Migration:** If Test Skill now stops at the hard gate on a props table, correct the prop names or types the source contradicts, add the required props it leaves out, and add the optional props it leaves out or label the table partial in its column header (for example `Props (simplified)`), then run Test Skill again.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill now compares a documented form that lists no parameters but states a return type, such as an entry with `params: ""` and `return_type: "Environment"` beside a `coco.default_env()` call example. The signature plan offered as `alternatives` only forms that list parameters or give a usage form, so the return type of a no-parameter function with a call example was never compared, and a wrong one passed. Such a form is now offered after the other forms, and the form compared as `documented` does not change; a form with no return type, or with a return written as names of values such as `(nodes, edges)`, is still not offered. Such a form's empty parameter list is compared too, since a blank `params` says the name takes none. This can block a skill that passed: a wrong return type on such a form, or parameters it leaves out, is now a Critical `signature-mismatch` gap. ([#992](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/992); issue [#914](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/914))

  **Migration:** If a skill now stops at the hard gate on a no-parameter form, correct the documented return type, or the parameters a `params: ""` form leaves out, then run Test Skill again.

### Changed

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's split-body cross-check no longer compares two forms of one name that belong to different declarations of it, such as a core function and a renderer's function of the same name, or a runner a lazy re-export passes on beside the orchestrator a namespace exports. Forms whose own citations name two declarations (for the inventory reader, which has no surface: two files the skill presents as different things, a re-export naming none), or that the signature plan binds to two, are two exports: each is compared only with the forms of its own declaration, a form attributed to neither is a mismatch only when it contradicts both, and the signature check still holds each form to its own declaration. When the source declares the name again outside the surface's records, a split-body mismatch's Source no longer picks a side by comparing both forms with the one declaration the surface records: it stays at the reference file and says no source settled it. Before, two correct forms of two same-named functions could be read as a High `split-body-mismatch` gap, which blocks the hard gate and tells Update Skill to rewrite one file to match the other. ([#994](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/994); issue [#927](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/927))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's inventory contract now records a function's or a class's form the skill writes as a call expression, such as `await coco.mount([subpath,] process_fn, *args, **kwargs)` or `new Client(opts)`, whole in the entry's `usage_signature`, unless the inventory floor pins that place; a class written as a parameter list or a signature keeps it in `params`. The signature check reads it as a call: its argument names stand for the parameters at their positions and are not compared as names, and a bracketed argument such as `[subpath,]` is optional, so the call is compared with and without it. A list of bare names in `params` still names parameters, so a correct skill no longer passes or fails the hard gate by which reading the judge picks. A function or method recorded only as such a usage counts as complete in a docs-only skill's Export Coverage. ([#990](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/990); issue [#916](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/916))
- **skf-test-skill:** The naive-mode Reference Consistency section's **Exports Cross-Checked** count is now read from `inventory.json`, where `validate-inventory.py` writes it as `crossChecked`: the documented names that two or more of the files the inventory reads (SKILL.md and each listed reference) write, a mention in prose included. It used to be counted by hand, so its meaning and value changed from run to run. ([#988](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/988); issue [#920](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/920))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill no longer compares a function or class an example defines as the reader's own code with the library export of the same name, when its fenced block also defines names the skill does not document as exports and the inventory floor pins no signature there: its entry carries no form, so it records no gap. oms-cocoindex's connector-author `mount_table_target(db_key, ...)` was a Critical gap for one reader and left out by another. ([#991](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/991); issue [#973](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/973))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's Type Coverage now counts a name the stale-scope guard restored (a root export defined in a file no `scope.include` glob covers once a glob matches no file) when the skill's provenance map gives that name a type kind at the same file. The map's kinds are read as Type Coverage's: a class, dataclass, NamedTuple or TypedDict is a class, a Protocol an interface, a type alias a type and an enum an enum, while a TypeVar, a constant or a function is no type. Before, every restored name had no kind, so Type Coverage was scored over the few types left (oms-cocoindex: 1 type, where the map gives 41 restored names a type kind). A restored name still without a kind is left out of Type Coverage and named in the score's warnings, which no longer say the source has no types. A skill whose brief has a stale include glob can see its Type Coverage, and so its score, change on its next test. ([#986](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/986); issue [#913](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/913))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's documented inventory now leaves out a name the skill writes only in a type position, inside another export's documented type or signature, such as `ExceptionContext` in `Callable[[BaseException, ExceptionContext], None | Awaitable[None]]`, or in a parameter table's Type cell, even as a code span that is exactly the name, unless the skill also writes it as an export outside a type position (a heading, an export table's first cell, a code span that is the name, a fenced declaration, or a place the inventory floor lists). Readers had counted such a name documented in one run and undocumented in the next; it now counts as undocumented. ([#991](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/991); issue [#967](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/967))

### Fixed

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill no longer reports a documented module as scoped out by the brief when a name the module passes on has the module's own name and is defined in a file the brief scopes out, such as cognee's `start_visualization_server` submodule, which imports the `start_visualization_server` function from `cognee/shared/utils.py`. The recipe runner's `entry_point_diff.outside_scope` row for a namespace's member now names the namespace (`namespace`), `load-coverage-inputs.py` carries it into `excluded.outsideScope`, and the gap ledger no longer takes such a member for the documented module: the module is an Info documented extra when the source still declares it, else the usual Medium `stale-documentation` gap, instead of a Medium gap that says to widen the brief's scope or remove correct documentation. When the source declares the documented name in the member's own file, the name is that member and the scoped-out gap stays. The member is still listed under Scoped Out by the Brief. ([#989](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/989); issue [#969](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/969))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's signature rules now say how a call to a class is compared, so a correct constructor call no longer depends on the judge's reading. A call to a class is compared with its constructor's parameters after its leading `self` or `cls` (Python's `__init__`, else `__new__`, else the nearest base's; the fields a dataclass, attrs class, pydantic model or NamedTuple generates; a TypeScript or JavaScript `constructor`), a call to an instance with its class's `__call__`, and a name bound to a class with that class's constructor. A leading `self`, `cls`, `&self` or `this: T` the source writes is never compared, as the scoring script already reads it. An extra positional argument exists when the declaration takes `*args` or a rest parameter, and any keyword exists when it takes `**kwargs`, so `Task(fn, max_chunk_size=512)` matches an `__init__` that takes `**kwargs`. A class whose constructor is written only outside the source tree, such as an `Exception` subclass that declares none, counts as matching. Before, a judge that read a call's first argument as `self`, or a keyword only `**kwargs` takes as unknown, reported a Critical `signature-mismatch` gap that blocked the hard gate. ([#987](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/987); issue [#968](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/968))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's scoring script now reads a return written as names of values, such as `→ (nodes, edges)`, `→ [state, setState]` or `=> { data, error }`, as stating no return type, as its signature rules say. A mismatch the signature judge tags `annotation-contradicted` on such a form is therefore graded as an untagged mismatch (Critical), with a warning that the documented signature states no return type, as a form that writes no return already is. A type written alone or in a list (`→ str`, `(str, int)`), a single name (`→ result`), a list that writes a type among its names and a description followed by a type still state one. The signature rules now say the same of a bracketed or braced list of names. ([#983](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/983); issue [#957](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/957))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's signature plan now keeps the declaration line the extraction recorded for a name that a by-eye read also reports in the same file. After the files listed in `readByEye` were read by eye and `surface` ran again, each name found there got a record with no line, which sorted before the extraction's record of that name in the same file, so the plan gave its check `line` and `signatureLine` null and the signature judge had to find the declaration by hand. The line-less record also counted as a second declaration in that file: a citation of the file with no line bound the form to nothing, and a name declared in several files listed it as a candidate with no line. The check, its candidates and its bindings now use the extraction's record, and a record with no line stands in only for a file the extraction gave no line for. ([#984](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/984); issue [#921](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/921))
- **skf-test-skill:** When a skill states members several names share once and places one of a name's own members before or among them, Test Skill's inventory now records that name's whole parameter list in the skill's order, so a correct order is no longer reported as a Critical reordered list. A place the inventory floor pins keeps its pinned parameters after the shared text. ([#990](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/990); issue [#917](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/917))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill no longer reports a documented public export as stale because the name set it counts leaves the export out. `reconcile-coverage.py` now finds a stale name against the whole source surface on both the barrel and the scalar branch: the counted set, the `all` set and every name on the `surface.json` export records. A documented Tier B name of a stratified skill and a documented name of a nested Python entry point (`excluded.nestedEntries`) the brief does not scope out are now neither counted nor stale, so they get no `stale-documentation` gap and no documented-extra note. Before, the barrel branch listed every documented name outside the counted set as stale, and both branches listed a nested entry's names, so the gap ledger told update-skill to update or remove correct documentation and the Stale Documentation count was inflated. ([#985](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/985); issue [#912](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/912))

## [8.1.0](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/compare/v8.0.0...v8.1.0) (2026-11-07)

### Changed

- **all workflows, skf-forger:** When a workflow, or Ferris, cannot find SKF's own customization helper, it now warns `customization_resolver_unavailable: SKF helper skf-resolve-customization.py not found` instead of the bare `not found` that a missing BMAD core resolver also gave. A bare `customization_resolver_unavailable: not found` is unchanged and now always means BMAD core's customization script is missing, as in a project with SKF alone. Reinstall SKF when the new warning appears. ([#979](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/979); issue [#965](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/965))

### Fixed

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill no longer reports a Critical `fabricated-signature` gap for a documented name the source exports through a rename `classify-stale` did not read: a rename of a rename across files (`from .impl import _Impl as Impl` where `impl/__init__.py` renames `_CoreImpl`, in a compatibility `try`/`except` import too, or assigns `_Impl = _core._Impl`; `export { Internal as Entry } from './internal'`, where `internal.ts` renames `API_Entry` by an export list or by an import then a plain re-export), a generic `type Entry<T> = API_Entry<T>`, an annotated `export const Entry: typeof createEntry = createEntry` or Python `Impl: type[_Impl] = _Impl`, a one-line `try: from .impl import _Impl as Impl`, and a compatibility import inside a module-level `with` or `finally` block. Each such name is now `aliased`, an Info documented extra at its first rename's line, whose `renames` is the name the cited file declares where the chain ends (for a one-step rename, the name that line renames). `classify-stale` in `skf-verify-provenance-completeness.py` follows the chain through each file it resolves that declares the name or renames it by one of these forms, until it reaches the declaration a provenance entry cites; a chain that leaves those files, loops or ends at another declaration stays fabricated. ([#975](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/975); issue [#954](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/954))
- **skf-test-skill:** A stale name's gap in Test Skill's Gap Report again cites the line that documents the name when the skill writes it only as a quoted item in a fenced code block, such as an `__all__` list: oms-cocoindex's `ManagedConnection` reads "`references/connectors.md:111` documents `ManagedConnection`" again, where 8.0.0 gave the gap a bare `SKILL.md` Source. A declaration in a fenced block outside the inventory floor (a fence no citation heads, or any fence in a nested reference) now ranks below a heading, an export table's first cell and a code span that name the export, so a function an example defines as the reader's own code under an export's name, such as oms-cocoindex's connector-author `mount_table_target` helper, is cited only when nothing else documents the name: that name now cites `references/target-state.md:125` instead of the helper at `:163`, and oms-uitripled's `add` moves from its declaration at `references/catalog.md:110` to the call `add(componentName, options)` at `:115`. A quoted string in a data block (json, yaml...), in an HTML comment or in prose, or one that holds other words too (`"add x"`), still documents nothing. ([#977](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/977); issues [#966](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/966), [#972](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/972))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill no longer reports a Critical `fabricated-signature` gap for a documented name whose rename chain passes through a middle file that exports a name as its default (`import { createEntry } from './api'; export default createEntry;` in `mid.ts`, re-exported as `export { default as Entry } from './mid'`). `classify-stale` in `skf-verify-provenance-completeness.py` now reads a column-0 `export default L`, where an import or a declaration of the same file binds the bare identifier `L`, as a rename of `L` to `default`, so the chain goes on to the cited declaration and the name is `aliased`, an Info documented extra whose `renames` is the name the cited file declares. A default export of a call, an object, an arrow or any other expression still ends the chain. ([#980](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/980); issue [#974](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/974))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill now names the skill in its report's title. The report template's title is `# Test Report: {{skillName}}`, and the step that creates the report replaced only its frontmatter, so a run could publish a report titled with the placeholder, as two oh-my-skills reports were. That step now writes the skill's name into the title, and the report check that runs before the result files are written halts with `report-anchor-missing` when the report does not hold the line `# Test Report: <skill>` exactly once. ([#978](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/978); issue [#971](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/971))

### Documentation

- Verifying a Skill now quotes strict SKF 8.0.0 tests of the version each of oh-my-skills' four reference skills ships: oms-cocoindex, oms-storybook-react-vite and oms-uitripled pass at 100%, and oms-cognee is still blocked by the two `run_pipeline` false positives of #918, whose fix (#956) is not in 8.0.0. The page says what 8.0.0 changed on unchanged skill text (storybook from 98.23% to 100% through the star re-export rule of #926; uitripled's rest-element forms settled by #932, its score unchanged at 100%), that cocoindex's first 8.0.0 run counted `ExceptionContext` as undocumented (#967) before oh-my-skills documented it, and which open calls each pass still rests on, now written down in every report. `docs/_data/pinned.yaml` records the 8.0.0 scores and run ids (`test_score: null` for oms-cognee). ([#976](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/976))

## [8.0.0](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/compare/v7.0.0...v8.0.0) (2026-11-07)

### Breaking changes

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's inventory floor now cuts a name at its first `[` as it does at `(` and `<`, so an export-table first cell or a code-only heading that writes a Python or Go generic, such as `App[P, R]`, pins `App`, and a call written that way, such as `first[T](xs: list[T]) -> T`, pins its form too when it writes its return after `->`, `=>`, `→` or `:`, or writes no return, so a Go generic call such as `Index[T any](s []T, v T) int` pins only its name. `validate-inventory.py --floor` then refuses an inventory that leaves such a name out, so Export Coverage stops dropping generic exports unchecked. A TypeScript array type such as `Foo[]` still pins no name. Because the floor now holds more names, a skill that passed before can now stop at the hard gate on one of them. ([#945](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/945); issue [#915](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/915))

  **Migration:** If a skill now stops at the hard gate on a gap for a name it writes with square brackets in an export table's first cell or a code-only heading, document that name correctly or remove it from the skill, then run Test Skill again. The run's `inventory-floor.json` lists each name's `origins`, so find the line that put the name in the floor; when it is not an export, change that line rather than document a name that is not an export. If the run stops on a `signature-mismatch` for a form such a call writes, correct that form in the skill (the origin's `signature` in `inventory-floor.json` gives what the floor read), or, if that `signature` misreads the line, report it as a bug with the line and the `signature`.

### Added

- **skf-campaign:** Campaign now saves whether its capstone, verification and refinement stages completed, were skipped or failed, with the failure's `halt_reason` and `exit_code`, as the optional `campaign.stage_outcomes`. The report gains a Stages section and `SKF_CAMPAIGN_RESULT_JSON` an optional `stage_outcomes`, so a pipeline can tell a failed verification from a skipped one. ([#939](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/939); issue [#906](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/906))
- **skf-quick-skill, skf-create-skill, skf-update-skill, skf-create-stack-skill:** The result lines of Quick Skill, Create Skill, Update Skill and Create Stack Skill now carry `security_result` (`pass`, `warn` or `skipped`), so a pipeline can tell a security scan that could not run, such as one without `SNYK_TOKEN`, from one that ran. `pass` means the scan exited 0 and skill-check reported no finding, which does not show that the scan found nothing. `validation_issues.security` is unchanged. ([#936](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/936); issue [#902](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/902))

### Changed

- **skf-quick-skill:** Quick Skill no longer documents the names an `export *` or `export type *` from another package brings in: it used to list them from the README as `re-export` exports, and since Test Skill, like the recipe runner, leaves such a star unresolved, each name read as stale and a correct skill got a Medium `stale-documentation` gap for each. The skill now names the star instead, with its file and line and the package it re-exports, so a reader knows to look in that package. A named re-export from another package (`export { a, b } from 'pkg'`) still counts, and a star from a module of the source that could not be read still takes its names from the README. A skill built before this change keeps those names until it is built again. ([#962](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/962); issue [#958](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/958))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's signature rules now settle four forms its judges decided alone. A declaration whose parameter list is written only in a package outside the source tree, such as storybook/test's bindings destructured from a value cast to `typeof domTestingLibrary` or a const typed `typeof vitestSpyOn`, has its parameters, their optionality and its return left uncompared and counts as matching, and a const annotated with a function type declares that type's parameters, so a form may name a parameter as the type does or destructure it as the arrow does. A return written as names of values, such as `→ (nodes, edges)`, states no return type and is not compared, while `→ str` still states one. A `...props` rest in a component's destructured props form stands for every prop the form does not name, own or inherited, so a form that copies the source's destructuring no longer reads as leaving out a prop. Each of these forms now gets one verdict, so two runs on an unchanged skill agree on it. ([#947](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/947); issues [#925](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/925), [#928](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/928), [#930](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/930), [#932](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/932))
- **skf-test-skill:** A stale name's gap in Test Skill's Gap Report now cites the line that documents the name as an export: its line in the inventory floor, else a declaration of it in a fenced code block, else a heading or an export table's first cell that names it, else a line whose code span is the name or opens its call (`get` or `get(key)`), read from `SKILL.md` and every Markdown file under `references/`, subfolders included. It used to cite the first line that wrote the name as a word, frontmatter and prose included, so oms-uitripled's `add` read "`SKILL.md:7` documents `add`", the frontmatter's `npx shadcn@latest add`, instead of `references/catalog.md:110`. A name the skill writes only as a word, or inside a longer code span such as `uitripled add`, now has an Issue that reads "the skill documents", and a Medium `stale-documentation` gap for it has Source `SKILL.md`. The Issue of every stale-name gap, and the Source and remediation of a Medium `stale-documentation` gap, move to that line. ([#953](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/953); issue [#922](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/922))
- **skf-test-skill:** When Test Skill reads a file by eye (a file the recipe runner could not parse, a statement the Quick-tier parser warns about, or the fallback per-file scan), an `export *` or `export type *` from another package now adds no name to the surface, as the recipe runner leaves such a star unresolved; a named re-export from another package still counts. Each per-file result lists those statements in `unresolved_stars`, and the Coverage Analysis section names them as unresolved. A run used to decide alone whether, and which, of the package's names to count, so one skill's tier A set and Export Coverage changed from run to run: oms-storybook-react-vite counted none, six or all 19 `@vitest/spy` types across three runs. A skill that documents names such a star brings in, including the names Quick Skill takes from a package's README for it, now gets a `stale-documentation` gap for each at every tier, as it already did where the recipe runner read the file. ([#946](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/946); issue [#926](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/926))

### Fixed

- **skf-campaign:** When Create Stack Skill, Verify Stack or Refine Architecture printed a result line holding an integer of more than 4,300 digits or nesting too deep to decode, `set-campaign` exited 1 with a Python traceback and the campaign stopped. Campaign now records that stage as failed with `result-unreadable` and goes on, as it does for any other line it cannot parse. ([#952](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/952))
- **skf-campaign:** When Create Stack Skill, Verify Stack or Refine Architecture printed a result line Campaign could not parse (cut off, or not a JSON object), `set-campaign` exited 2 and the campaign stopped. Campaign now records the stage as failed with `result-unreadable`, logs an unparseable-line event and goes on, as it already did for Export Skill. A line with no `status` or no `exit_code` is now recorded the same way: before, one with no `status` was saved like a skipped stage, and a success line with no `exit_code` was recorded as a result. ([#939](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/939); issue [#905](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/905))
- **skf-campaign, skf-quick-skill, skf-create-skill:** When Quick Skill could not write a Tier B batch's summary file, Campaign marked every skill of the batch failed with `no-batch-result`, even the ones Quick Skill built. The `batch_summary` event of a Quick Skill or Create Skill `--batch` run whose `summary_path` is null now also gives `batch_file`, the path of the batch run folder's `batch.jsonl`. Campaign reads each target's result from that file and logs the `summary_write_failed` warning, so the skills Quick Skill built are recorded completed with their skill path and quality score. ([#938](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/938); issue [#904](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/904))
- **skf-create-skill:** Create Skill's validation step showed the `skill-check --fix` call before the description guard, so a run read top to bottom could rewrite SKILL.md before the guard captured the description and before the first hash. The call now sits inside the guard block, and the evidence report's Auto-Fixed Issues line is among the fields validation fills, so it no longer keeps the "none" written before skill-check ran. ([#952](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/952))
- **skf-create-skill, skf-update-skill:** Create Skill and Update Skill now read skill-check's security scan as Quick Skill and Create Stack Skill do, from its exit code and the last lines it prints on stderr. A scan that did not finish (no `SNYK_TOKEN`, no scan runner, a scanner that stopped, or a call cut short) is recorded as skipped with the reason, and finding codes in those lines as a warning, where before anything but a stderr naming `SNYK_TOKEN` read as passed. `security_result` in both result lines follows, so `pass` means the scan exited 0 and skill-check reported no finding, which does not show that the scan found nothing. ([#949](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/949); issue [#934](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/934))
- **skf-create-skill, skf-update-skill:** Create Skill and Update Skill now hand the description guard its copy of the description in a file in the run folder, as Quick Skill does, never in a shell string. Before, the shell read the description: a double quote broke the restore or was dropped, a `$` and the name after it became the shell's value, so the guard could even write a changed description over one `skill-check --fix` never touched, and backticks or `$(...)`, which a description quoting code can hold, ran as commands. The description is now restored exactly as it was, and nothing in it runs. ([#960](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/960); issue [#951](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/951))
- **skf-quick-skill:** A Quick Skill `--batch` run used to end with no halt line when the batch helper could not hand out the next target or write the batch summary, and to go back to the same target again and again when a target's outcome could not be recorded. It now stops with exit code `4` (`write-failure`) and a halt line of phase `batch-mode`, as a Create Skill `--batch` run already does, and the health check does not run. ([#937](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/937); issue [#903](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/903))
- **skf-quick-skill, skf-create-skill, skf-update-skill, skf-create-stack-skill:** When `skill-check --fix` rewrote SKILL.md, Quick Skill and Create Skill listed no auto-fixed issue, Update Skill kept its stale copy, and Create Stack Skill neither warned nor validated again, because each read a `fixed[]` list skill-check 1.2.0 never writes. Each now hashes SKILL.md before and after the call; when it changed, Quick Skill and Create Skill list "skill-check --fix rewrote SKILL.md", Update Skill re-reads it, and Create Stack Skill warns that `metadata.json` may be out of date and validates again. Without the hash helper, Quick Skill, Create Skill and Create Stack Skill say SKILL.md may have been rewritten (not hashed) and act the same. ([#935](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/935); issue [#901](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/901))
- **skf-quick-skill, skf-update-skill, skf-test-skill, skf-audit-skill, skf-rename-skill, skf-drop-skill, skf-analyze-source, skf-export-skill, skf-refine-architecture, skf-create-stack-skill, skf-verify-stack, skf-create-skill:** Quick Skill now says its summary carries `security_result`, that a `--batch` run can also print a batch-level halt line, that `run_id` is null on a line emitted without a run folder, and that a batch summary event can name its file beside a warning; Update Skill's schema names `result_file_write_failed`. Test, Audit, Rename and Drop Skill tie their `-latest` copy, hook and `result_path` to the per-run record, eight schemas say a `--result-dir` that names no folder leaves `result_path` null with no warning, and the workflows guide says a `pass` from Create Skill, Stack Skill or Update Skill does not show the scan found nothing. ([#952](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/952))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill now records a documented name that a file under a `docs`, `examples` or `benchmarks` folder still declares as a documented extra when the provenance map cites that file, such as Storybook's `CheckboxControl` in `code/addons/docs/src/`. `classify-stale` in `skf-verify-provenance-completeness.py` skipped those folders at every depth, the cited file included, so such a name was a Medium `stale-documentation` gap whose remediation said to remove it. It now reads a file the map cites wherever it lies, `dist`, `build`, `vendor` and `tests` included, and its walk skips `docs`, `examples` and `benchmarks` only right below the package it reads and below each package root inside it, unless the folder holds a cited file. ([#943](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/943); issue [#924](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/924))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill no longer reports a Critical `fabricated-signature` gap, which blocks the hard gate, for a documented name the source exports by renaming the cited declaration in a form `classify-stale` did not read: `export { default as Button } from './Button'`, `export const Foo = FooImpl`, `type Foo = FooImpl`, Python `Foo = _Foo`, an import renamed then re-exported, a quoted `as "Foo"`, an export list after a block comment, a Python import inside a module-level `try` or `if`, a file that declares the name before it renames to it, and a cited module that is itself the default export. Each such name is now `aliased`, an Info documented extra at the rename's line. `classify-stale` in `skf-verify-provenance-completeness.py` also resolves the rename's relative `from` module and the import that binds the renamed name, so a rename of another file's same-named declaration stays fabricated, while a package it cannot resolve keeps the earlier rule. ([#955](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/955); issue [#910](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/910))
- **skf-test-skill:** The Issue of a `stale-documentation` or `fabricated-signature` gap in Test Skill's Gap Report now names the line that documents the name, as a documented extra's Issue already did: a name written only in a reference file reads "`references/connectors.md:9` documents `ColumnDef`", where it used to read "SKILL.md documents `ColumnDef`". When no line of `SKILL.md` or a top-level reference file writes the name, the Issue says "the skill documents", including for a name the brief scopes out. Titles, Sources and remediations are unchanged. ([#942](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/942); issue [#923](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/923))
- **skf-test-skill, skf-create-skill, skf-update-skill, skf-create-stack-skill, skf-audit-skill:** The provenance line check now reads a column-0 `export default` line as the definition of the export named `default`, the name SKF's extraction records for a module's default export, whatever follows it (`export default storybookTest;`, `export default async function postinstall() {}`, an anonymous function or class, an object or any other expression). A correct citation of a default export no longer leaves an Info `provenance-unverified` gap in Test Skill's report, and a stale `default` whose cited file has that line is a documented extra, no longer a Critical `fabricated-signature` gap. A `default` entry at a wrong line now gets that line, so Create Skill, Update Skill and Create Stack Skill move it as they move any entry. A `default` entry an extraction left out, whose cited file has a column-0 `export default`, is now a baseline gap that Audit Skill and Update Skill read by eye, no longer a removed export. `export default foo` still defines `foo`, and CommonJS `module.exports =` still defines no `default`. ([#944](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/944); issue [#929](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/929))
- **skf-test-skill, skf-update-skill:** Test Skill's Info `provenance-unverified` gap for a documented name that classify-stale marks `aliased` now names the alias line and how to record the rename; it sent the person to a line of the cited file, which never defines the name. The coverage check, when it records its gaps, passes classify-stale's result to `gap-ledger.py append --from provenance-line` through `--stale`, and the `aliased` item gains a `renames` key holding the renamed local name. The gap stays at the cited `file:line`, and its remediation first asks to record the rename in the provenance map (`export_name` the local name, `reexported_as` the documented one) if no other entry already has that `export_name`, else to cite the alias line. When the local name is `default`, which the map keys on `export_name` and so holds once, it only asks to cite the alias line. Update Skill's not-routed reason for the gap gives the same advice. ([#961](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/961); issue [#911](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/911))
- **skf-update-skill:** Update Skill could not write a new version of an older skill that keeps its provenance map, evidence report and extraction rules directly in its forge folder rather than in a version folder: it started the new version's forge folder without them, so the provenance-map write found no map and the run halted with nothing written. It now copies each of the three from that folder when the map it loaded came from there, and leaves the originals in place. A repair from a test report of such a skill reads that map too, when the skill's version folder exists in its forge folder. ([#950](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/950); issue [#948](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/948))
- **skf-update-skill:** When Update Skill found no change in a skill whose provenance map was still in its flat forge folder, it wrote no result file, said nothing, and still called the `on_complete` hook with the path of an `update-skill-result-latest.json` that did not exist. It now creates the version's forge folder first. When it cannot, the line carries a `result_file_write_failed` warning and the hook is skipped. ([#940](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/940); issue [#907](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/907))
- **skf-update-skill:** A repair from a test report of an older skill that keeps its forge data directly in its forge folder, with no folder for its version there, halted at the provenance-map write with `No such file or directory`, because nothing created the folder the updated map goes into. A repair now creates that folder first, copies the skill's flat `evidence-report.md` and `extraction-rules.yaml` into it when it does not hold them yet, and writes the map there, so the update is appended to the full evidence report and later versions keep the extraction rules; the flat files stay as they were. When the folder cannot be created, the run halts with `halted-for-write-failure` and the repair is undone. ([#963](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/963); issue [#959](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/959))
- **skf-update-skill:** A headless Update Skill run whose result could not be written ended with no `SKF_UPDATE_RESULT_JSON` line, so a pipeline could not tell why. It now ends on a `halted-for-write-failure` line with `error.phase` `report:result-contract` and the emitter's message. The version the run wrote stays in place. ([#940](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/940); issue [#908](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/908))
- **skf-verify-stack, skf-audit-skill, skf-test-skill, skf-refine-architecture, skf-analyze-source, skf-drop-skill, skf-export-skill, skf-create-stack-skill:** Verify Stack, Audit Skill, Test Skill and Refine Architecture said any result file that could not be written leaves `result_path` null, but only a failed per-run record does: a failed `-latest` copy leaves it set, and a `result_file_write_failed` warning names the copy. Their report steps and eight result envelope schemas now say so, and Refine Architecture and Export Skill no longer say their completion hook runs after both result files were written. Test Skill no longer promises that `skf-test-skill-result-latest.json` holds a blocked run's FAIL when the run could not write it. ([#941](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/941); issue [#909](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/909))

### Documentation

- Verifying a Skill now quotes strict SKF 7.0.0 tests of the version each of oh-my-skills' four reference skills ships. oms-cocoindex and oms-uitripled pass at 100% and oms-storybook-react-vite at 98.23%; oms-cognee is blocked by two false positives, a documented function compared with another of the same name (#918). The page says how the first 7.0.0 tests and two or three rounds of hand fixes per skill found real errors in all four skills, the two that first passed included, and which open calls the storybook and uitripled passes turn on. `docs/_data/pinned.yaml` records the new scores (`test_score: null` for oms-cognee), the storybook worked example ends with its 7.0.0 pass, and the skill model's oms-cognee excerpt shows its new counts (t1 36, t1_low 50). ([#933](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/933))
- The README's reference-output paragraph no longer quotes the old 99.0% to 99.49% range for oh-my-skills. It now gives the strict Skill Forge 4.0.0 results that Verifying a Skill already quotes: oms-cocoindex passes at 100% and oms-cognee at 99%, while oms-uitripled and oms-storybook-react-vite are blocked, and every report is published, failing ones included. Like that page, it now calls oh-my-skills a public record of what the pipeline gets right and where its test still falls short, not proof that the pipeline does what it says. ([#900](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/900))

## [7.0.0](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/compare/v6.0.0...v7.0.0) (2026-11-06)

### Breaking changes

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's inventory floor now records the signature a skill writes in a fixed, complete form, not only the name: a function declaration in a cited code block, the leading code span of a `Signature` or `Signatures` cell, and a code-only heading or the export-table first-cell span that writes the name as one call such as `fetch(url): Promise<T>`, with nothing else in the span. `validate-inventory.py --floor` refuses an inventory where no entry of that name carries the form, so the pinned names carry the same form in every run (the signature check still skips a `method` entry and an alternative form it drops). `Props`, `Params` and `Parameters` cells, usage forms and forms written only in prose stay the reader's. Because a pinned form no longer changes between runs, a skill whose pinned form is wrong can now stop at the hard gate on it in a run that used to pass. ([#898](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/898); issue [#888](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/888))

  **Migration:** If a skill now stops at the hard gate on a `signature-mismatch` for a form it writes in a cited declaration, a `Signature` cell, a code-only heading or an export table's first cell, correct that form in the skill (the run's `inventory-floor.json` gives each origin's file, line and `signature`), then run Test Skill again. If that `signature` misreads what the skill writes at that line, the floor is wrong: report it as a bug, with the line and the `signature`.

### Fixed

- **skf-analyze-source, skf-create-skill, skf-update-skill:** When the `-latest` copy of the result file could not be written, Analyze Source, Create Skill and Update Skill still called the `on_complete` hook with that path, which then held an earlier run's record or no file. The hook now runs only when the run wrote that copy, and otherwise is skipped with a line that says why, as Quick Skill already does. Create Skill also skips it when the per-run record could not be written, and Update Skill when the result contract could not be written at all. ([#893](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/893); issue [#891](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/891))
- **skf-campaign:** When Create Stack Skill, Verify Stack or Refine Architecture printed no result line during a campaign, Campaign recorded the stage the same way as one it skipped on purpose. It now records the run through the new `campaign-state.py set-campaign --no-result <field>`, with the halt reason `no-result`: the stage summary shows `failed (no-result)` and the decision log names the missing line and the exit code, while the state still holds null for the field, as for a skip. Campaign also reads the line one of these runs prints on stderr when it halts, so a halt keeps its own halt reason instead of counting as no line. A stage skipped on purpose (no skill to compose, no architecture document) is still shown as skipped, and the campaign still goes on. ([#894](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/894); issue [#890](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/890))
- **skf-quick-skill, skf-create-skill:** A Quick Skill or Create Skill `--batch` run now says how a caller reads it: the `batch_summary` event, printed before the health check, and the summary file its `summary_path` names, never `quick-skill-batch-latest.json` or `create-skill-batch-latest.json`, which may be another batch's. A batch that printed no `batch_summary` event, as when a headless session ends partway, has no batch result unless it printed a halt line of its own, and each target ended as its `done` or `fail` event says. After a cut-off batch, a Quick Skill batch runs again from its first target, while a Create Skill `--batch` run with the same briefs goes on with the brief it was working on. ([#895](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/895); issue [#889](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/889))
- **skf-quick-skill, skf-create-stack-skill, skf-create-skill, skf-update-skill:** When skill-check's security scan cannot run or does not finish (no `SNYK_TOKEN`, no scan runner, or another scanner failure), Quick Skill now reports `Security: skipped` with the reason. It takes the validation verdict from skill-check's JSON instead of its exit code, so a scan that never started no longer reads as a failed validation or a security warning. A `pass` now reads "scan exited 0; skill-check 1.2.0 does not pass the scan's findings on": the scanner also exits 0 when its analysis fails, and skill-check's JSON output does not carry the scan's findings, so a pass does not show that the scan found nothing. Create Stack Skill lists a skipped or clean scan as a note in its validation results instead of recording a finding, and Create Skill and Update Skill now record the scan as skipped, not passed, when skill-check's error output asks for `SNYK_TOKEN`. ([#897](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/897); issue [#885](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/885))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill no longer records a correct export-list alias as a Critical `fabricated-signature` gap. When no file a documented name's provenance entries cite defines it, `classify-stale` in `skf-verify-provenance-completeness.py` now looks for an item of an export list or of a Python `from X import` clause that renames to it a name the cited file declares (`export type { API_Entry as Entry }`, on one line or as an item of a multi-line list, or `from .impl import _Impl as Impl`, on one line, in parentheses or after a backslash); such a name gets the new reason `aliased`, `fabricated: false` and a `defined_at` at the alias. It is then an Info `Documented extra` observation and its provenance entry an Info `provenance-unverified` gap, so neither blocks the hard gate. Any other rename, such as `export { default as Entry }`, `const Entry = API_Entry` or an import then an export, stays fabricated, and so does a homonym that renames nothing the cited file declares. ([#896](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/896); issue [#886](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/886))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's documented inventory no longer records a function written with empty parentheses in running text or a description cell, such as `instrument()` in a Purpose column, as a form that takes no argument. The inventory contract tells the reader to leave `params` and `usage_signature` out for such a mention, and the signature comparison rules say it claims nothing, so a function with a required parameter no longer gets a Critical `signature-mismatch` gap from it. A description cell is any table cell but an export table's first cell and a cell in a column that writes the call or signature, such as Signature, Props, Params, Parameters, Arguments, Usage, Syntax or Example. A `name()` the skill writes in a heading, an export table's first cell, such a column or a fenced example is still a form, compared as before. ([#896](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/896); issue [#887](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/887))

## [6.0.0](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/compare/v5.0.0...v6.0.0) (2026-11-05)

### Breaking changes

- **all workflows, skf-forger:** A headless run under `claude -p` no longer stops partway because a step left a subagent running when its turn ended. Under `claude -p` a run stops when the agent's turn ends, so a Test Skill run that started a subagent in the background and ended its turn exited `0` five minutes in, with no `SKF_TEST_RESULT_JSON` line and its `.test-skill.lock` left behind. Every workflow, and Ferris, now runs each subagent in the foreground and waits for every long-running command to exit, and a headless run never ends its turn while either still runs. In a headless run `ccc index` runs in the foreground with the shell's longest timeout, so a first Setup index that outlasts it is reported as a failed index, and the troubleshooting guide says to run `ccc index` in a terminal, then re-run Setup; an interactive run can still build a long index in the background and wait for it. The docs and every workflow's headless contract no longer tell callers to read a `-latest.json` result file to learn a run's outcome: a caller reads the run's own `SKF_*_RESULT_JSON` line, since a run that printed none has no result to read, whatever the process exit code (it was cut off, or could not write its result), and its `-latest.json` file may then describe an earlier run. Ferris halts a pipeline with `no-result` when a workflow in it printed no result line. Campaign fails a skill whose Create Skill run printed no line (`no-result`), and records an export whose Export Skill run printed none as failed with `no-result`, or with `result-unreadable` when its line cannot be read. ([#882](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/882), [#883](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/883))

  **Migration:** An automation that reads a `-latest.json` result file to learn a headless run's outcome reads the run's own `SKF_*_RESULT_JSON` line instead and treats a run that printed none as failed. A Campaign that relied on Create Skill finishing with no line, on an install missing the shared emitter, installs SKF again with `npx bmad-module-skill-forge install`.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's async/sync check now also checks each method a class, interface, struct, trait or type entry of the inventory lists, tied to its class. Before, only `function` and `method` entries were read, so an example that awaits a method the skill documents as sync, or never awaits one it documents as async, passed. Such an example now raises a High finding, which can stop a skill that passed Test Skill at its hard gate. A method name the skill documents on two owners is now checked per owner, so the second owner's example can raise its own High finding. ([#877](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/877); issue [#844](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/844))

  **Migration:** For a skill that now stops at the hard gate on such a finding, make the example agree with the documented method (await one the skill documents as async, drop the `await` of one it documents as sync), or correct the description when the source says otherwise, then run Test Skill again.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's inventory rules now say how to record a documented `const` whose value is a component, such as a `forwardRef(...)` or `memo(...)` call or an alias like `const Tabs = TabsPrimitive.Root`: as a `constant` with the declaration or usage form the skill gives as `usage_signature`, while a data constant carries no signature field. The rules had no such line, so whether a component constant's signature entered Signature Accuracy depended on how a run recorded it. Recorded this way, its form is compared with its declaration, so a skill some runs passed can now stop at the hard gate. A component whose props type comes from a package outside the source tree, such as that `Tabs` alias, is checked only for being a component: its props are left uncompared. ([#878](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/878); issue [#837](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/837))

  **Migration:** If a skill now stops at the hard gate on a component constant's `signature-mismatch` gap, correct the form the gap quotes as `documented_sig`, then run Test Skill again.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's signature judge now compares only what a documented form writes. A call example (`RecursiveSplitter()`, `embed(text, model=m)`) is compared as a call, so leaving out an optional parameter is no difference, an ellipsis (`(...)`, `(tasks, data, ...)`) claims nothing about the parameters it stands for, and a list of bare names (`connect(host, port)`) does not claim to be complete; a form that writes a type or a default still does, so an optional parameter it leaves out stays an `omitted-optional` difference. Optionality is stated only by a default, a `?` or an optional marker, never by a type, so a parameter list that states it for no parameter has its optionality left uncompared: `connect(host, port)` and `connect(host: str, port: int)` both match `def connect(host: str, port: int = 5432)`. A default's value is not compared, only the optionality it marks. A parameter written without a type is not compared on type (bare `*args` matches `*args: P.args`), the names of `*args` and `**kwargs` are not compared, and parameters after `*` are compared by name rather than order. A return type the form does not state, a type the source leaves unannotated and type arguments either side leaves out (`dict` against `dict[str, Any]`) are not compared, so a function documented with no parameters and no return type no longer raises a Critical `signature-mismatch` gap against `-> None`; a TypeScript or JavaScript parameter with a literal default (`pageSize = 20`) still has that literal's type. A blank `return_type` states none, while Go's result list and the type before a C, C++ or Java name count as a stated return type. A documented parameter type that names some members of the source's union is no mismatch, since calls that follow it are valid, and neither is a keyword-only `*` the form adds. Equivalent spellings are no mismatch: `Optional[X]`, `Union[X, None]` and `X | None`, a union's members in any order, `List[X]` and `list[X]`, a `typing.` prefix, `Array<T>` and `T[]`, a type alias against the type it names, and type variables renamed consistently. A Python `*args` or `**kwargs` counts as optional, like a TypeScript rest parameter, but in a language without keyword arguments an optional parameter left out before one the form writes is a mismatch, since it shifts the caller's positions. A documented return type that matches what the function's body demonstrably returns, where the declared annotation says otherwise, is no longer a Critical `signature-mismatch` gap, since the skill documents what callers get: the judge tags it `annotation-contradicted` with the body line that returns it, and Test Skill's scoring script checks that the documented signature states a return type and writes the source's parameters as the rules read them (the parameters' names and order, an optionality the documented list states, and a type both sides write, read with common equivalent spellings), and that the line falls between the declaration and the next one and, read from the local source the script is now given with `--source-root`, starts with `return` (or is a one-line declaration's own expression body). It then records an Info `observation` titled `Annotation contradicted: {name}` that blocks nothing and asks for no change to the skill, only that the annotation be reported upstream; a case whose facts do not check stays a Critical gap, and where no such line exists (a Rust tail expression, say) or the judge cannot name it, the declaration decides. The coherence check's reference judge and the split-body Source, which tag nothing, read such a return type as agreeing with the source. Once a parameter list marks any parameter optional, a parameter written without a default, a `?` or a marker is read as required, so a skill a lenient judge passed on such a list can now stop at the hard gate. ([#869](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/869), [#873](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/873), [#880](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/880); issue [#835](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/835))

  **Migration:** If a skill now stops at the hard gate on a `signature-mismatch` gap whose documented parameter list marks some parameters optional and not others, write the default or `?` the source declares on each optional parameter, then run Test Skill again.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill now compares each form a skill documents a name in that lists parameters or gives a usage, such as a brief usage form in SKILL.md and a full props list in a reference file. `score-signatures.py plan` kept one form per name, so whichever form ranked first stood in for the others: a correct skill could get a false Critical `signature-mismatch` gap, and a wrong form went unchecked. The documented inventory now lists a name once per place the skill documents it, under one kind, and a check lists the name's other forms as `alternatives` (the fallback per-file scan reads them from the plan's `documentedAlternatives`).
