The judge compares the declaration with each form by that form's own reading rules and reports a mismatch for each form that does not match, naming it in the mismatch's new optional `form` key, and `score` grades each mismatch by its own form, so an optional member left out of a form the skill labels partial is an Info observation. A form's label lowers a grade only when the mismatch quotes that form's text as `documented_sig`; otherwise `score` warns and grades it against the form it quotes. The gap's title (`Signature mismatch: {name} (form 1 of 2)`) and Issue name the form, so the ledger keeps one gap per form. Entries that say the same thing are one form, and of two that differ only by a partial label, the full one stands. A form that lists no parameter and gives no usage is never an alternative, and a `form` the check did not offer is a warning, graded against the first form. A usage form is read as what it writes: a component usage such as `<Canvas of={Primary} />` as the names of the props it sets, a call as its arguments in order, and a JSX spread, children or a call's `...args` can pass a required member. Forms that were never compared now are, so a skill that passed can stop at the hard gate. ([#878](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/878); issue [#826](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/826))

  **Migration:** If a skill now stops at the hard gate on a `signature-mismatch` gap for a form it did not compare before, correct the form the gap quotes as `documented_sig`, then run Test Skill again.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill now lists every name a skill documents in a fixed form before it reads the skill for its documented exports: the first column of an export table, a heading that is only a code span, and a public declaration in a code block whose first line is a comment citing its source. The new `load-coverage-inputs.py floor` writes them to `inventory-floor.json` in the run folder, and `validate-inventory.py --floor` refuses an inventory that leaves one out of SKILL.md or a reference file the reader lists, so two runs on the same skill agree on those names and Export Coverage and Type Coverage stop shifting with them. A refused inventory is dispatched again once with the missing names, and the run halts `inventory-invalid` the second time. Names a skill writes only in prose are still the reader's call. Because the names the floor adds are now always counted and compared with the source, a skill that passed before can now stop at the hard gate on one of them. ([#872](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/872); issue [#790](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/790))

  **Migration:** If a skill now stops at the hard gate on a gap for a name it documents in an export table, a code-only heading or a cited declaration block, document that name correctly or remove it from the skill, then run Test Skill again. The floor checks SKILL.md and the reference files the reader lists, and the run's `inventory-floor.json` lists each name's `origins`, so find the line that put the name in the floor. When the name is not an export (an example, or a heading over something that is not an export), change that line, for example rename the heading or move the citation comment out of the example block, rather than document a name that is not an export.

- **skf-test-skill, skf-create-skill:** Test Skill now compares a component's documented signature by its props alone: `FC<P>`, `ComponentType<P>`, a `memo`, `forwardRef` or other wrapper over `P` and `(props: P) => JSX.Element` are one contract, and a component's return type is never compared, so writing one where the source declares another no longer raises a Critical `signature-mismatch` gap. This holds for React, Preact, Solid, Vue and Svelte components, class components included; a function that takes several positional parameters, such as `flexRender(Comp, props)`, is compared as a function. A component's own props are the ones its package writes, `VariantProps` of its own variants included. A prop it inherits from another package's type (`HTMLAttributes`, `ComponentProps<typeof Link>`), the `ref` a `forwardRef` adds and the `children` a `PropsWithChildren` adds need not be documented when optional, but a required inherited prop, such as a `Link`'s `href`, must be, and every prop a form writes must exist on the component's props. A usage (`<Canvas of={X} />`) or a list of bare prop names is compared as a call: it must pass every required prop, and an optional prop it leaves out is no difference. `| null` and `| undefined` on an optional prop, a props type name the source does not declare and the values in a usage example are not compared. A type never states optionality: a props list that states it for no member, with no `?`, no Required column and no default, has its optionality left uncompared. In an object type that writes `?` on any member, a member written without one is read as required, so a skill a lenient judge passed can now stop at the hard gate; a Default cell or a destructuring default marks only its own prop, so a props table whose Default cells are empty reads no prop as required. The judge is told a renamed prop is a mismatch, not a renamed-parameter difference, since callers set props by name. A partial label in a table's column header, such as `Props (simplified)`, now marks every row of that table partial. Every signature judge, the fallback per-file scan's subagents and a stack skill's reference judge included, reads these rules and the `difference` tags from one file, `signature-comparison-rules.md`, and Create Skill no longer says a component is always `(props: XProps) => JSX.Element`. ([#869](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/869); issue [#827](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/827))

  **Migration:** If a skill now stops at the hard gate on a component's `signature-mismatch` gap, write `?` on each optional prop of an object type that marks any (or give the table a Required column), list the required props it inherits, then run Test Skill again.

- **skf-test-skill, skf-update-skill:** Test Skill's split-body cross-check now compares two `references/` files that document one export when the `SKILL.md` body does not settle them (it does not document the export, or agrees with both); before, a contradiction between two reference files surfaced only when the inventory happened to carry the wrong form. Such a contradiction is a High `split-body-mismatch` gap titled `Split-body mismatch: {export} ({other_file}, {reference_file})`, so a skill that passed can now stop at the hard gate. When no source settles it, its Source is the reference file whose path sorts last, and Update Skill edits that file to match the other. `validate-inventory.py` accepts `other_file` and `other_line` in place of `skill_md_line`, and now refuses a pair out of order (the one that sorts first in codepoint order, by path and then line, is `other_file`) or a `reference_file` or `other_file` that is not a `references/` file of the skill. The Reference Consistency table's `SKILL.md Line` column is now `Other Side`. ([#879](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/879); issue [#841](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/841))

  **Migration:** If a skill now stops at the hard gate on a split-body gap between two reference files, run `@Ferris US <skill> --from-test-report` on that report, or edit the cited reference so both files document the export as its source declares, then run Test Skill again.

### Changed

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's split-body cross-check compares a parameter's optionality only when both forms state it. An ellipsis claims nothing about the parameters it stands for, and a call, a list of bare names or a form its own file labels partial may leave out a parameter the other form does not state as required, unless that shifts a caller's positions in a language without keyword arguments; any other form that leaves one out is still a mismatch. Each export's form is read alone, so `(action, sink, tracking_record, child_invalidation)` is no longer a High `split-body-mismatch` gap when other rows of its table write defaults, and two runs on an unchanged skill agree on it. ([#879](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/879); issue [#843](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/843))
- **skf-test-skill:** At the Deep tier, Test Skill no longer asks for a gh version check, a type cross-check or a re-export trace that nothing ran or recorded: at any tier, the workspace drift guard checks the local source tree against the pinned commit when both exist, the recipe runner traces each re-export to the file that defines it whenever it runs (the fallback per-file scan does not), and the signature check compares each documented signature with its declaration. A documentation error a Deep run sees that no script checks, such as an import path whose module does not export the name, is now an Info `observation` gap, `Not checked by script: <name>`, in the Gap Report, at the documenting line, whose remediation says to correct the documentation to match the source. It never blocks. ([#874](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/874); issue [#828](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/828))
- **skf-test-skill, skf-update-skill:** Test Skill's provenance line check now records a citation that does not resolve. An entry whose file the pinned source does not hold, such as `portable-stories.ts` for a `portable-stories.tsx` export, or whose line is past the end of its file or below 1, is a Low `provenance-line` gap, and a line that is not a number is an Info `provenance-unverified` gap; before, they reached no report line. Update Skill's `--from-test-report` moves an out-of-range line when the file defines the export on one line, and leaves an entry whose file is gone unchanged, with a warning that names the file. Neither gap changes a score or the hard gate. ([#875](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/875); issue [#832](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/832))

### Fixed

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's async/sync check no longer takes a call of a same-named method on another namespace as a call of the method it checks. The inventory now gives a method the class or object the skill documents it on (`owner`), while a function a module holds stays a `function`, and `locate-export-segments.py` counts only calls on that owner (`cognee.agents.get(...)`) or on a variable the same example binds to it (`gen = UuidGenerator()`); a call on a receiver it cannot tie is listed as unverified and raises nothing. So `cognee.config.get(...)` no longer gives the async `cognee.agents.get` a High finding that blocks the hard gate. A signature line that lists annotated parameters without a return type (`get(key: str, reveal_secrets: bool = False)`) now counts as a signature, not an unawaited call. ([#877](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/877), [#881](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/881); issue [#842](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/842))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's inventory reader now keeps the members a skill states once for several names. Where a skill documents several names together and states the members they share once, in one table row or paragraph, in a sentence or caption just above a table, or in the table's column header, such as record models that each take the same base fields followed by each model's own fields, the reader records each name's `params` as the shared text, then `; `, then that name's own members as the skill writes them, rather than the name's own fields alone. The signature comparison rules read the shared text as part of that form, so a model is no longer a Critical `signature-mismatch` gap for leaving out a required field the shared text documents, and two runs on an unchanged skill agree on it. ([#880](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/880))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill now plans the signature check of a name exported through a local `export { ... }` list, such as the `export { Button, buttonVariants }` that ends a shadcn/ui component file, at the declaration the judge compares instead of the list line, so the judge no longer searches the file for it. The recipe runner records such an item's same-file declaration in two new keys, `declaration_line` and `declaration_signature_line`, and keeps its `source_line`, `signature_line` and citation at the list, so Create Skill's citations do not change. The surface's `line` and `signatureLine` take the declaration, which also moves the Sources and Source Locations Test Skill takes from the surface to it. A list item that names an import or a destructured binding stays at the list. ([#867](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/867); issue [#836](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/836))
- **skf-test-skill:** A test report the hard gate blocks now records `analysisConfidence` in its frontmatter, as a scored one does: Test Skill writes it to the report the moment it resolves the source access, and again when it scores or blocks the run. Test Skill refuses to publish a report whose `analysisConfidence` is not `full`, `provenance-map`, `metadata-only`, `remote-only` or `docs-only`: it writes the source access it resolved and builds the result again, and halts before the report gets its public name only when the value is still refused. ([#874](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/874); issue [#823](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/823))
- **skf-test-skill:** Every Denominator line of Test Skill's report that carries a count now reads it from `surface.json`. `load-coverage-inputs.py surface` now writes `candidates.tierAIncludeFiles` and `candidates.scopeIncludeFiles` (the files that define each set's names) and `candidates.subpathEntries` (the in-scope subpaths the `subpaths` set reads, each counted once however many files it names), each null when its set is absent, so a report no longer carries a count made by hand, and a count no file gives reads `absent`. ([#874](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/874); issue [#822](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/822))
- **skf-test-skill, skf-create-skill, skf-update-skill, skf-create-stack-skill:** The provenance line check no longer reports a bookkeeping variant (`X_def`, `X_exact`, `a11y_X`) as unverified when its line defines `X`: when the cited file never names the variant, `skf-verify-provenance-completeness.py` checks the line against `X`, the fold Test Skill's Source Access Protocol defines. In an oms-storybook-react-vite run this clears 10 of 27 Info `provenance-unverified` gaps, such as `mockChannel_def`. A variant at a wrong line now gets the base's definition line, so Create Skill, Update Skill and Create Stack Skill move it as they move any entry. The fabricated-signature test still checks the documented name as written. ([#875](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/875); issue [#847](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/847))
- **skf-update-skill:** Update Skill's `--from-test-report` repair now reads the skill brief's scope and never repairs an export from a file a gap cites or its Remediation names that the scope leaves out. In 5.0.0 a gap whose Source was another package's file that declares the name itself, such as Vue's own `definePreview` while the provenance map holds `@storybook/react-vite`'s, rewrote the export's documentation from that file, and a gap on a name the map does not hold was re-extracted from a cited or Remediation file outside the scope and added to the map. Such a gap now ends `unknown`, whatever its severity and with no halt: `cited-elsewhere` with `citation_check` `outside-scope` when the map holds the name, `outside-scope` otherwise; the map and the documentation stay as they were, and a `provenance:` warning names the file and the fix (when the skill covers it, change the brief's `scope.include` or `scope.exclude` so the scope takes it, else re-run Test Skill). A skill with no brief repairs as before, and so does a file the scope takes, so when the scope takes several packages that declare the name, still check each gap's Source before the repair. Each verification record `skf-build-change-manifest.py gap-records` writes now carries `outside_scope`, the files the gap names that the scope left out. ([#868](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/868); issue [#824](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/824))
- **skf-update-skill:** Update Skill's `--from-test-report` repair now records the warnings of every gap it does not route in one call right after each translation, not one call per gap, and a rescope re-run keeps its own output, so a re-run that fails loses none of the first run's warnings. The spot-check records and the provenance map write record their `provenance:` warnings the same way, one call each. The result emitter's `record` takes `--warning` more than once and a `--warnings-file`; a repeated `--warning` used to keep only the last. ([#874](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/874); issue [#825](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/825))

## [5.0.0](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/compare/v4.0.0...v5.0.0) (2026-11-04)

### Breaking changes

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill now compares the signature of a function the skill documents as taking no argument with `params: ""` (the form the inventory gives a function that takes none) and no return type. Such an entry was left out of Signature Accuracy, so a skill that documents a component as `X()` while its source takes props passed unchecked; an entry with `params: []` was already compared. The entry is now planned, counted and compared, which can raise new Critical `signature-mismatch` gaps, so a skill that passed Test Skill can now stop at its hard gate. Only a function's empty `params` counts: a type or a constant with `params: ""` is still not compared. When the inventory lists a name more than once, an entry that lists its parameters or gives a usage form is compared before one that gives neither, then a full form before a partial one, then one that lists its parameters before one that gives only a usage form. On a skill whose zero-argument entries match the source, those entries now count toward Signature Accuracy and raise no gap. ([#850](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/850), [#862](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/862), [#864](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/864); issue [#794](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/794))

  **Migration:** For a skill that now stops at the hard gate on such a gap, run `@Ferris US <skill> --from-test-report` on that test report, or document by hand the parameters the source declares (for a component, its props), then run Test Skill again. In a monorepo, first check that each gap's Source is a file of the package the skill documents: when the skill's citations name none or several of the files that declare the name, Test Skill can cite another package's declaration of it, and the repair would rewrite the export's documentation from that file. Fix such a gap by hand instead, with an `[AST:]` or `[SRC:]` citation of the skill's own file on the line that names the export, so the next test compares that declaration.

### Added

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's inventory now records `signature_form: "partial"` for a signature the skill labels partial (such as `Props (simplified)`, a summary of the key parameters, or a `...` that stands in for omitted members, not rest or variadic syntax), and an optional parameter or member such a form leaves out is an Info `observation` titled `Partial signature: {name}` instead of a Critical `signature-mismatch` gap: the run is not blocked, and Signature Accuracy counts the signature as matching. The signature judge tags that difference `"difference": "omitted-optional"`, and `score-signatures.py` lowers it only when the inventory marks the form partial, so a form the skill does not label partial is still held to every parameter the source declares. The split-body cross-check no longer reports such a form against the full one a reference file gives. `validate-inventory.py` accepts a `signature_form` of `partial` or `full` and refuses any other value. The Coverage Analysis table shows such a signature as matching (`yes (Info)`), rates its row WARN, not FAIL, and leaves it out of the Signature Mismatches count. ([#834](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/834); issue [#816](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/816))
- **skf-update-skill:** The `SKF_UPDATE_RESULT_JSON` line's `files_written` can now name `references`, listed when the run wrote, added or removed one or more `references/*.md` files (the merge, the provenance fixes or a body split). Before, the emitter refused a payload that named a reference file, so a pipeline could not see that `references/` changed, which can be the only content change of a `--from-test-report` repair. ([#854](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/854); issue [#799](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/799))

### Changed

- **skf-analyze-source, skf-audit-skill, skf-brief-skill, skf-create-skill, skf-test-skill, skf-update-skill:** The recipe runner (`skf-extract-public-api.py --mode full`) now reads the names bound by a destructuring pattern that opens an `export const`, `let` or `var` statement, such as storybook/test's `export const { fireEvent, within } = lib;`, whether the names share the line or sit on lines of their own. Each such name the package's entry points export, directly or through `export *`, is now on the public surface (`entry_point_diff.public`, counted in `exports_public_api` and `effective_denominator`) and, since no recipe matches it, an `extraction_gaps` row at its own line, so Create Skill's read-by-eye pass is pointed at it. Before, these names reached neither list and no warning named them. Analyze Source, Audit Skill and Brief Skill read the runner's public names, counts and gaps, so their public-API counts and surfaces now include these names, and a skill that does not document them can show new missing exports in Test Skill. A pattern after the statement's first declarator (`export const a = 1, { b } = o`), or one the runner cannot read (one that does not close, or a default holding a template literal over several lines), still binds nothing with no warning, so read it by eye. Quick mode (`--mode quick`) is unchanged: it still warns about the statement and leaves its names to be read by eye. ([#829](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/829); issue [#786](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/786))
- **skf-create-skill, skf-test-skill, skf-update-skill, skf-audit-skill, skf-brief-skill, skf-analyze-source:** When two packages of a monorepo each define a public name, such as `composeStories` in Storybook's core and React renderer, Test Skill now compares the documented signature with the declaration the skill cites instead of reporting a false Critical `signature-mismatch` against the other package's, and its `scope.include` and `tier_a_include` sets count the name when any in-scope file that defines it matches. The recipe runner keeps every in-scope definition of a public name, in every language family, listing those beside its `public` row in the new `entry_point_diff.other_definitions` (`--mode denominator` reads them from `--extraction`), and a star re-export that the entry point's own export of the name shadows no longer moves that row. So `effective_denominator` can rise by the names that regain an in-scope file or drop where such a star counted one, and `curated_subset` can turn true when the basis leaves out a file that defines a counted name, which can change whether Create Skill and Update Skill store the count; `exports_public_api` does not change. The `root` and `subpaths` sets hold a name any root or subpath entry point gives. A `public-api` skill marks each such definition `public: true` and documents it, and Brief Skill lists its file. A re-export that names a workspace package (`from '@storybook/react'`) is still not followed. ([#863](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/863); issue [#830](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/830))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill now grades a renamed parameter that callers cannot see as a Low `signature-mismatch` gap instead of a Critical one, so it no longer stops a run at the hard gate, and Signature Accuracy counts the signature as matching. The signature judge tags a mismatch whose only difference is a parameter name with `"difference": "parameter-name"`, and `score-signatures.py` lowers it only when the file the surface records for the export is a `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.mts`, `.cts`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.go`, `.rs`, `.java`, `.c`, `.h`, `.cc`, `.cpp`, `.cxx` or `.hpp` file, whose callers pass arguments by position, and the judge reported it there. A renamed Python parameter stays Critical, because the script cannot see which parameters a caller must pass by position, and so does every other difference. The Coverage Analysis table shows such a signature as matching (`yes (Low)`), rates its row WARN, not FAIL, and leaves it out of the Signature Mismatches count. ([#834](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/834); issue [#793](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/793))
- **skf-update-skill, skf-test-skill:** Update Skill's `--from-test-report` repair no longer repairs a `stale-documentation` or a `metadata-drift` gap. A `stale-documentation` gap (documentation for a name the source surface lacks), which Update Skill used to route, is now listed under "Not repaired by this run" with its reason, and the repair writes nothing for it; before, it gained a provenance entry with no `source_file` and a place in `exports[]`. A `metadata-drift` gap is listed the same way: the update recounts those counts each time it writes the skill, so its metadata patch never held and the gap came back on every test. Every gap the repair leaves now carries a reason that says who repairs it: the `test-report: not routed:` warning ends with it, and each `not_routed[]` item gains a `reason` key. Test Skill's `metadata-drift` remediation now sends diverging barrel counts to Create Skill, which rebuilds `exports[]` from the source, explains diverging documented-surface counts by the `Type::method` entries they differ by, and no longer says Update Skill applies either; its FAIL recommendation says which gaps Update Skill repairs. ([#833](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/833); issues [#798](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/798), [#803](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/803))

### Fixed

- **all workflows, skf-forger:** Customization overrides in `_bmad/custom/<skill>.toml` and `_bmad/custom/<skill>.user.toml` apply again on BMAD core 6.4.0 to 6.10.0. Every workflow, and Ferris, passed BMAD core's customization resolver `--project-root`, a flag core takes only from 6.11.0, so on an older core the resolver stopped with a `usage:` line, the run warned `customization_resolver_unavailable` without saying why, and the overrides were ignored. Each run now goes through SKF's own helper, `skf-resolve-customization.py`, which runs core's resolver with `--project-root` and, when an older core rejects it, runs it again without the flag if that core would read this project's overrides on its own. When it would read another folder's, such as a submodule's or another repository's, the run keeps the bundled defaults and warns `customization_resolver_unavailable: BMAD core before 6.11.0: ...`, naming that folder and the upgrade to 6.11.0 or later. Core 6.11.0 and later run as before, in one call with the flag. ([#775](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/775); issue [#770](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/770))
- **installer:** The tool report that `install`, `update` and `status` print now shows the version of a `skill-check` installed globally with npm, yarn or bun (with npm on Windows) instead of `installed, version unknown`. skill-check has no `--version` option, so the check reads the version from the installed package's `package.json` and no longer runs skill-check. ([#773](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/773); issue [#768](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/768))
- **installer:** The tool check that `install`, `update` and `status` run no longer runs tessl. Since v3.0.0 it ran `tessl --version`, which could start tessl's own update check and update download and, on a tessl that had never run, accepted tessl's Terms and saved tessl's default preferences, usage sharing on, in `~/.tessl/preferences.json` without asking. `tessl config set shareUsageData false` turns usage sharing off. The check now reads tessl's version from the name of the binary tessl installs, `tessl-<version>-<platform>` in tessl's `versions` folder: the file `~/.local/bin/tessl` links to, which is also the one the npm and Homebrew `tessl` launchers run (their own package version can differ), or on Windows the file `tessl\bin\tessl.exe` was copied from. An `@tessl/cli` before 0.63.0 is tessl itself, not a launcher, so the check reads its package version. tessl no longer reads `installed, version unknown` when it is slow to start. It still reads `installed, version unknown` when it was installed with winget, pnpm or Volta, when an npm or Homebrew launcher's binary is not installed at `~/.local/bin/tessl` (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\tessl\bin\tessl.exe` on Windows), or when two files in `tessl\versions` have the size of the Windows copy. ([#773](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/773), [#774](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/774); issue [#768](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/768))
- **skf-create-skill, skf-test-skill, skf-update-skill, skf-audit-skill, skf-brief-skill, skf-analyze-source:** The recipe runner (`skf-extract-public-api.py --mode full`) now counts a TS/JS export whose name starts with `_`, as the Source API Surface Definition and quick mode do. Such a name a package's entry points export, such as storybook's `__definePreview`, which `export * from './preview'` passes on, is now an export and a public name like any other: counted in `exports_public_api` (and, in scope, `effective_denominator`), an extraction gap when no recipe found it, and a signature Test Skill checks. Before, every `_` name was dropped, so such a name was neither public, internal nor a gap, and a wrong documented signature for it went unchecked. Python, Rust and Dart `_` names stay private: Python's by the Source API Surface Definition, Rust's because such an item is hidden (a `#[doc(hidden)] pub mod __private`) or unnamed (`pub const _`), and Dart's because the language keeps it private to its library. A skill that does not document a TS/JS `_` export can now show it as a missing export in Test Skill, Analyze Source and Brief Skill read it among the runner's exports, and Update Skill and Audit Skill take it from the runner rather than reading it by eye. Denominator mode (`--mode denominator`) now counts in `exports_internal` a `_` export of any other language too (TS/JS, Java, Kotlin and the rest) when no public name has it. Quick mode is unchanged. ([#831](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/831); issue [#817](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/817))
- **skf-create-skill, skf-test-skill, skf-update-skill, skf-audit-skill, skf-brief-skill, skf-analyze-source:** When several package entry points export one name and the first of them by path is out of scope, the recipe runner (`skf-extract-public-api.py --mode full`) now records the name where an in-scope entry point defines it, so `entry_point_diff.public` carries the in-scope file and line, Test Skill finds the name's kind and signature line there, and `effective_denominator` counts it. In a storybook skill whose brief scopes in only the `react-vite` framework, `defineMain` was recorded at the Angular framework's file, out of scope, with no kind or signature line. An entry point's own explicit export still wins over a name its `export *` passes on. A name whose only exporting entry point is out of scope, defined in a file out of scope, is now an `entry_point_diff.outside_scope` name, outside `effective_denominator`, even when a recipe found the same name in another file, which is another definition; before, it was neither an extraction gap nor outside scope. Brief Skill's tier A candidates leave out the files of `outside_scope` names, and Analyze Source reads the same public names and counts. The first Audit Skill re-index after the upgrade can list as added the names the runner now reads at their in-scope file. ([#831](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/831); issue [#787](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/787))
- **skf-create-skill, skf-update-skill:** The body split (`skf-shard-body.py`) no longer overwrites a reference file. When `references/<name>.md` already holds other content, or two moved sections take the same name, the section goes to the next free `<name>-2.md`, `<name>-3.md` and so on, as `skill-check split-body` names them, and the `> See` pointer in `SKILL.md` names that file. Before, the second section replaced the first one's file, and its content was lost. ([#854](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/854))
- **skf-export-skill:** The token report's Context Budget Impact now reads each value from the token helper (`skf-count-tokens.py`), which emits them as `context_budget` (`always_on`, `on_trigger`, `full_disclosure` and `snippet`), with the managed section's skill count (`managed_section.skills`) and the target files that hold it (`managed_section.target_files`). The full disclosure cost is SKILL.md plus `references/`, never the package total, which also counts the snippet and metadata.json, so two runs on the same skill report the same cost. The always-on cost names the context file it was measured in, and reads N/A when no context file holds the managed section. In a multi-skill export, the report gives the always-on cost once and each skill's budget on its own line. ([#840](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/840); issue [#819](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/819))
- **skf-export-skill, skf-update-skill:** Export Skill now keeps a gotcha that the current SKILL.md states, even when the evidence report records no T2-future annotation. Before, such a gotcha was marked `[CARRIED]` on one export and dropped on the next. A gotcha now counts as current when the evidence report's T2-future annotations state it, or when SKILL.md states it in a gotchas, deprecation, migration, breaking-change or import-correction section, in a `## Key API Summary` row that says deprecated or removed, or as an `await` call in its Quick Start. The `|gotchas:` line now holds at most 3 pitfalls, separated by `; `: the prior pitfalls still stated come first, then new ones. `[CARRIED]` now marks a single pitfall that nothing current states, and that pitfall is dropped, with a warning, on the export after. The `|api:` line now has a fixed order, so it no longer changes from one export to the next. The order is the prior `|api:` names, then the `## Key API Summary` rows, then the metadata.json `exports`. A name appears only when `exports` lists it and SKILL.md does not mark it deprecated or removed. The line holds 10 names at Deep tier and 5 at the other tiers. The first export after this change can rewrite a skill's `|api:` line once. The `#quick-start` and `#key-types` anchors now stay on SKILL.md when SKILL.md has the heading, and point into `references/` only for a split-body skill whose SKILL.md lacks it. Update Skill follows the same rules when it regenerates a snippet. It also regenerates a snippet whose anchors are wrong. A gap-driven repair still leaves the snippet alone when only the `|api:` order would change. ([#840](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/840); issues [#810](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/810), [#811](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/811), [#818](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/818))
- **skf-quick-skill, skf-create-stack-skill, skf-update-skill:** The output validator (`skf-validate-output.py`) no longer warns about a context snippet of 201 to 300 tokens. Its long-snippet warning now uses the same 300-token ceiling as Export Skill, at every tier. A snippet above 300 tokens still gets a low-severity warning, and the warning now names the 300-token ceiling. Create Stack Skill's validation step now quotes the same bounds, 40 and 300 tokens. ([#840](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/840); issue [#812](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/812))
- **skf-test-skill:** When the inflation guard fires because the brief's `scope.include` union sweeps in internal infrastructure, and a stratified-scope or multi-entry skill's Export Coverage counts that union, Test Skill's gap ledger now records one Medium `denominator-inflation` gap at the skill brief, titled "undocumented names in the inflated scope.include union", instead of one Medium `missing-export` gap per undocumented name. It sits beside the guard's own `denominator-inflation` gap at the same brief and defers to it: correct the denominator as that gap says, then re-run Test Skill, and the names the corrected denominator counts that the skill does not document come back as gaps. Its issue gives the size of the union and lists up to 50 of the names, each marked when it is a type and given its file and line when the surface records one, then how many more. Before, a skill whose union counted dozens of infrastructure names got a "document this export" gap for each, which Update Skill's gap-driven mode would then add to the skill. Other skills, and a union the surface lacked, keep one gap per name. The Export Coverage score does not change. ([#856](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/856); issue [#795](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/795))
- **skf-test-skill:** A name the skill documents that an entry point exports, but from a file the brief scopes out, is still a Medium `stale-documentation` gap, and when the brief is the cause the gap now says so. Its issue names the entry point and the file and line that define the name, and its remediation names the skill brief and the fix: to keep the documentation, narrow the `scope.exclude` glob that matches the file (removing it takes a `demoted-exclude` amendment in the brief) or, when no `scope.include` glob covers the file, widen `scope.include`; otherwise remove the documentation. Before, the gap said the source does not export the name and never mentioned the brief. A file out of scope for another reason, such as one no recipe reads, keeps the old wording. Each `excluded.outsideScope` row in `surface.json` now carries the name's `line` and `entry`, with `excludeGlob` and `outsideInclude` saying why the brief scopes the file out, and the Coverage Summary's "Scoped Out by the Brief" line now gives each file with its line. ([#856](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/856); issue [#796](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/796))
- **skf-test-skill:** On the scalar coverage branch, Export Coverage now counts only the documented names in the denominator's set when that set can be trusted. Before, the numerator was every documented name the skill writes, so each documented extra offset an undocumented export: a skill of five exports that documents three of them and two names the source does not export read 100% with nothing missing. It now reads 60% and lists the two undocumented names. `load-coverage-inputs.py surface` writes a new `denominator.setCounted`, true only for a scope set (not `all`) whose every name sits at the file that defines it: a complete runner extraction (neither `incomplete` nor truncated), the fallback per-file scan, or quick output that traces each name. On such a set, `coverage.json` reports `numeratorSource` `surface`, lists the undocumented names in `missing` and gives the set's name and size (`surfaceSet`, `surfaceSetSize`); the denominator stays the stored count, with a warning when the two differ. The ledger records a Medium `missing-export` gap per missing name at the file the surface records for it (or, as on the barrel branch, one summary gap at the brief when the inflation guard fired on that `scope.include` set), plus one gap for the rest when the stored count exceeds the set's names, and the Coverage Analysis section shows the per-export table and a new `Coverage Warnings` line. Over `all`, a set read by eye or from an incomplete extraction, or an empty set (which warns), the numerator is looked up as before, the verified numerator count still replaces it when inflated, and one gap covers the count. Export Coverage can drop on skills whose set is counted. ([#859](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/859); issue [#792](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/792))
- **skf-test-skill:** On the scalar coverage branch, where a stratified-scope, specific-modules or multi-entry skill is measured against its stored `stats.effective_denominator`, Test Skill now reports a documented name the source does not export. The coverage step passes `reconcile-coverage.py` the surface (`--surface` and `--surface-set`), and when the surface was read from the source, `coverage.json` lists in `stale` each documented name the whole public surface lacks (the `all` set together with the denominator's set, so a nested package's name is not stale), with `staleApplicable` true. This holds whether or not the branch counts its set. The run grades each name as it does on the barrel branch: a Critical `fabricated-signature` gap when no file its provenance cites defines it, an Info `observation` for a documented extra the source still declares, else a Medium `stale-documentation` gap. Before, the scalar branch never listed a stale name. A documented name the denominator's set leaves out but the source exports, such as a Tier B name of a stratified skill, is not stale. ([#859](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/859); issue [#791](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/791))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill now compares a documented signature with the declaration the skill cites. For a name the source surface records in more than one file, such as a function each framework package of a monorepo defines, the signature check read whichever file sorted first, so a skill that documents another package's declaration got a false Critical `signature-mismatch` gap. `score-signatures.py plan` now takes `--skill-dir` and plans the check at the file that the skill's `[AST:]` or `[SRC:]` citation names on a line naming the export. When the citations name none of those files or several, the check lists each declaration as `candidates`: the judge reports one mismatch, at the closest candidate, only when the documented signature matches none of them, and names that candidate in the mismatch's new optional `file` key, which becomes the gap's Source. `score-signatures.py score` reads the plan (`--plan`), takes a mismatch's `file` only when the plan offered it for that check (any other is a warning) and keeps one mismatch per check. A surface record with no file no longer takes the check from one with a file. The judge, and each subagent of the fallback per-file scan, is also told that a documented signature matching the implementation of an overload set, or any of its overloads, is no mismatch; no script checks this. ([#850](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/850), [#862](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/862); issues [#781](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/781), [#845](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/845))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill no longer raises a High finding that blocks the hard gate when an example awaits a function the skill describes as sync only through another call: as an argument of an awaited call (`await coco.mount(coco.component_subpath("p", f), g)`), or under a member chained after it (`await coco.use_context(E).embed(t)`). `locate-export-segments.py` now reports for each call whether the await applies to the call itself (`directlyAwaited`) and how it is awaited (`awaitedVia`, with the `enclosingCallee` of an enclosing call), and the sync check raises its finding only for a call awaited directly, or for one in the arguments of an awaited `asyncio.gather`, `asyncio.wait` or `asyncio.wait_for` or of a runner such as `asyncio.run`, `loop.run_until_complete` or Rust's `block_on`. The finding's Source now cites the file of the call it names, which can be a `references/*.md` file, instead of always `SKILL.md`. ([#838](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/838); issue [#783](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/783))
- **skf-test-skill:** The Test Skill subagent that lists a skill's documented exports now writes its JSON to `inventory-response.txt` in the run folder with the Write tool and returns the path, so the main agent no longer copies the whole response into that file by hand. A subagent that cannot write files returns the JSON instead, and the main agent saves it whenever the subagent returned the JSON or left the file absent or empty. Before the one re-dispatch after a failed validation, the refused file is deleted, so a stale response is never validated twice. ([#857](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/857); issue [#814](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/814))
- **skf-test-skill:** When a skill's `evidence-report.md` pins no usable `t2_future_count` (the field is absent, empty, `null` or quoted, or the report has no frontmatter, as in every report Create Stack Skill writes), Test Skill's migration section check now records that the report pins no count, and tells you to re-run Create Skill only for a skill Create Skill made, instead of saying the file was not found. The note now has its own line in the report's Coherence Analysis section. A report with Windows line endings is now read the same as any other, where before its pinned count was never found. The check still raises no gap, and a skill with no evidence report at all still skips it with no note. ([#857](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/857); issue [#784](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/784))
- **skf-test-skill:** At Forge tier, Test Skill now reads by eye each file the recipe runner could not parse or decode (a syntax error or a file that is not UTF-8) whenever the runner lists one, not only when the run is `incomplete`, reads those files once, and lists them in the Coverage Analysis section as read by eye. A complete run that listed such a file used to leave it to the recipes, so an export they missed there was left off the API surface Test Skill measures coverage against. A file the runner could not open at all (`missing` or `unreadable`) is no longer sent to be read by eye: the Coverage Analysis section lists it as unread. ([#857](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/857); issue [#789](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/789))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's report template and the frontmatter its first step writes into a new report now list the same keys, and the step says its frontmatter replaces the template's. The two lists used to differ (the template had no `thresholdSource`, the step no `health_check_dispatched`) and nothing said which one won, so a report could start without the threshold source that scoring reads back from it. ([#857](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/857); issue [#777](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/777))
- **skf-test-skill:** On a stratified-scope, specific-modules or multi-entry skill whose brief lists `scope.tier_a_include` files, Test Skill now checks the stored `stats.effective_denominator` against the tier A set it re-derives from the source, when each name sits at the file that defines it (Forge tier and above, the fallback per-file scan, or Quick tier output that traces every name to its defining file). When the two differ by more than 25% in either direction, a Medium `metadata-drift` gap titled `denominator drift: effective_denominator disagrees with the brief's tier_a_include set` asks you to recount by re-running Create Skill, which stores the runner's tier A count when `effective_denominator_decision.store` holds and the brief's `scope.notes` documents the stratification, and otherwise drops the stored count. Until then a stratified-scope or multi-entry skill counts the tier A set and a specific-modules skill its `scope.include` set; an incomplete extraction, which can miss tier A names, keeps a stored count above the set. Before, a stale stored count stayed the denominator after the brief gained or changed its tier A list, so Export Coverage can now rise or fall on such a skill. A stored 0 the set counts any name against raises the same gap, with no percentage; only the gap is new, since a stored 0 was never the denominator. When the deflation and inflation guards both fire, the `scope.include` set stays the denominator and the `metadata-drift` and `denominator-inflation` gaps now name one fix: add or edit `scope.tier_a_include` in the brief to list the files that define the authored names (on an umbrella barrel, those files rather than the barrel), since the `scope.include` union is itself inflated. No guard gap asks you to set `stats.effective_denominator` by hand any more: Update Skill's next recount drops such a value. `surface.json` `guards.deflation` gains `basis` (`tier_a_include`, `scope.include` or `all`). ([#849](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/849); issues [#788](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/788), [#813](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/813))
- **skf-test-skill, skf-create-skill, skf-update-skill:** Test Skill no longer treats a skill's source as a monorepo because of a workspace whose members the skill brief's `scope.exclude` drops, such as a Rust workspace beside the Python package the skill documents, and so no longer picks the stratified-scope coverage denominator for it. A workspace member now counts only through the files the brief keeps: excluding its source files is enough to drop it (`rust/**`, `rust/**/*.rs` or `rust/*/src/**`), excluding only its manifest (`**/Cargo.toml`, or the root `Cargo.toml`) changes nothing, and a workspace with no member left is no workspace, while one with a member left still is. The recipe runner's monorepo arm (`arms.monorepo`) follows the same rule, so a skill whose only workspace the brief excludes stops storing `stats.effective_denominator` on its next Create Skill or Update Skill run. Whether `scope.include` lists a curated subset is decided as before, over every workspace of the source. ([#858](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/858); issue [#780](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/780))
- **skf-test-skill, skf-update-skill:** An export bound by destructuring, such as storybook/test's `export const { fireEvent, within } = lib;`, is now defined on the line where its name appears, whether the names share the line or sit on lines of their own. Test Skill no longer reports such an export as a Critical `fabricated-signature` gap whose remediation deletes correct documentation, and Update Skill's provenance check now verifies its entry, or moves a wrong line to the name's line, instead of leaving it unverified. An overloaded Python function's entry at a line that does not define it now moves to the function's first `@overload` stub instead of staying a `several-definition-lines` warning. ([#821](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/821); issues [#785](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/785), [#806](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/806), [#782](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/782))
- **skf-test-skill, skf-update-skill:** A split-body mismatch (the `SKILL.md` body and a `references/` file document one export differently) now points at the file the pinned source contradicts. When Test Skill reads the local source at the pinned commit, at the Forge tier or above, and one declaration settles it, its `split-body-mismatch` gap cites `SKILL.md` when the reference matches the declaration and the body does not, and cites the reference file otherwise; its remediation names the file to edit, the file whose form it takes and the declaration, or says that both forms agree with the source or that no source settled it. The gap's title now names the reference file, so two reference files that disagree with one body are two gaps. Update Skill's `--from-test-report` run keeps that citation as the manifest entry's `package_citation` and edits the file it names, changing only what contradicts and keeping each file's level of detail, where before it always copied the body into the reference file, even when the body was the wrong one. ([#848](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/848); issues [#778](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/778), [#779](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/779))
- **skf-update-skill:** Update Skill on a skill whose provenance map was written before entries carried a `signature_source` kept those entries without one, so the stats check reported a `confidence_distribution` violation that named no entry and that relabeling could not fix. The provenance write now gives each entry with no `signature_source`, or an unrecognized one, the tier its labels imply: its `confidence` when that is `T1-low`, `T2` or `T3`, else `T1` when its `extraction_method` is `ast-grep` or `ast_bridge`, else `T1-low`. Its summary counts these by tier in `signature_source_backfilled`, and the update report lists one warning for them, which names each unrecognized value it replaced. ([#853](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/853); issue [#802](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/802))
- **skf-update-skill:** When Update Skill recounts a skill's `stats.effective_denominator` to another value, or drops it, it now removes the `effective_denominator_*` stats keys that explained the old count (such as `effective_denominator_source`), with a warning that names each one, instead of keeping them beside the new count. Every other stats key an earlier run added that Create Skill does not write for the skill's scope type (such as a `reconciliation_note` a gap-driven repair added) stays, with a warning that names it, so a note that no longer matches the new counts gets reviewed instead of carried silently. ([#852](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/852); issue [#815](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/815))
- **skf-update-skill:** Update Skill's `--from-test-report` repair no longer re-extracts an export whose gap cites another file than the provenance map's entries of its name, as when the test compared another package's declaration: a gap on `definePreview` whose Source is Angular's `__definePreview`, while the map holds `definePreview` in `@storybook/react-vite`. In 4.0.0 such a blocking gap was re-extracted from the files its Remediation names: when one of them declared the exact name, the repair added a second provenance entry and merge replaced the correct export's documentation with that declaration; otherwise the run halted with `halted-for-remediation-path`. Such a gap now ends `unknown`, with `unknown_reason` `cited-elsewhere`, whatever its severity, and the run goes on without a halt: the provenance map and the export's documentation stay as they were, and merge now keeps the documented content of any gap-driven `MODIFIED_EXPORT` recorded `unknown` or `missing`, never rewriting it from the gap's text. The `provenance:` warning names the gap, the cited file and what its check there found (such as `missing` or `no-definition`), and where the map holds the name, with the fix: when the map is right, re-run Test Skill, and if the gap comes back, exclude the cited file in the brief's scope when the skill does not cover it; when an export moved, fix that map entry by hand, then re-run update-skill. When the check read nothing at the cited file, it says to give update-skill the source tree, re-install SKF, or fix what the check failed on, then re-run. One case is unchanged from 4.0.0: when the cited file declares the name itself, such as Vue's own `definePreview`, the check finds it there and the repair rewrites the export's documentation from that file, so before you run the repair on a monorepo skill, check that each gap's Source is a file of the package the skill documents. Each verification record `skf-build-change-manifest.py gap-records` writes now carries `citation_check` and `map_locations`, set for such a gap. ([#861](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/861), [#864](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/864); issue [#824](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/824))
- **skf-update-skill:** Update Skill's `--from-test-report` repair now takes the signature of each export its spot-check locates from the source. When the check finds the export at its recorded line or at the line it moved to (a `signature-mismatch` gap on an export the provenance map holds, or a cited export the map lacks), the targeted re-extraction now reads that file as well, and the repair takes the export's type, parameters and return type from the record the recipe runner gives at that line: SKILL.md documents them and the provenance map records them. Before, an export the map held kept its old `params` and `return_type` while SKILL.md was repaired (a moved one changed only its line), and a cited new export took its signature from the repaired documentation, so the map and SKILL.md could disagree and the gap came back on the next test. A repaired entry keeps its confidence and extraction method; an `ast-grep` or `ast_bridge` entry takes `signature_source` from the record, and the update report lists each one that changes, such as a signature read by eye that moves an entry from T1 to T1-low. A cited new export keeps its `source-read` labels. An export the runner does not report at that line keeps its signature, with a warning, and a cited new export then takes it from the documentation, as before. `skf-build-change-manifest.py gap-records --plan` lists these exports in `reextract.signatures`, each verification record gains `params`, `return_type`, `extraction_method` and `ast_node_type` beside `export_type`, the `targeted_reextraction` evidence record gains `signature_files_scanned`, and the record call needs `--remediation-records` whenever the plan lists a file. ([#846](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/846); issues [#804](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/804), [#809](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/809))
- **skf-update-skill:** Update Skill's `--from-test-report` repair now finds an export a test report names by the public name of a renamed re-export. The recipe runner names each export after its declaration, so a gap naming `experimental_MockUniversalStore`, which the package re-exports from `MockUniversalStore`, matched nothing in the targeted re-extraction, and a blocking gap halted the run with `halted-for-remediation-path`. At Forge tier and above, `skf-build-change-manifest.py records` now lists in each record's `aliases` the public names the runner's entry-point diff gives its declared name in that file, and `gap-records` matches a gap by its exact name first, then by such a public name, within the gap's own paths. The repair documents the export under its public name and maps it as a barrel rename: the provenance entry keeps the declared `export_name` at the declaration's line, with `reexported_as` the public name, which metadata.json's `exports[]` lists, so the provenance check passes and a later repair of the same gap finds that entry. At Quick tier, or when the recipe runner finds no `ast-grep` it can run, such a gap still ends unresolved. ([#855](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/855); issue [#807](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/807))
- **skf-update-skill:** On a skill whose body was split into `references/`, Update Skill now applies a removed, moved, renamed, changed or new export to every file that documents it, `SKILL.md` and each `references/*.md` file alike, and a new export also corrects a reference line that called it not covered. A reference file a removal leaves documenting nothing is deleted, with the `> See` pointer to it. A [MANUAL] block in a reference file is left as it is, since only those in `SKILL.md` are verified. A `--from-test-report` repair now writes every reference file the merge changed or added, not only those its structural fixes touched. Before, the reference files kept the old text, so they could contradict `SKILL.md` after the update. ([#854](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/854); issue [#800](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/800))
- **skf-update-skill:** In a skill whose provenance map names several libraries (Storybook's names `@storybook/react`, `storybook` and `storybook/test`), Update Skill gave every export it added to the map the `source_library` of the map's first entry, whatever file the export is in. A new entry now takes the library the other entries of its file name, else the one the entries under the nearest folder above it name; when they name a library and its subpaths, such as `storybook` beside `storybook/test`, it takes the library itself. An export in a moved file, or one that moved from another file, also tries its old file. When neither settles it, or the export has no source file, the entry takes the map's first library as before, and one warning counts and names those entries so you can correct them. ([#853](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/853); issue [#808](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/808))
- **skf-update-skill:** Update Skill now records in `metadata.json` `tool_versions` the toolchain that last wrote the skill, as Create Skill does: `skf` names the installed SKF version (`unknown`, with a warning, when it cannot be read), and `ast_grep` and `qmd` name the versions this update ran. A tool the update did not use keeps the version recorded before. Until now every update kept the versions of the run that created the skill, so a skill an SKF 4.0.0 update rewrote still named SKF 3.0.0. ([#852](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/852); issue [#801](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/801))
- **skf-update-skill:** Update Skill now splits the `SKILL.md` body when skill-check reports `body.max_tokens`, as it already did for `body.max_lines`, so an update that adds content no longer leaves the token warning in place and the quality score at 90. It runs `skf-shard-body.py`, which moves the largest `## Full` sections to `references/` until the body is within 400 lines (500 when only the token warning is reported) and 4,500 words, keeps Tier 1 inline and never moves a section a [MANUAL] block reaches into. `skill-check split-body` now runs only when that helper is missing. When no such section is left to move, the run records a `Spec compliance: WARN` with that reason in `warnings[]` instead of trimming Tier 1; a helper that fails stops the run with `blocked` (`write:body-split`), naming any reference file it already wrote; and the evidence report's Validation Summary lists each section a split moved. `skf-shard-body.py` gains `--word-budget` and `--skip-manual`, and its report gains `body_words_before`, `body_words_after`, `under_word_budget` and `word_budget`. ([#854](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/854); issue [#797](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/797))
- **skf-update-skill:** Update Skill's `--from-test-report` repair now says why it could not check a new or modified export the provenance map already holds, and what to fix. When the map holds several entries of the export's name, or the spot-check of its entry ends `unknown` or `missing` (the entry's file is gone), the repair leaves its entries as they were, as before, and its `provenance:` warning now gives the cause of an `unknown`, such as `ambiguous`, `no-definition`, `several-definitions` or `unchecked-language`. For a gap of a severity other than Medium, Low or Info, the warning also names the gap and the one fix a re-run acts on: fix the entry by hand (its `source_file` and `source_line`), or, for several entries of the name, give the gap a `file:line` Source at the definition when that file holds only one of them. Before, the warning gave only the export and the outcome, while the gap-driven step said every such gap is read from the source or halts the run; it now says these entries stay unchanged, with that warning. Each verification record `skf-build-change-manifest.py gap-records` writes now carries its `gap_id`, and an `unknown` one its cause in `unknown_reason`. ([#855](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/855); issue [#805](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/805))

### Documentation

- Verifying a Skill now walks through the published oms-cognee 1.6.2 `search` provenance entry, which passes the line, label and citation checks (an ast-grep match on its `def` line, labeled `T1`, cited `[AST:]` in `SKILL.md`), and keeps the older 1.0.0 entry as the example of what those checks catch. Its score table quotes the four oh-my-skills test reports from SKF 4.0.0, including the oms-storybook-react-vite repair that named its story-authoring tier in `scope.tier_a_include` instead of documenting internal exports. The examples, skill model and getting started pages now follow oms-cognee 1.6.2. ([#820](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/820); issue [#761](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/761))
- Verifying a Skill now quotes strict SKF 4.0.0 re-tests of oh-my-skills' four reference skills, run against the version each one ships. The earlier passes (oms-cocoindex 100%, oms-cognee 99.00%, oms-uitripled 100%, oms-storybook-react-vite 95.17%) mostly read the signature rules leniently, and strict re-tests that apply the written rule blocked all four at first. After fixes, oms-cocoindex passes at 100% and oms-cognee at 99%, both on borderline calls their reports write down. oms-uitripled is blocked by one gap oh-my-skills judges to be a false positive, and oms-storybook-react-vite by two false positives and two older real errors that are not fixed yet. `docs/_data/pinned.yaml` records those scores (`test_score: null` for the two blocked skills). The worked example walks through how storybook's earlier score turned out to be too high, and the skill model's oms-cognee excerpt shows its new counts (t1 37, t1_low 49). ([#851](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/851))

## [4.0.0](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/compare/v3.0.0...v4.0.0) (2026-10-15)

### Breaking changes

- **skf-brief-skill, skf-create-skill, skf-test-skill:** A `scope.tier_a_include` glob now counts a public name only in a file that a `scope.include` glob also matches, in the count Create Skill stores and in the `tier_a_include` set Test Skill re-derives alike. Create Skill used to count names in files `scope.include` leaves out while Test Skill dropped most of them, so a tier A list over such files only stored a count that raised a Medium `metadata-drift` gap naming no cause, and a list mixing them with files in scope scored Export Coverage over names the surface leaves out. Create Skill now warns `scope.tier_a_include pattern '<glob>' matches only files outside scope.include` for each such glob, and a list that counts no name in scope falls back to `scope.include` with its warning. Brief Skill no longer proposes as tier A candidates the files whose names the recipe runner lists as outside the scope (`entry_point_diff.outside_scope`). A name a stale `scope.include` glob restores no longer counts in a tier A list either, so a count Create Skill stored from a tier A glob over such a name's file now raises the deflation guard's Medium `metadata-drift` gap, and a run that passed can fail. ([#729](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/729); issue [#725](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/725))

  **Migration:** Re-run Create Skill on each skill whose brief has `scope.tier_a_include`, then Test Skill. On the warning that a tier A glob matches only files outside `scope.include`, widen `scope.include` to cover the file or remove the glob from `scope.tier_a_include`.

- **skf-create-skill, skf-test-skill:** When no `scope.tier_a_include` glob in a skill brief counts a public name (each matches no file, or only files `scope.exclude` drops or that define no public name, such as a barrel that only re-exports), the tier A list no longer narrows the coverage denominator to zero. Create Skill counts over `scope.include` instead (every file when the brief has none), warns that the tier A globs count no public name, and stores that count only when `scope.include` lists a curated subset. Test Skill falls back to the `scope.include` set, checks a stored count against it and raises a Medium `metadata-drift` or `denominator-inflation` gap that says the globs count no public name. A stored `stats.effective_denominator` of 0 is now such a `metadata-drift` gap once the source defines a public name, not a halt on 0 exports discovered in source. The per-file scan Test Skill runs when ast-grep cannot be used makes the same checks and reports a stale tier A glob as a `brief-scope-stale` gap. Export Coverage and Type Coverage can fall, so a run that passed can fail. ([#720](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/720); issue [#712](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/712))

  **Migration:** Re-run Test Skill at Forge tier on each skill whose `metadata.json` stores `stats.effective_denominator`. On a deflation or inflation gap that says no `scope.tier_a_include` glob in the brief matches a file or counts a public name, edit or remove those globs in the skill brief by hand, then re-run Create Skill.

- **skf-test-skill:** At Quick tier, Test Skill now parses the entry points of every Python, JavaScript or TypeScript skill read from a local source with `skf-extract-public-api.py --mode quick`, as it already did for a skill Quick Skill built, instead of reading them by eye, and places each name at the file that defines it. Quick mode gives each Python, JavaScript and TypeScript export a new `defined_in` key when it reads files under `--source-root`: the file that defines the name, traced through each import, re-export, `export *` and star import to the end of its chain, or null when the chain leaves `--source-root`. `source_file` still names the entry file read, so the export list Brief Skill shows and Quick Skill's `metadata.json` do not change. A name an entry file passes on from a file the skill brief scopes out (outside `scope.include`, or dropped by `scope.exclude`) no longer counts in the `scope.include` set, as at Forge tier, so it is no longer scored as missing and no longer fires the deflation or inflation guard over a correct stored `stats.effective_denominator`. A name behind a statement the parser warns on, such as the entry file's own `export *` or a Python star import with no literal `__all__`, is still read by eye at the entry file, so it still counts in that set when its file is scoped out and can still fire either guard. A `scope.tier_a_include` glob over the files that define the names can now give a `tier_a_include` set at Quick tier. Export Coverage can move either way: the parser can list a name the read by eye left out, so a run that passed can fail. ([#758](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/758); issue [#750](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/750))

  **Migration:** Re-run Test Skill at Quick tier on each Python, JavaScript or TypeScript skill Create Skill built from a local source, then document each name it now reports as missing, or leave it out of the skill brief's `scope.include` (or add its file to `scope.exclude`) and re-run Create Skill.

- **skf-test-skill:** At Forge tier and above, where the recipe runner reads the source, Test Skill's standard barrel no longer shrinks when the skill brief is older than the source. When a `scope.include` glob matches no file in the source tested (a module that became a package in a new major version, say), the coverage surface now keeps each root export defined in a file no include glob covers, unless `scope.exclude` or a `scope-expansion` amendment whose latest action is `skipped` or `demoted-include` matches that file, and the gap ledger records one Medium `brief-scope-stale` gap at the brief that names the globs and each restored export with its file. Such exports were reported as stale documentation before. Now they count in the Export Coverage denominator, so Export Coverage can fall and a run that passed can fail. The recipe runner's output also lists the unmatched include globs in `scope.unmatched_include`. ([#689](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/689); issue [#677](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/677))

  **Migration:** Re-run Test Skill at Forge tier on each skill whose brief was written for an older version of its source. On a `brief-scope-stale` gap, edit `scope.include` in the skill brief by hand so each glob matches the files it meant in this version of the source, or add to `scope.exclude` the files the brief meant to leave out: Update Skill does not rewrite an include glob.

- **skf-test-skill:** At Forge tier and above, where the recipe runner reads the source, a `scope.tier_a_include` glob in the skill brief that matches no file in the source tested (a brief written for an older layout of the source, say) no longer lowers the stratified Export Coverage denominator without a word, and no longer keeps the denominator deflation and inflation guards off. The recipe runner now names such a glob in its `warnings` and lists it in `scope.unmatched_tier_a_include`. Test Skill builds the `tier_a_include` set from the tier A globs that match a file, and when none does it leaves the set out, so the next denominator applies and the deflation and inflation guards run. The stale tier A globs are named in the same Medium `brief-scope-stale` gap a stale `scope.include` glob raises. When every tier A glob of a brief matches no file, Export Coverage is now counted over the `scope.include` set (or checked against it by the deflation guard) instead of a stored count or an empty set, so Export Coverage can fall and a run that passed can fail. (issue [#695](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/695))

  **Migration:** Re-run Test Skill at Forge tier on each skill whose brief was written for an older version of its source. On a `brief-scope-stale` gap that names a `scope.tier_a_include` glob, edit that glob in the skill brief by hand so it matches the files it meant in this version of the source: Update Skill does not rewrite a tier A glob.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's deflation and inflation guards no longer stay off at Quick tier, or when it reads the source remotely by eye with no local clone, just because the skill brief lists a `scope.tier_a_include` glob that lies inside a `scope.exclude` glob (such as `src/gen/**` or `src/gen/extra.ts` beside an exclude of `src/gen/**`, or one file named in both lists). Every file such a glob can match is excluded, so it counts no name there, as it already did at Forge tier. A stored `stats.effective_denominator` far below the re-derived surface then raises a Medium `metadata-drift` gap and can be scored over the `scope.include` set, so Export Coverage can fall and a run that passed can fail. ([#752](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/752); issue [#749](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/749))

  **Migration:** Re-run Create Skill on each skill whose brief lists a `scope.tier_a_include` glob inside a `scope.exclude` glob, then Test Skill. On a `metadata-drift` gap that says no `scope.tier_a_include` glob in the brief counts a public name, remove those globs from `scope.tier_a_include` in the skill brief by hand (or from `scope.exclude`, if their files belong in the authored tier), then re-run Create Skill.

- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's deflation and inflation guards no longer stay off at Quick tier, or in the per-file scan it falls back to when the recipe runner printed no JSON, just because the skill brief lists a `scope.tier_a_include` glob. At Quick tier a tier A glob whose folder or file differs from every `scope.include` glob's before any wildcard (such as `gen/**` beside `src/**`) counts no name, as it already did at Forge tier. The per-file scan now passes `--fallback-scan`, since each of its results names the file that defines its exports, so a tier A list that matches no file, only files `scope.include` leaves out, only files `scope.exclude` drops or only files that define no public name counts no name there too. A stored `stats.effective_denominator` far below the re-derived surface then raises a Medium `metadata-drift` gap and can be scored over the `scope.include` set, so Export Coverage can fall and a run that passed can fail. ([#740](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/740); issue [#733](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/733))
