  **Migration:** Re-run Create Skill on each skill whose brief has a `scope.tier_a_include` list that counts no public name (matching no file, only files outside `scope.include`, only files `scope.exclude` drops, or only files that define no public name), then Test Skill. On a `metadata-drift` gap that says no `scope.tier_a_include` glob in the brief counts a public name, edit or remove those globs in the skill brief by hand, then re-run Create Skill.

### Changed

- **skf-audit-skill:** A headless Audit Skill run now ends on its `SKF_AUDIT_RESULT_JSON` line: the run hands the line to the shared health check, which displays it after everything else, so `claude -p` prints the envelope, with its `drift_score`, `next_workflow` and `upstream_ref`, as the final message instead of the health check's closing `Workflow complete.` line. Interactive runs are unchanged, and a halt still ends on its own line. ([#762](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/762))
- **skf-create-skill:** For a skill whose scope type is `public-api`, Create Skill now writes to the provenance map, documents in SKILL.md and `references/`, and lists in metadata.json's `exports` only the exports on the package's public surface, by the rule Update Skill adds new exports by: a name the recipe runner's `entry_point_diff` lists as public or as an extraction gap at that file, or a submodule the entry point exports by name. Before, every export the runner found became a provenance entry and was documented, internals included, so `public_api_coverage` read far above 1 (6.6 on cognee 1.6.2 with broad include globs, where the rule keeps 43 of 424 names). `skf-extraction-inventory.py init` marks each export `public` in the extraction inventory, `add` marks an export read by eye the same way, `provenance` leaves out each export marked `public: false` and `provenance --add-entries` adds no entry of one, `summary` counts and lists them in its new `not_public`, `set` drops them from `top_exports`, and one inventory warning, shown in the extraction summary, names each export left out with its file, which the evidence report lists in full. The extraction summary's zero-export check now also fires when every export is off the surface. When the runner's output gives no surface the rule can read (no entry-point diff, an incomplete run, or an entry point it could not trace), every export is documented as before, with a warning that says why; a run without the runner, and any other scope type, document every export as before. ([#705](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/705); issue [#699](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/699))
- **skf-create-skill:** Create Skill now writes `metadata.json` through `skf-extraction-inventory.py metadata` instead of typing it field by field. `generation_date` is a real UTC time to the second, `description` is read from the staged `SKILL.md`, `tool_versions.skf` is read from the installed module, and `exports[]` always lists the extraction inventory's exports less those marked `internal: true` or `public: false`, each name once (a docs-only skill lists its documentation items, a reference app none). `tool_versions.ast_grep` and `ast_node_count` come from the ast-grep run: the recipe runner's version and match count, or, when the recipes ran without the runner, the number of exports ast-grep matched and the version `ast-grep --version` gives (`unknown`, with a warning, when there is none); `tool_versions.ast_grep` is null when ast-grep did not run. The run only sends the fields it decides: the version, the language, the source location and the QMD version. ([#765](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/765))
- **skf-create-skill, skf-update-skill:** The script detector no longer takes a Python package's `tools/`, `cli/`, `bin/` or `scripts/` folder (one that holds `__init__.py`) for a folder of scripts. A `.py` module in such a folder is now a script only when it is the package's `__main__.py` or has a shebang or a top-level `if __name__ == "__main__":` block (either comparison order, never a line inside a string), so Create Skill no longer packages a package's modules as scripts and Update Skill no longer reports them as new scripts. Other files in the folder, and every file in a script folder that is not a Python package, are detected as before. ([#692](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/692); issue [#683](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/683))
- **skf-create-skill, skf-update-skill:** Create Skill and Update Skill now take the decision whether to store `stats.effective_denominator` in `metadata.json` from the recipe runner, which writes it beside the count (`counts.effective_denominator_decision`, with `counts.curated_subset`), and, for names counted without the runner's entry-point diff, from the runner's new `--mode denominator`. Only whether the brief's `scope.notes` documents the stratification is still judged. The rules are the ones both workflows applied before, with five differences: a count of 0 is never stored (Test Skill read a stored 0 as deflation), a monorepo's `scope.include` lists a curated subset when it leaves out a whole workspace or a file that defines a public name, a single package's `scope.include` lists one only when it leaves out a file that defines a public name (so a folder subset that holds every public name stores no count, and an update removes the count an earlier run stored), at Quick tier and on a hand count the arms come from the source tree instead of a reading by eye, and a remote source read by eye stores no count. ([#766](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/766))
- **skf-create-skill, skf-update-skill, skf-audit-skill, skf-test-skill, skf-brief-skill, skf-analyze-source:** For a submodule a package exports by name (`from . import sub`, `export * as ns`, a Rust `pub mod`), the recipe runner now lists in its `entry_point_diff.public` item a new `members` key: the names the module passes on, which users call as `pkg.sub.name`, each with the file and line that define it, a nested submodule's members in its place (`members` is null for a module the runner cannot read, such as a JavaScript target outside the repository or a Rust inline module). `counts.exports_public_api` and `counts.effective_denominator` count the members in place of the submodule, each name and file once, and a member no recipe found is an extraction gap, or outside scope when its file is. A member the module re-exports from another package has no file, is no gap when a recipe found its name, is marked public by its name, and, unlike the same form in an entry point, adds no `entry_points.unresolved` item, so the public surface still applies. For a `public-api` skill, Create Skill and Update Skill now mark the members public, so the provenance map, SKILL.md and `exports[]` document them, and no longer mark public an export named like the submodule in its folder. Test Skill's surface, Brief Skill's headless `public-api` include and tier-A candidates, and Analyze Source's `api_surface` read the members too. On cognee 1.6.2 with the oms-cognee brief, the 4 submodules give way to 43 members (`visualization_server`, the 8 `cognee.tools` functions, `Task`, `run_pipeline` and `export_dataset` among them), and `exports_public_api` moves from 64 to 102. A `public-api` skill made before this change keeps its map, so its `public_api_coverage` falls until an update documents the members (the gaps Test Skill reports, through a gap-driven Update Skill): oms-cognee 1.6.2 from 0.875 to about 0.55. ([#716](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/716); issue [#703](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/703))
- **skf-drop-skill:** A headless Drop Skill run, a `--dry-run` included, now ends on its `SKF_DROP_SKILL_RESULT_JSON` line: a finished drop hands the line to the shared health check, which displays it after everything else, and a dry run deletes its run folder before it displays the line, so `claude -p` prints the envelope as the final message instead of the health check's closing `Workflow complete.` line. Interactive runs are unchanged, and a halt still ends on its own line. ([#762](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/762))
- **skf-test-skill:** The Coverage Analysis section of a Test Skill report is now rendered by `reconcile-coverage.py render` from the run's coverage, surface and signature files instead of being written by hand. On an enumerated (barrel) denominator the Export Coverage table lists every export the denominator counts, every stale name and every name whose signature mismatches, with a fixed Status (`FAIL` for a signature mismatch, `WARN` for a missing or stale export, `PASS` otherwise) and the file and line the source surface records as its Source Location. **Files Analyzed** counts the distinct files on the source surface. A scalar or stack denominator, which counts exports without naming them, shows one line in place of the table, and so does a docs-only run, which has no source surface. The Coverage Summary and Category Scores come from the same files, and the summary also lists the names the brief scoped out, a nested Python entry point's names and the names the stale-scope guard restored. ([#764](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/764))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill now records a documented name outside the coverage surface that the source still declares as a documented extra: an Info `observation` gap titled `Documented extra: {name}` at the line that declares it, which Update Skill's `--from-test-report` leaves alone. Such a name used to be a Medium `stale-documentation` gap that Update Skill routed and could delete. Only a run of a Python or TS/JS source finds one, at the Forge, Forge+ or Deep tier, with `analysis_confidence` `full`, `workspaceDrift` not `overridden`, a provenance map and a coverage surface that a complete extraction built: `classify-stale` in `skf-verify-provenance-completeness.py` now adds a `defined_at` to each name it does not find fabricated, the line of a Python or TS/JS file that declares the name at column 0 (an import, a re-export, a `require(...)` or `import(...)` binding and an indented local never count, and a module or package named after the name declares it). It reads the files the name's provenance entries cite, then the package those entries lie in, leaving out tests, vendored copies, installed and built output, `docs`, `examples` and `benchmarks`, and lists every file there that declares the name in a new `declared_in`. Exactly one file must declare it, or, when several do, Test Skill takes the one that the skill's own `[AST:]` or `[SRC:]` citations name on a line that names it. A fabricated signature stays a Critical gap, and a name the source no longer declares, one that several files declare when the skill cites none or more than one of them, a dotted name, a name the brief scopes out (`excluded.outsideScope`) and every stale name of any other run stay Medium `stale-documentation` gaps. A name the skill documents from a Python sub-package that the standard barrel leaves out (`excluded.nestedEntries`) is a documented extra too while the source still declares it, and signature scoring still compares its documented signature. ([#690](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/690); issue [#678](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/678))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill no longer counts a Python sub-package inside another package's folder as a barrel of its own. When a folder with no `__init__.py` sits between them (FastAPI `routers/__init__.py` files, say), the inner `__init__.py` was read as a second package root, so its names were reported as missing exports. Its names now stay out of the standard barrel (the `all` and `root` sets) and are listed in `excluded.nestedEntries`, while a `scope.include` or `scope.tier_a_include` denominator still counts them. Only a package that exports a name holds another, so a stray empty `__init__.py` at the source root changes nothing, and a brief whose `scope.include` or `scope.tier_a_include` lists the inner `__init__.py` keeps it a barrel. ([#689](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/689); issue [#677](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/677))
- **skf-update-skill:** For a skill whose scope type is `public-api`, Update Skill now adds to the provenance map, documents in SKILL.md and lists in metadata.json's `exports` only the new exports on the package's public surface: a name the recipe runner's `entry_point_diff` lists as public or as an extraction gap at that file, or a submodule the entry point exports by name. Before, every export of an added file and every new export of a changed file became a provenance entry and was documented, internals included, so a skill with broad include globs could document hundreds of internal names against a few dozen public ones. `skf-build-change-manifest.py records` marks each export `public` in `reextract-records.json` and prints the count it marks off the surface, and `apply` lists each name it leaves out in its new `not_public` summary key and in `not-public.json` in the run folder, with one warning for them all. When the runner gives no surface it can read (Quick tier, a runner failure or an incomplete run), the update adds every export as before, with a warning that says so. The scope type is the one metadata.json records, else the skill brief's `scope.type`. An entry the map already holds is still updated, an export the update removes from one file and finds in another is kept, and any other scope type, a repair from a test report and a degraded run add every export as before. ([#693](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/693); issue [#685](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/685))

### Fixed

- **skf-analyze-source, skf-audit-skill, skf-brief-skill, skf-create-skill, skf-quick-skill, skf-test-skill, skf-update-skill:** A `skill-brief.yaml` that SKF 1.x wrote is read again. SKF 1.x closed every brief with a trailing `---`, which YAML reads as a second, empty document, so every script that reads a brief refused it as not valid YAML: Create Skill's brief check halted with `brief-malformed`, and the recipe runner (`skf-extract-public-api.py`) and the scope helpers stopped on it. These scripts now skip a document that holds no value; more than one document that holds a value is refused. ([#688](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/688); issue [#679](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/679))
- **skf-analyze-source, skf-audit-skill, skf-brief-skill, skf-create-skill, skf-test-skill, skf-update-skill:** The recipe runner (`skf-extract-public-api.py --mode full`) now names every error after its flags parse in one stderr line: a skill brief or a recipe file that is not valid YAML printed the parser's message over several lines, so the line a halt or a warning quotes held only its start. A flag error is argparse's, which prints its usage first; callers quote the line that holds `error:`. ([#700](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/700); issue [#694](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/694))
- **skf-audit-skill:** Audit Skill no longer reports a baseline export the recipe runner leaves out as a removed CRITICAL export while the source still declares it. The runner skips underscore names such as `__version__` and module entries, and nothing sent them to be read by eye, so they read as removed. `skf-extraction-snapshot.py build` now adds to `extraction_gaps` each provenance map entry the snapshot lacks whose file, extracted or read by eye, still declares the name (a Python or TS/JS declaration at column 0 or an alias that renames it, and for a `module` or `package` entry the module or package so named), at that line and with the map's `export_type` when it has one, and lists in `warnings` the entries in other languages, which it cannot check. The re-index step reads each gap by eye once, records it with the map's kind while the declaration still has that kind (so a real kind change is still reported), and warns about a gap it cannot place instead of reading it again. ([#691](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/691); issue [#682](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/682))
- **skf-audit-skill:** Audit Skill no longer reports the internal exports of a `public-api` skill as added drift. When the skill's `metadata.json`, or else its brief, gives the scope type `public-api`, the re-index passes `--scope-type public-api` to the recipe runner and to the snapshot build, which marks each export as on or off the public surface by the rule Create Skill and Update Skill keep the provenance map to. The structural diff then lists each new export off the surface under `not_public`, with its count in the summary and an "Off the public surface" note in the drift report, instead of under the added exports, where each one graded HIGH. These exports are not drift: they count in neither Total Drift Items, the drift score nor the diff's exit code, and a map entry off the surface is still compared, never reported removed. When the public surface cannot be read, as at Quick tier or after an incomplete runner run, every new export is reported as added as before, and the result envelope warns `public_surface_not_applied`. ([#714](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/714); issue [#702](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/702))
- **skf-audit-skill:** Audit Skill's Script/Asset Drift check no longer reports every untracked file under a `scripts/`, `bin/`, `tools/` or `cli/` folder as a new MEDIUM file. `skf-compare-file-hashes.py compare` now takes the skill brief (`--brief`) and lists as `added` only the files the brief's scope takes, by the scope test Update Skill uses: the modules of a Python package named like a script folder, files the provenance map's `entries[]` cite, and scripts or assets whose `scripts_intent` or `assets_intent` is `none` are never new files. Without a brief it can read, the audit still compares the tracked files but looks for no new one, and says why in the saved comparison's `added_not_checked`, in a note under the Script/Asset Drift table and in a `new_files_not_checked` warning of the result envelope. ([#701](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/701); issue [#696](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/696))
- **skf-audit-skill:** A Deep-tier audit now runs its semantic diff for a skill that has no QMD extraction collection registered, whatever tier the skill was compiled at. The step used to skip with a `Skipped` status; it now reads what the skill documents from its `SKILL.md` and `references/*.md`, as it already did for a registered collection that is empty, checks those claims against the current source and labels its findings `T1-low-fallback`, and the Semantic Drift header says the claims came from the skill's files and why. ([#691](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/691); issue [#681](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/681))
- **skf-audit-skill, skf-create-skill, skf-update-skill:** Audit Skill's Script/Asset Drift check now finds new files with the script and asset detector Create Skill and Update Skill use, so `skf-compare-file-hashes.py compare --brief` lists the same new scripts and assets as Update Skill. Before, it looked only under the script and asset folders and `docs/authoritative/`. Now a shebang script or a `package.json` `bin` entry point in any folder, and a `*.schema.json`, `openapi.*`, `*.example` or similar asset anywhere, is a new file when the brief takes it. A shebang script under an asset folder such as `examples/` counts as a script for `scripts_intent` and `assets_intent`, and files under `scripts/[MANUAL]/` or `assets/[MANUAL]/` are never new files. If `skf-detect-scripts-assets.py` beside it cannot be loaded or is out of date, the audit still compares the tracked files and says why in `added_not_checked`. The detector itself no longer fails on a root `package.json` that is valid JSON but not an object, such as `[]`, so Create Skill and Update Skill read the tree's scripts and assets as usual there. ([#719](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/719); issue [#711](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/711))
- **skf-audit-skill, skf-update-skill:** Audit Skill no longer grades a kind the provenance map recorded by eye as a changed signature. The structural diff compared `type` as written, so a by-eye `async_function` or `decorator` against the recipe runner's `function`, or an `enum` against its `class`, became a CRITICAL `changed/signature` finding. The diff now takes the two as one kind when the runner's signature shows that form (an `async def`, `async function`, `async fn` or `async unsafe fn`, or a `const`, `let` or `var` bound to an `async` arrow or function; a Python `def` for a decorator; a Python class with a stdlib `Enum`, `IntEnum`, `StrEnum`, `ReprEnum`, `Flag` or `IntFlag` base) and counts each such export under a new `export-type` entry of `applied_transforms`, which the drift report's Applied Transforms row shows. Such an export whose line also moved is a LOW `changed/location` finding. Update Skill's diff of the files that changed compares the same way, so it no longer lists such an export among its modified exports. ([#691](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/691); issue [#680](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/680))
- **skf-brief-skill:** In a forge-auto pipeline, Brief Skill's `[auto]` run now hands the docs it detects to the doc URL merge script, which gives each one its label from its content type and its `source` from how it was found, so a detected doc never carries a stray `README Link` label or a `source` the brief schema refuses. The brief writer now refuses a `doc_urls` source outside the schema's values before it writes anything, and the `[auto]` run then drops the doc enrichment with a warning and writes the upstream brief as it was. Before, one such source made it overwrite Analyze Source's valid brief with an invalid one and halt, and a resumed run halted on that brief too. Analyze Source uses the same writer but writes only `language-registry` sources, so it sees no change. ([#762](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/762))
- **skf-brief-skill, skf-analyze-source, skf-quick-skill:** Brief Skill now looks up the version of a source whose manifest states none, as its version rules document, and a script does the lookups: a Python package with a dynamic version reads `__version__` from its package or `_version.py`, or `version=` from `setup.py`; a Rust crate that inherits its workspace version reads the workspace root's `Cargo.toml`; and any source, a Go module included, then takes its release tag. On GitHub that is the newest tag whose name is a release version, so a repository that tags releases without publishing a GitHub Release counts too, or the pinned tag itself; for a local source it is the tag `git describe` names. Before, the brief recorded `1.0.0` with no warning, and Create Skill could then build the skill from an old `v1.0.0` tag. A JavaScript or TypeScript source on GitHub whose default branch carries a pre-release version (`-alpha`, `-beta`, `-rc`, `-next` or `-canary`) now takes the newest release instead, as the version rules say. A brief whose version still falls back to `1.0.0` carries a `no source version detected` warning, in the `SKF_BRIEF_RESULT_JSON` envelope of a headless Brief Skill run that derives the brief and in Analyze Source's brief preview. The public API extractor Quick Skill also uses now reports a Cargo `version.workspace = true` as no version, with a warning, instead of passing the table on. ([#762](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/762))
- **skf-create-skill:** In a component library, an export Create Skill reads by eye (in a file the recipes could not parse, or one a failed ast-grep call left unread) is now sorted by its shape, as at the Quick tier: a Props interface read so is taken as a Props contract, so its fields are documented in SKILL.md and recorded in the provenance map, and its component is linked to it, and a component read so is recorded as a component. Before, only the exports a recipe found were sorted, so such a Props interface was left with no fields, its component was recorded as having no Props interface, and metadata.json's `components_documented` left that component out. ([#751](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/751); issue [#748](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/748))
- **skf-create-skill:** Create Skill now decides whether to store `stats.effective_denominator` in `metadata.json` by the globs its coverage count used (`counts.effective_denominator_basis`; for a count it made by hand, `scope.tier_a_include` only when that list counts a public name, else `scope.include`), not by `scope.tier_a_include` whenever the brief has one. A count over every file, or over a `scope.include` that covers the full workspace (in a single-package repo, the whole package, which v3.0.0 could store; not when a `specific-modules` brief on a repository that is not a monorepo has a `scope.exclude` glob that leaves out part of the package that defines public names), is left out, and Test Skill then measures coverage as for a skill with no stored count. A skill that already stores such a count keeps it until Create Skill or Update Skill runs again. ([#726](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/726); issue [#724](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/724))
- **skf-create-skill:** When an ast-grep call of the recipe runner (`skf-extract-public-api.py`) times out, or is killed or crashes after it printed some of its matches, Create Skill now runs the runner once more and, when the run is still `incomplete`, reads by eye every file a failed call lists in `unread` and adds what it finds as T1-low. Update Skill and Audit Skill already run the runner again and read those files by eye, and Test Skill already reads them by eye. A file such a call left unread or cut in part used to ship with exports missing from the provenance map, behind a warning that named only how many files the call held and the first of them; the warning now says those files are read by eye. One failed call over a large batch of files can send all of them to the by-eye read. ([#739](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/739); issue [#731](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/731))
- **skf-create-skill:** When the recipe runner's run is still incomplete after Create Skill runs it a second time (an ast-grep call failed or ran out of time both times), Create Skill now leaves `stats.effective_denominator` out of `metadata.json`. A file the failed call left unread can hide a public name or the file that defines it, so the count could be 0 or partial: with a `scope.tier_a_include` list that counts no public name it stayed 0, and Test Skill then reported a Medium `metadata-drift` gap against a count the brief never set. Test Skill now measures such a skill over the set it re-derives, as for a skill with no stored count, so a `specific-modules` skill whose `scope.tier_a_include` list does count names is measured over `scope.include` until Create Skill or Update Skill runs again with ast-grep finishing. ([#760](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/760); issue [#744](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/744))
- **skf-create-skill:** A long or `--batch` Create Skill run whose context was compacted before its report step now still writes each finished brief's result contract (the `create-skill-result-*.json` file and its `create-skill-result-latest.json` copy), prints its `SKF_CREATE_SKILL_RESULT_JSON` line and runs the `on_complete` hook a team configured. The report step now finds the result emitter and the `on_complete` value on its own, so a complete install no longer skips the contract as if the emitter were missing, no longer sets `validation_status` to `schema-unavailable` in the skill's `metadata.json`, and no longer skips a configured hook as if it were empty. ([#763](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/763))
- **skf-create-skill:** Create Skill now keeps its script and asset detection to the brief's scope by the brief's own glob rules, the ones the recipe runner and Update Skill use: `**` also matches at the top of the source, `*` never crosses a folder, and `scope.exclude` is honoured. The detector used to match `scope.include` with Python's `fnmatch`, so Create Skill could package a file the brief excludes or miss one it takes. `skf-detect-scripts-assets.py detect` takes the brief with `--brief` in place of `--scope-include`, and exits 1 with one `error:` line for a brief it cannot find or read. ([#701](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/701); issue [#697](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/697))
- **skf-create-skill:** For the shapes Create Skill stores `stats.effective_denominator` for (a monorepo, a `specific-modules` scope or a multi-subpath `exports` map, with the tiers described in `scope.notes`), a `scope.tier_a_include` list wider than a curated `scope.include`, for example `src/**` over `src/utils/**` and `src/index.ts`, no longer keeps that field out of `metadata.json`. With this release's breaking change to tier A counting, such a list counts the curated subset, and Create Skill now judges the files the count read instead of the tier A list alone. Test Skill measures the same number with or without the stored count: without it, it takes the `tier_a_include` or `scope.include` set instead. ([#736](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/736); issue [#730](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/730))
- **skf-create-skill:** When Create Skill counts the public API by hand (at Quick tier, by source reading, for a brief whose language no recipe reads, when the recipe runner cannot run, or for files no recipe reads beside files it does read), it now counts a name the package's entry points pass on from two files or in two languages once in `stats.effective_denominator`, as the recipe runner does and as Test Skill counts it, while `stats.exports_public_api` still counts it once per file. A hand count could store one more for each extra file, so a curated skill that documented every name scored Export Coverage below 100 on the stored count (66.67 for two names counted as three). A skill keeps its old count until Create Skill or Update Skill runs again. ([#757](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/757); issue [#746](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/746))
- **skf-create-skill:** An export Create Skill reads by eye and adds to its extraction inventory with `./` in front of its file, or with `\` separators, now merges with the recipe runner's record of the same export instead of being documented twice. Such a copy added a second, T1-low entry for the same name, file and line to the provenance map and raised `stats.exports_documented` and `public_api_coverage` with it, and when an ast-grep call fails every file it held is read by eye, so one such read could double nearly every export of the skill. A call that sends an export with an absolute path is now refused and adds none of its exports until the path is sent relative to the source root, with a message that names each such export. Such an export used to be added as a second entry or, on a `public-api` skill, marked off the public surface, so an export only that read found was left out of the provenance map. ([#753](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/753); issue [#747](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/747))
- **skf-create-skill, skf-audit-skill:** When the recipe runner (`skf-extract-public-api.py`) leaves no JSON and prints an `error:` line, on an input error such as a recipe file it cannot read or a source root it cannot find, or on a failure it did not foresee, Create Skill and Audit Skill still extract without it and now warn `Recipe runner failed` with that line instead of falling back without a word. Create Skill shows the warning at its extraction gate and in the evidence report; Audit Skill shows it with its AST fallback warnings and records `recipe_runner_failed` in its result envelope. A shell timeout, which prints no such line, still falls back without the warning. ([#700](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/700); issue [#694](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/694))
- **skf-create-skill, skf-quick-skill, skf-create-stack-skill, skf-rename-skill:** On Linux and macOS, two overlapping `active` link flips (`skf-atomic-write.py flip-link`) of one skill no longer both hold `active.skf-lock`. A flip refused by a held lock used to remove the holder's lock file, and a flip that had locked a file already removed went on anyway, so a later flip could lock a new file while an earlier one still held the old one. One of them then failed with a Python traceback (exit 1) where exit 2 is documented, or exited 0 naming a version `active` did not point at, which Create Skill and Quick Skill reported as active. Now only the flip holding the lock removes the file, a flip whose locked file is no longer at the path opens the path again, and the flip that finds the lock taken exits 2 with the `another process holds flip lock` message, as documented. ([#721](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/721); issue [#713](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/713))
- **skf-create-skill, skf-test-skill:** Create Skill now stores `stats.effective_denominator` with each public name counted once, as the recipe runner's help and Create Skill's instructions say. A name the package's entry points pass on from two files (a module or namespace member named like another public name, such as `foo` re-exported from `./a` beside `export * as ns from './b'` when `./b` defines its own `foo`) or in two languages used to count once per file, while Test Skill counts each name once, so a skill that documented every name scored Export Coverage below 100 on the stored count (66.67 for two names counted as three). Export Coverage on a stored count can rise. It can also fall: Test Skill checks that each name `metadata.json` declares appears in the docs, and when that check finds a name missing, the count of names it found becomes the numerator. That check now also runs when the provenance map holds no impl-block method and its distinct names equal the stored count, as it already runs when `stats.exports_documented` does. So a skill that documents every name, one of them passed on from two files, gets the check instead of `skipped`, and a High `numerator-inflation` gap can now appear where the check reported `skipped`. The gap now asks only that the absent names be documented, no longer that `stats.exports_documented` be set by hand. `stats.exports_public_api` is unchanged. A skill keeps its old count, one high for each extra key, until Create Skill or Update Skill runs again. ([#738](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/738); issue [#734](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/734))
- **skf-create-skill, skf-update-skill:** For a `specific-modules` brief on a repository that is not a monorepo, with the tiers described in `scope.notes`, Create Skill now judges whether its coverage count covers a curated subset by the files `scope.include` matches less those `scope.exclude` drops, the surface Test Skill carves from both lists, and Update Skill judges the same way on each update. So a whole-package `scope.include` such as `src/**` with `scope.exclude: [src/core/**]` keeps `stats.effective_denominator` in `metadata.json` when `scope.exclude` leaves out part of the package that defines public names, as a curated `scope.include` does. Excludes that drop only files defining no public name, such as tests or build output, still leave a whole-package count out. Test Skill's Export Coverage does not change: it re-derives the same number, and the stored count is what its deflation check compares. ([#759](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/759); issue [#743](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/743))
- **skf-create-skill, skf-update-skill:** Create Skill no longer takes a release-time placeholder such as `0.0.0-development` or `0.0.0-semantically-released` from a semantic-release package as the source version. It now reads the source's version with the public API extractor, which reports a placeholder, and a version that is not a string, as no version, so a skill built from such a package's release tag keeps the brief's version instead of being written under a `0.0.0-development` folder with that version in `metadata.json`. Update Skill reads the source's version the same way, so it no longer reads that placeholder as the source version either. ([#762](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/762))
- **skf-create-skill, skf-update-skill:** At Quick tier, in a run the recipe runner cannot serve, and for files no recipe reads, Create Skill no longer matches the brief's globs, counts the entry points or tells internal exports and extraction gaps apart by eye. It takes the files in scope, those in a language no recipe reads included, the entry points and the arms from `skf-extract-public-api.py` (full mode now ends its JSON with `files_in_scope_list` and `files_without_recipes_list`, and `--mode denominator` gives them with no recipe run, also from a remote repository's file list), and has `exports_public_api`, `exports_internal`, `effective_denominator` and the entry-point diff (`entry_point_diff`) made by script from the public names it finds, read with quick mode for a local Python, JavaScript or TypeScript source and by eye otherwise. Update Skill counts the same way where it counted by hand, at Quick tier included. When that script cannot run, or fails again after a second try, both workflows halt instead of counting by hand. The counts stored in `metadata.json`, which Test Skill reads as its coverage denominator, can change on those runs. ([#766](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/766))
- **skf-create-skill, skf-update-skill, skf-audit-skill, skf-test-skill:** The recipe runner (`skf-extract-public-api.py --mode full`) now puts a Python package's explicit binding of a name before its submodule: when `x/__init__.py` binds `y` with an import (`from .y import y`) or a `def` or `class`, `from .x import y` is the name it binds, at the file and line that define it, and it is the submodule `x/y.py` only when `x/__init__.py` binds no `y` or binds the submodule itself (`from . import y`, `from pkg.x import y`). A `y` that `x/__init__.py` binds only through a star import (`from .impl import *`) is still read as the submodule `x/y.py`. Before, the runner took any `x/y.py` beside that `__init__.py` for the name, so it listed such a function as a submodule (`via: namespace`) with no line, counted the other names of its file as reachable instead of internal, and never reported it as an extraction gap or as outside scope. On cognee 1.6.2, 22 of the 26 names the runner listed as submodules are functions or classes (`cognee.visualize` is now `visualize` at `visualize.py:193`, and `cognee.delete` the function `delete/__init__.py` defines), so `counts.exports_internal` moves from 311 to 355, `entry_point_diff.extraction_gaps` now names `session` and `entry_point_diff.outside_scope` names `SearchType`. ([#716](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/716); issue [#703](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/703))
- **skf-drop-skill, skf-update-skill:** When Drop Skill purged the version a skill's `active` link named and the helper that points the link at the remaining version could not run or could not move the link (it exits 1 when `skf-atomic-write.py` is missing from the install, or when the skill folder refuses the change), Drop Skill named no rule for that exit, so the drop could report `success` with no warning and leave `active` pointing at the deleted folder. It now records `active_link_dangling` with a fix that points the link at the remaining version and the helper's error, so the report and the result record name the link to repair. In the same case Update Skill now stops with `halted-for-write-failure` (`error.phase` `write:active-symlink`) and shows the helper's error. On Linux and macOS its next check used to stop the run, saying the flip did not apply and suggesting an `ln -sfn` to the version its rollback removes. ([#737](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/737); issue [#732](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/732))
- **skf-setup, skf-brief-skill, skf-create-skill:** On Windows, a write to `forge-tier.yaml` through `skf-forge-tier-rw.py` no longer fails with `atomic write failed ... [WinError 5] Access is denied` when another process has the file open at the moment the helper renames its new copy over it, such as a call about to take the registry lock checking that the file exists, a `read` call, or a virus scanner. Windows refuses that rename while any process holds the file open, so the write now retries it for up to 5 seconds before it fails. Before, the write exited 2: Setup halted at `step 2:write-tools`, or skipped its registry cleanup; Brief Skill and Create Skill went on without the `qmd_collections` entry of a collection they had just made, or the `ccc_index_registry` entry of Create Skill's index; and when Create Skill's rollback could not remove an entry, the registry kept one for a collection QMD no longer has. ([#717](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/717); issue [#715](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/715))
- **skf-setup, skf-forger:** Ferris and Setup now start in a project whose `forge-tier.yaml` an SKF 1.x setup wrote. That file holds `tier_detected_at` and `ccc_index.last_indexed` as unquoted timestamps, and the preflight both run first crashed on them: Ferris stopped at activation with a Python `TypeError`, and Setup halted with `on-activation:config-malformed`, so the setup run that would rewrite the file could not start. The preflight now prints such values as ISO 8601 strings. ([#675](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/675); issue [#674](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/674))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill no longer picks the coverage denominator's clause by hand. `load-coverage-inputs.py surface` picks it from the brief, the extraction and `metadata.json` and writes it to `surface.json` as `denominator` (`clause`, `branch`, `surfaceSet`, `ladderStep`, `absentSet`, `rebuild` and the entry points' state it read, `barrel`). It takes the curated-subset verdict and the monorepo layout from the extraction (`counts.curated_subset`, the rule Create Skill stores `stats.effective_denominator` by, and `arms.monorepo`), and where no file gives them, what only the workflow can tell as four new flags: `--monorepo`, `--pattern-reference-intent`, `--curated-subset` and `--barrel` (an entry point read by eye, empty or missing). An extraction the per-file scan replaces that found no entry point now reads as one with none, as a complete run does, so the clause no longer depends on whether ast-grep is installed. A `specific-modules` or multi-entry skill that stores `stats.effective_denominator` is now measured against that stored count, under the deflation guard, as the source access protocol and Create Skill already said, where the coverage step had counted its name set instead, so its Export Coverage can change; a stored 0 is no denominator. A provenance map whose raw count equals `stats.effective_denominator` is no longer folded, and `canonical` now reports `skipped` and `residual`. ([#766](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/766))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill no longer records a removed API as a documented extra. `classify-stale` in `skf-verify-provenance-completeness.py` found such a name in two places: in an example, demo, sample, script, playground, end-to-end test, benchmark or migration folder of the package (`example/old.ts`, `pkg/migrations/0001.py`), and in a module named after the name, such as `pkg/client.py` for a removed `client()`, whatever the module holds. Its walk now leaves out the `e2e` and `__fixtures__` folders wherever they lie, and the `example`, `demo`, `demos`, `sample`, `samples`, `scripts`, `playground`, `bench`, `benchmark` and `migrations` folders right below the package it reads and below each package root inside it (deeper in a package such a folder is still read, and so is one that holds a file the provenance map cites; a file the map cites in any of these folders is still read). With its new `--inventory` flag, which Test Skill now passes, a module so named no longer declares a name the skill documents as a `function`, `hook`, `class`, `interface`, `enum` or `type`, unless a provenance map entry of the name is a `module` or `package` one or the module is a TypeScript or JavaScript file that is itself the export (`export default`, `module.exports =`). Such a name is now a Medium `stale-documentation` gap, which Update Skill routes, instead of an Info `Documented extra` observation. ([#707](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/707); issue [#698](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/698))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill's workspace drift check now finds the skill's source folder under `source_root` in `metadata.json`, the key Create Skill and Quick Skill write. It looked for a `source_path` key that no SKF workflow writes, so it could skip the check and record `workspaceDrift` as `not-checked`. A source checked out at another commit was then tested instead of stopping with `workspace-drift`, and with `--allow-workspace-drift` a pass was published as `PASS`, with exit code 0 and `next_workflow` `export-skill`, instead of `pass-with-drift`, with exit code 4 and `update-skill`. A skill whose `metadata.json` records no `source_root`, such as a docs-only or stack skill, now logs `workspace_drift_check: skipped (metadata.json records no source_root)`, and the message Test Skill shows when it finds no exports in the source names `source_root` too. ([#764](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/764))
- **skf-test-skill:** When Test Skill falls back to its per-file scan because the recipe runner cannot be used, the subagent for each file now leaves out a name that file only passes on from another module of the source being tested (`export { x } from './x'`, `export * from`, an `__init__.py` import, a Rust `pub use`), which that module's own result counts, and still lists a name it passes on from another package (`export { z } from 'zod'`), which no other result counts. A barrel, or an entry file that defines a name of its own, used to list every name it passes on as its own, so a name defined in a file the skill brief scopes out (outside `scope.include`, or dropped by `scope.exclude`, as Update Skill's gap-driven rescope does) counted in the `scope.include` set: Export Coverage could score it as missing, and the deflation or inflation guard could raise a Medium `metadata-drift` or `denominator-inflation` gap over a correct stored `stats.effective_denominator`. The per-file scan now counts the `scope.include` set the recipe runner counts. ([#758](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/758); issue [#750](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/750))
- **skf-test-skill:** When the recipe runner (`skf-extract-public-api.py`) exits 2 in the coverage check, on an input error such as a skill brief it cannot read or on a failure it did not foresee, Test Skill now halts with `helper-failed` and the runner's error line instead of running the slow per-file fallback scan as if the runner could not be used. The fallback scan still runs when the runner's JSON says it cannot do the work (no ast-grep, no files in scope or no recipe for them), or when it prints no JSON on another exit. ([#688](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/688); issue [#676](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/676))
- **skf-test-skill:** Test Skill now checks the verdict fields it wrote into the test report (`testResult`, `score`, `threshold`, `thresholdFallback` and `originalThreshold`) against the scoring output before it publishes the report. A field that disagrees with what the scoring settled, such as `testResult` `pass` when a cap turned the run into a `FAIL`, a bare `pass` on a run whose workspace drift was overridden (`--allow-workspace-drift` with the workspace off the pinned commit), or the target threshold on a run the threshold fallback accepted at the 80% floor, now halts with `helper-failed` (phase `report:result-contract`) and leaves the report under its in-progress name and the previous result files in place, instead of publishing that verdict with exit code 0 and `next_workflow` `export-skill`. A correct run is unchanged. ([#764](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/764))
- **skf-test-skill, skf-create-skill, skf-quick-skill, skf-create-stack-skill, skf-rename-skill:** On Windows, a Test Skill gap-ledger append (`gap-ledger.py append`) that finds the ledger's `.skf-lock` file still being removed by the append before it now waits and goes through instead of failing with `WRITE_FAILED`, and gives `LEDGER_LOCKED`, naming the refusal, only when the file stays refused for the whole 30-second lock wait. In the same case the `active` link flip (`skf-atomic-write.py flip-link`) now waits up to about a second and goes through, where it used to fail with a Python traceback that stopped Create Skill and Quick Skill, rolled Rename Skill back and left Create Stack Skill a `flip-link-failed` warning. A lock file still refused after that wait ends the flip with exit 2 and the `another process holds flip lock` message, naming the refusal, which Create Skill's `active-link-blocked` halt now shows instead of saying the `active` path is not a symlink. ([#708](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/708); issue [#706](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/706))
- **skf-update-skill:** Update Skill no longer halts its script and asset check (`detect-changes:category-d`) on a provenance map that has no `file_entries` field, such as one written before the field existed or one whose skill has no script, asset or promoted document. `skf-hash-content.py compare` and `skf-new-file-diff.py` now read a missing or null `file_entries` as no tracked file instead of refusing the map; a `file_entries` that is not an array is still an error. ([#692](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/692); issue [#684](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/684))
- **skf-update-skill:** Update Skill now moves a provenance map entry to the new file when an export moves from one changed file to another, whether or not it also changed, as `skf-build-change-manifest.py apply` documents. The change manifest now names the file a moved export left (`old_file`), and `apply` finds the entry there; before, it looked for the entry in the new file, found none and left it at its old file and line, adding a second entry for an export that also changed. ([#693](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/693); issue [#686](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/686))
- **skf-update-skill:** Update Skill now gives an export that moved within its file the labels of this run's recipe runner match along with its new line (`extraction_method: ast-grep`, confidence T1, the match's `ast_node_type`, and `signature_source` T1 when the match read each part of the signature the entry records), as a re-extracted export takes them. Before, `apply` moved only the line, so an entry an older SKF version had labelled `source-read` with T1 failed the stats coherence check and was downgraded to T1-low, which rewrote its `[AST:]` citations to `[SRC:]`. An export read by eye still moves its line only, and a move never changes an entry's type, parameters or return type. ([#693](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/693); issue [#686](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/686))
- **skf-update-skill:** Update Skill no longer reports every script and asset of the source repository as a new file. Its new-file check walked the whole repository with no scope, so an update of a skill scoped to one package listed hundreds of `NEW_FILE` rows from folders the skill brief leaves out. `skf-new-file-diff.py` now takes `--brief` and keeps only the paths the brief's scope takes, by the same in-scope test as the file-level changes (an empty `scope.include` included), drops a kind whose `scripts_intent` or `assets_intent` is `none`, and sets aside code the map's `entries[]` cite; it lists what it set aside in `tracked_code`, `out_of_scope` and `intent_none`, never in `stats`. A skill with no brief skips the check with a `new-files-not-checked` warning instead of walking the repository, and a failed check now halts with `detect-changes:category-d`. ([#692](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/692); issue [#683](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/683))
- **skf-update-skill:** Update Skill dropped `stats.effective_denominator` from `metadata.json` on its first run after Create Skill stored it: it gave the stats helper no `effective_denominator` and wrote back the stats the helper returned, so Test Skill then measured a curated subset without that count and without its check for a lowered count. Update Skill now passes the recipe runner's count under the rules Create Skill uses, so the stored count follows the source version and the brief each update reads (a rescope that excludes files lowers it). It removes the count when those rules do not hold, and replaces one set by hand or by a repair from a test report. When `--allow-workspace-drift` lets it run on a source checkout that is not at the skill's pinned commit, it keeps the recorded count. An update whose recipe runner run is still incomplete after its second run also removes the stored count, so Test Skill measures coverage as for a skill with no stored count until an Update Skill or Create Skill run where ast-grep finishes stores it again. ([#755](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/755); issue [#741](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/741))
- **skf-update-skill:** Update Skill now writes `metadata.json` through `skf-build-change-manifest.py metadata` instead of editing it by hand. `skf-build-change-manifest.py apply` lists in `metadata-lists.json`, in the run folder, the `exports[]` the update leaves (the names the skill listed, less each name whose provenance entry the update removed or renamed, plus each name it mapped, never one off a `public-api` skill's public surface; a reference app's stays empty) and one `scripts[]` or `assets[]` row per script or asset the provenance map tracks (a row the skill had stays as it was, and a new file's purpose is read from the file). The `metadata` call writes those lists, the version, the generation date, the source commit and the stats, removes `last_update` and `update_type`, keeps every other field, and refuses stats whose script or asset counts differ from the lists, so `exports[]` names the exports the provenance map holds and `stats.scripts_count` and `stats.assets_count` match the rows. ([#765](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/765))
- **skf-update-skill:** When the recipe runner (`skf-extract-public-api.py`) exits 2 while Update Skill reads the exports of the changed files or of the files a test report names, on an input error such as a file list it cannot read, on a failure it did not foresee, or when `uv` fails to start it, the update now halts with `blocked` and the runner's error line (phase `detect-changes:category-b` or `re-extract:records`) instead of reading every file by eye as if the runner could not be used. When it exits 2 while counting the public API for `metadata.json`, the counts are still made by hand, and the run now warns `public-api-counted-by-hand` with the error line. No ast-grep, no JSON on another exit, a missing runner and Quick tier keep the by-eye read. ([#700](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/700); issue [#694](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/694))
- **skf-update-skill:** When the check Update Skill runs right after it points the skill's `active` link at the new version found a real folder in the link's place (a copy, as `ln -s` makes in Git Bash without symlink rights) or found the skill folder gone, its helper exited 1 with no result and Update Skill named no rule for that exit, so a run could go on to report `success` with `active` no longer a link, which the next update and Create Skill, Quick Skill and Rename Skill then refuse to replace. It now stops with `halted-for-write-failure` (`error.phase` `write:verify-active-symlink`), shows the helper's error and undoes what the update wrote, as the same check already did when the link named another version. The folder at `active` is left for you to replace with a link. ([#754](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/754); issue [#742](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/742))
- **skf-update-skill:** When Update Skill repairs the gaps a test report names and the recipe runner (`skf-extract-public-api.py`) is still `incomplete` on its second run over the files those gaps name, for example after it stopped at its time limit, the update now reads by eye each of those files the runner left unread or found no export in, and tells you which files it read by eye. A blocking gap (Critical, High, or one with no recognized severity) whose export sits in such a file now goes on to its judgments and resolves as `re-extracted` (T1-low, `source-read`) instead of halting with `halted-for-remediation-path` and a report blaming the remediation text, and a Medium, Low or Info missing export or type now gets its source line instead of ending `unknown`. An exit 2 from the runner still halts with `blocked`. ([#718](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/718); issue [#710](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/710))
- **skf-update-skill, skf-audit-skill:** Update Skill no longer reports a module, an alias that renames, a dunder such as `__version__` or another underscore name as a `DELETED_EXPORT` while the changed file still declares it. The recipe runner never reports these names, and the export check read again only the names the runner itself flagged. A new `skf-build-change-manifest.py baseline-gaps` call now lists, at every tier, each provenance map entry of a modified file that the runner did not report and whose file still declares it, into `baseline-gaps.json`, and the export check reads each one by eye with the map's kind while the declaration keeps it, recording each name and file once. An entry no rule can check (a file neither Python nor TS/JS, a test file, a path through a symlink, or a dotted module name) is listed in `unchecked`, and the export check records it only when its file still declares it; Audit Skill's extraction snapshot now names such entries in its warning instead of dropping them in silence. An entry its file no longer declares is still reported deleted. The selection is the one Audit Skill's extraction snapshot uses, now shared from `skf-verify-provenance-completeness.py`, and a verifier that cannot be loaded halts the run with `detect-changes:category-b`. ([#692](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/692); issue [#687](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/687))
- **skf-update-skill, skf-audit-skill, skf-test-skill:** When an ast-grep call of the recipe runner (`skf-extract-public-api.py`) is killed or crashes after it printed some of its matches, the runner still keeps those matches and now also lists every file of that call in the `unread` of its `errors[]` item, as it already did when the time limit stopped a call. A file whose matches were cut in part used to keep some of its exports and lose the rest with no warning. Now, after a second run that is still `incomplete`, Update Skill (when it re-extracts changed files and when it repairs the gaps a test report names) and Audit Skill's extraction snapshot read that file by eye, and the snapshot no longer reports `complete: true` for such a run. Test Skill's coverage check now reads by eye every file a failed call lists in `unread`, not only the first. One failed call over a large batch of files can send all of them to the by-eye read. ([#727](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/727); issue [#722](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/722))
- **skf-update-skill, skf-drop-skill, skf-create-skill, skf-quick-skill, skf-create-stack-skill:** On Linux and macOS, Update Skill and Drop Skill now take `active.skf-lock` when they point a skill's `active` link at a version, the lock Create Skill, Quick Skill and Create Stack Skill take for that flip, so these flips of the link run one at a time. When another run's flip of the link landed during Update Skill's own flip, Update Skill could stop with `halted-for-write-failure` saying the flip did not apply though it had, roll back the new version, and suggest an `ln -sfn` that pointed `active` at the removed folder; when two runs moved one skill's link at nearly the same moment, Drop Skill could record `active_link_dangling` with a fix that undid the other run's flip; and two such runs could fail with exit 1 and a `No such file or directory` error. Now a run waits while another flip holds the lock. When it stays held for 5 seconds, Update Skill stops with `halted-for-concurrent-run` (`error.phase` `write:active-symlink`, `error.reason` starting `busy:`) and undoes what it wrote, and Drop Skill records `active_link_dangling` with a fix to run once the other run has finished. A Create Skill, Quick Skill or Create Stack Skill flip that meets one of these flips now gets the documented `another process holds flip lock` refusal, where it used to go through. ([#728](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/728); issue [#723](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/723))
- **skf-update-skill, skf-drop-skill, skf-create-skill, skf-quick-skill, skf-create-stack-skill, skf-rename-skill:** On native Windows (Git Bash or PowerShell), the helper that points a skill's `active` link at a version (`skf-update-active-symlink.py`) exited 1 on every run with "use WSL2 to run update-skill", so Update Skill could not make the version it wrote live (a run could end with `metadata.json` on the new version and `active` on the old one), and a Drop Skill purge that had to move the link left it on the deleted version. The helper now makes a directory junction when Windows refuses a symlink, as Create Skill already does, reads a junction back as the version it names, and takes the link's lock (`active.skf-lock`) there as on Linux and macOS. Every fix Drop Skill gives that points the link at a version, the recovery its refusal to drop the active version names included, and the fix Update Skill shows when the link names another version now run `skf-atomic-write.py flip-link` instead of `ln -sfn`, which Git Bash without symlink rights turns into a copy of the folder. Create Skill, Quick Skill and Create Stack Skill, which flip the link through the same code, now also replace a junction whose version folder was deleted, and on Windows remove the old link first when Windows refuses to rename the new one over it. ([#756](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/756); issue [#735](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/735))

### Documentation

- Troubleshooting has a new entry for when Setup says the CCC index failed, for example on an index an older ccc wrote (`Failed to deserialize pickle payload`): run `ccc reset`, then `ccc daemon restart`, then `@Ferris SF` again. Without the restart, the next index can fail with `environment already open in this program`. ([#675](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/675))

## [3.0.0](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/compare/v2.2.0...v3.0.0) (2026-10-04)

SKF 3.0.0 is safe to use in a skills folder shared with other skills: it moves, updates, renames and deletes only the skills it generated. Update Skill now reads a remote source at the exact commit the skill tracks and writes each update into a new version folder, and every provenance entry is labeled by the tool that read it and checked against the line it cites. Read Breaking changes before you upgrade: SKF now requires Python 3.11, the Setup result envelope no longer lists the `write_failure` status, `npm install bmad-module-skill-forge@rc` and `@alpha` stop resolving once 3.0.0 is published, and some runs now stop with a message that says what to run. Those are runs on a skill still in the old flat layout (Create Skill, Quick Skill, Stack Skill, and Update Skill with `--detect-only` or `--dry-run`), Drop Skill and Rename Skill on a skill folder that also holds files SKF did not write, Drop Skill on a never-exported skill without `--mode purge`, Update Skill of a remote skill when it cannot read the commit it tracks, Update Skill with `--allow-workspace-drift` when a gap needs a line or a signature from the pinned commit (as every new or changed export does) or a recount of the public API there (as a removed export does), a second Update Skill of a skill whose run lock another update holds (`halted-for-concurrent-run`), and Update Skill with `--from-test-report`, `--dry-run` included, when a gap rated Critical or High, or with no severity it recognizes, names no source line and no file to read for an export it has no provenance for.

### Breaking changes

- **all workflows, skf-forger:** Every workflow now runs BMad core's customization resolver through `uv run`, with `--project-root`, instead of a bare `python3`. Customization overrides in `_bmad/custom/<skill>.toml` and `_bmad/custom/<skill>.user.toml` therefore start to apply where the resolver used to fail silently (a bare `python3` missing or older than 3.11), so a setting such as `forbid_purge_in_headless` now takes effect. When the resolver still cannot run, for example in a project without the BMAD Method installer's customization script, the run prints `[activation/warn] customization_resolver_unavailable: <reason>`, uses the bundled `customize.toml` alone, and reports `customization_resolver_unavailable: <reason>` among the run's warnings: in the result envelope and result file, or in Campaign's decision log. Ferris (`skf-forger`) runs the same resolver with `--key agent`, so `_bmad/custom/skf-forger.toml` and `_bmad/custom/skf-forger.user.toml` can give him `activation_steps_prepend`, `persistent_facts` and `activation_steps_append` (his roster values stay as shipped); when it cannot run he opens his greeting with the same warning line. ([#650](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/650), [#652](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/652); issue [#595](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/595))

  **Migration:** Review `_bmad/custom/<skill>.toml` and `_bmad/custom/<skill>.user.toml`, since their settings now apply, and install `uv` if runs warn `customization_resolver_unavailable`.

- **packaging:** The npm dist-tags `rc` and `alpha`, which still point at `1.0.0-rc.3` and `0.10.1-alpha.0`, are removed once 3.0.0 is published, so `npm install bmad-module-skill-forge@rc`, `npm install bmad-module-skill-forge@alpha` and `npx bmad-module-skill-forge@rc` stop resolving instead of installing a build two majors older than `latest`. From now on `latest` is the only permanent dist-tag: `alpha`, `beta` and `rc` exist only while a prerelease line is open, and the stable release that closes the line removes its tag. ([#636](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/636); issue [#568](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/568))

  **Migration:** Install `bmad-module-skill-forge@latest`, or an exact version such as `bmad-module-skill-forge@3.0.0`, instead of `bmad-module-skill-forge@rc` or `bmad-module-skill-forge@alpha`, and change any script or pipeline that names `@rc` or `@alpha` the same way.

- **requirements:** SKF now requires Python 3.11 or newer; Python 3.10 is no longer supported. What SKF needs did not change: in v2.2.0 the helpers that read package manifests (used by Quick Skill, Brief Skill, Analyze Source and Stack Skill) already needed 3.11, and Quick Skill runs one of them with a bare `python3`, so its export extractor already crashed on 3.10. The documented minimum now says so. ([#522](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/522))

  **Migration:** Run `python3 --version`. If it prints 3.10 or older, install Python 3.11 or newer and make it the `python3` on your `PATH`; nothing else needs to change.

- **skf-analyze-source:** Analyze Source writes every `skill-brief.yaml`, on the `[auto]` path and in the interactive step alike, through `skf-write-skill-brief.py`, and outside the documentation-URL branch checks it with `skf-validate-brief-schema.py`, the check Brief Skill runs when it reads a brief, before any brief reaches the forge data folder. A brief either one rejects now stops the run with exit `4` (`write-failed`) and an error envelope, where `AN[auto]` used to write it, report success and leave `BS[auto]` to halt one stage later (a whole-language caveat holding an apostrophe was enough). `brief_paths` therefore lists only briefs that passed these checks. Exit `4` with `write-failed` at the end of a run now means that the shared emitter refused the result payload twice: a result file that cannot be written leaves `result_path` null and a `result_file_write_failed` warning, and the run finishes with exit `0`. The auto path also reads the target's whole file list from one file, so shape detection sees every grammar file and compiler folder. ([#634](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/634); issue [#592](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/592))

  **Migration:** Re-run `@Ferris AN[auto] <target>` (or the `forge-auto` pipeline) on a target whose run stops with `write-failed`: the envelope's `error.reason` names the brief field the writer or the schema rejected. A pipeline that treated exit `4` as a missing result file now checks the envelope's `warnings` for `result_file_write_failed` before it reads `analyze-source-result-latest.json`.

- **skf-analyze-source:** Analyze Source drops two customization settings that could not do what they offered. `brief_schema_path` pointed the analysis at a copy of the brief contract, but the brief writer and the schema gate check every brief against the bundled schema, so a house-style copy either changed nothing or produced briefs the gate rejects. `unit_detection_heuristics_path` pointed it at a copy of the unit detection rules, but the size limits, the generated-file rules and the unit names come from the shared helpers, so a copy changed only some judgments. Both settings are now ignored when an override sets them. `analysis_report_template_path` now ships its real default, `templates/analysis-report-template.md`, and the comments of `customize.toml` say when the activation hooks run and that the `on_complete` command receives `--result-path` with the latest result file and never fails the run. ([#637](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/637); issue [#596](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/596))

  **Migration:** Remove `brief_schema_path` and `unit_detection_heuristics_path` from `_bmad/custom/skf-analyze-source.toml` and `_bmad/custom/skf-analyze-source.user.toml`. Rules your copy of the heuristics added for the analysis to keep in mind go into `persistent_facts` instead.

- **skf-analyze-source:** When no unit is confirmed (every unit rejected, or every boundary dropped in a headless run), Analyze Source now ends like any other run: it writes `analyze-source-result-<YYYYMMDD-HHmmss>.json`, replaces `analyze-source-result-latest.json` with that record, which lists no brief, prints `SKF_ANALYZE_RESULT_JSON` with `brief_paths: []` and `unit_counts.confirmed: 0` (which the forger's AN circuit breaker reads as no skillable unit), and runs the `on_complete` hook and the health check. Before, it stopped with no envelope, ran no hook and left an earlier run's `analyze-source-result-latest.json` in place. The `on_complete` hook now also runs when an `[auto]` run ends with a coexistence `redirect` or `skipped` status, which before wrote its record without calling the hook. Every envelope now comes from the shared emitter and follows the new schema `skf-analyze-result-envelope.v1.json`: each one gains `result_path` (the per-run result file, null on a halt), a halt's gains `error` with the step it stopped at (`phase`) and its message, a redirect or a skip carries `report_path`, `brief_paths` and `unit_counts` too, and `headless_decisions` lists the `[auto]` merge-or-split decision and the choice of the documented language when a run made them. Every HARD HALT of a headless run prints its envelope, from activation on. ([#634](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/634); issues [#585](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/585), [#593](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/593))

  **Migration:** A hook or pipeline that reads `analyze-source-result-latest.json` (the `on_complete` hook's `--result-path`) as a run that wrote briefs checks the record first: its `status` (`redirect` and `skipped` write no brief) and whether its `outputs` hold an entry of type `brief`.

- **skf-audit-skill:** Audit Skill no longer offers degraded mode, which had no baseline to compare against and could not finish: the `degraded` input, the degraded-mode gate and its `init.degraded-mode` entry in the envelope's `headless_decisions` are gone, and so is the report's Mode row (`confidence_mode`). A skill with no provenance map, such as a Quick Skill, now stops with the new halt reason `no-baseline` (exit `3`) in every mode, and names Test Skill and Create Skill; before, a headless run stopped there as `user-cancelled` (exit `6`). A docs-only skill is now audited by its documents: the audit compares each document's hash with the one recorded at compile time, grades each changed document HIGH (the new `--doc-drift` input of `skf-severity-classify.py`), so the score is `SIGNIFICANT` and `next_workflow` is `update-skill`, or `CLEAN` when nothing changed. A docs-only skill that records no document hash stops with `no-baseline`, and one none of whose documents could be compared (offline, for example) stops with the halt reason `source-unreadable` (exit `3`); when only some could not be compared, the envelope's `warnings` carry `doc_fetch_failed` or `doc_not_hashed` with their counts. A stack built from code is now audited, from the project root it was scanned from and library by library, where it stopped at `source-dir-missing`. Audit Skill now checks `uv` and its shared helpers before the first question and stops with `helper-missing` when one is missing, so it no longer falls back to diffs, grades or hashes made by hand; a skill-inventory helper that is missing or crashes is now `helper-missing` instead of `skill-not-found`, and a missing script and asset hash helper skips that check with a note instead of halting. The `severity_rules_path` setting is removed: `skf-severity-classify.py` grades every finding by its own rule table, so the setting changed grades only in the by-hand fallback, which is gone. `drift_report_template_path` now names its default, `assets/drift-report-template.md`, and the comments of `customize.toml` say to keep a template copy outside the skill folder, named from `{project-root}`, what the copy must keep, and that `on_complete` is a shell command run from the project root once a finished audit's result file is written. ([#640](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/pull/640); issues [#594](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/594), [#596](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/596), [#599](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/599), [#600](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/600), [#589](https://github.com/armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge/issues/589))

  **Migration:** Drop `degraded` from audit-skill invocations and `severity_rules_path` from `_bmad/custom/skf-audit-skill.toml` and `skf-audit-skill.user.toml`. For a skill without a provenance map, run Test Skill (`@Ferris TS`) to check it against its source, or re-create it with Create Skill (`@Ferris CS`) to make it auditable. A pipeline that matched `user-cancelled` or an `init.degraded-mode` decision for such a skill matches `no-baseline` instead. Run audits where `uv` is installed.

- **skf-audit-skill, skf-forger:** Audit Skill no longer checks out SKF's shared clone to audit a newer upstream ref: the `[C]` choice of its upstream-drift gate reads that ref into a private tree of the run's own and leaves the clone as it was, with no lock held across steps. The dirty-worktree sub-gate goes with the checkout, and so do its inputs `dirty_worktree_choice` and `force`. Since nothing on disk changes any more, `[C]` is now the headless default when `upstream_drift_choice` is unset (it was `[S]`, stay on the baseline). The upstream check is one script call that compares commits, so a clone made with `--depth 1 --branch <tag>` no longer reads as moved on every audit. The result contract and the `SKF_AUDIT_RESULT_JSON` envelope gain `upstream_moved` and `upstream_ref`, and `next_workflow` is now `update-skill` also when upstream moved, whatever the drift score, so a `maintain` pipeline reaches update-skill after an upstream release: the forger's gate no longer skips US after a `CLEAN` audit whose `next_workflow` is `update-skill`, and it passes `upstream_ref` to update-skill as `--target-ref`.
